- पंच जनाः (*paṃca janāḥ*)—the five peoples, the gods, Gandharvas and the rest
- सुशर्माणः (*suśarmāṇaḥ*)—may they be endowed with excellent happiness

May all the gods cause our dwelling-places to grow. May Indra, Earth, Pūṣan, Bhaga, Aditi and the five peoples, the gods, Gandharvas and the rest, be for our good endowed with excellent happiness, endowed with excellent food, and excellent guides. May they be excellent protectors and excellent givers of shelter.

May they, Indra, Earth, Pushan, Bhaga, Aditi, and the five orders of beings, give increase to our habitations: may they be to us granters of happiness, bestowers of food, guides to good, our gracious defenders end preservers.

With this verse the seer speaks of himself in the third person. O gods, may this Bhāradvāja, born in the line of Bharadvāja, the hotṛ, the praiser, this seer, quickly reach the heavenly abode, the dwelling-place in heaven; and he asks for your good thought, that is, your gracious mind. To that end, together with other sacrificers seated and performing a long sacrificial session,
with fellow sacrificers who are fit for the sacrifice, the sacrificer, performing the rite, this seer, desiring wealth for himself, has praised the host of the gods; that is, he adores them.
- भारद्वाजः (*bhāradvājaḥ*)—born in the line of Bharadvāja
- होता (*hotā*)—this seer, who praises and calls the gods
- आसनेभिः (*āsanebhiḥ*)—who sit at the sacrificial altar
- मियेधैः (*miyedhaiḥ*)—who are fit for the sacrificial rite; with other sacrificers
- यजमानः (*yajamānaḥ*)—this seer, the performer of the sacrifice

O gods, may this seer, born in the line of Bharadvāja, who praises and calls the gods, quickly obtain the abode in the heavenly world. He asks for your excellent gracious mind. This seer, the performer of the sacrifice, together with other sacrificers who sit at the sacrificial altar and are fit for the sacrificial rite, desiring wealth, offers reverence to the host of the gods.

May the presenter of the oblation, Bharadwaja, quickly obtain, gods, a celestial abode, as he solicits your good-will : the institutor of the ceremony, together with pious associates, desirous of riches, glorifies the assembly of the gods.

On the fourth day of the Daśarātra, in the Prauga-śastra, the verse beginning अप त्यं वृजिनं (*apa tyaṃ vṛjinaṃ*) is used; it is a Vaiśvadeva triplet. It is also laid down in the sūtra, which states that the Prauga recitation is in the Anuṣṭubh metre (Ā. 7-11). O Agni, drive that well-known crooked enemy, the sinner, one of evil intent who wishes harm, a thief and destroyer, away to the farthest distance; cast him away (the root is asu, to throw). O Agni, protector of the good, make for us an easy, pleasant going. Here the Vaiśvadeva character arises from the praise of Agni, whose nature includes all the gods.
- सत्पते (*satpate*)—O Agni, protector of the good
- सुगं (*sugaṃ*)—for us an excellent means of happiness
O Agni, drive the well-known enemy, of sinful nature, the cause of suffering, a thief, away to the farthest region. O Agni, protector of the good, produce for us an excellent means of happiness.
Drive away, Agni, to a distance the wicked, felonious, malignant enemy : grant us felicity, protector of the virtuous.

On the fourth day of the sacrifice called Daśarātra, at the time of reciting the Prauga-śastra mantras, the three Ṛks beginning with अप त्यं वृजिनं (*apa tyaṃ vṛjinaṃ*) are to be recited as the Vaiśvadeva triplet. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra अप त्यं वृजिनं रिपुमंबितमे नदीतम इन्यानुष्टभं प्रउगं (*apa tyaṃ vṛjinaṃ ripumaṃbitame nadītama inyānuṣṭabhaṃ praugaṃ*) (Ā. 7-11).

O Soma, these pressing stones of ours, used for pressing, long for your friendship; the word kam is a filler, and hi has the sense of "because". Since this is so, destroy the Paṇi, the merchant who gives nothing, the Atrin, the devourer, a Rākṣasa or the like. That Paṇi is a wolf, bent on seizing; he is always one who robs us. Therefore destroy him: this is the meaning.
- ग्रावाणः (*grāvāṇaḥ*)—these stones that press out the juice
- पणिं (*paṇiṃ*)—him who is not given to giving
- वृकः (*vṛkaḥ*)—is like a wolf that devours everything

O god Soma, these our stones that press out the juice keep longing to win friendship with you. Therefore destroy completely the Paṇi, who is not given to giving and who devours everything. He is like a cruel wolf.
These our grinding stones are anxious, Soma, for your friendship : destroy the voracious Pani, for verily he is a wolf.

O gods of good gifts, you indeed are powerful and prosperous. Indrajyeṣṭhāḥ means those of whom Indra is the eldest, the chief. Abhidyavaḥ means those whose splendour has come near. You, on the way, together with us, being our guardians and protectors, grant us happiness. The syllable ā is used in the sense of joining; and grant happiness as well.
- यूयं हि ष्ठ (*yūyaṃ hi ṣṭha*)—you alone are lords of all
- इंद्रजेषाः (*iṃdrajeṣāḥ*)—those who have Indra himself as leader
- अभिद्यवः (*abhidyavaḥ*)—those who have extended radiance; you, such as these
O gods of excellent giving, you alone are lords of all. You who have Indra himself as chief and who have extended radiance, being with us on our ways as our protectors, produce happiness for us.
You are manifest and illustrious, gods. with Indra for your chief : be with us, protectors, on the road, and grant us happiness.

This verse beginning अपि पंथां (*api paṃthāṃ*) is to be muttered by the sacrificer on coming back from a journey; this is laid down in the sūtra, which says that on returning he mutters it with a kindling stick in his hand (Ā. 2-5). We have come upon the path; that is, we have reached it. What kind of path? One that is to be travelled in well-being, and free from sin. Going by which path a man avoids all the hostile creatures, that is, drives them off and wards them away, and gains wealth: such a path is meant.
- येन (*yena*)—on which path, as he travels (a man)
- अनेहसं (*anehasaṃ*)—that which is free from sin
- अपि अगन्महि (*api aganmahi*)—we have followed and come
We have followed and come by the path on which a man, as he travels, escapes all the hostile creatures: a path that brings welfare and is free from sin.
We have travelled along the road prosperously traversed and free from evil, and by which (a man) avoids adversaries and acquires wealth.

After going on a journey to some other place and returning, this Ṛk beginning आपि पंथां (*āpi paṃthāṃ*) is to be muttered. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra आपि पंथामगन्महीति प्रत्येत्य समित्पाणिः (*āpi paṃthāmaganmahīti pratyetya samitpāṇiḥ*) (Ā. 2-5).

A certain seer named Atiyāja sacrificed to the gods with the thought: "May I be superior to this Ṛjiśvan." Ṛjiśvan rejects that sacrifice with this verse. I do not approve of that sacrifice of the seer Atiyāja as being joined with the heavenly world, that is, with the host of gods dwelling there; I give it no assent. Nor do I approve of it as joined with the host of gods of the earth. Nor do I think it equal to the sacrifice performed by me, nor equal to these other works done by me. The gods have been brought under my power and do not accept his sacrifice, and through ignorance he cannot even sacrifice properly: this is the sense. Further, may the mountains, the well-existing ones, sent by Indra, destroy that seer (the root ubbi has the sense of injuring). So too may the sacrificer of that Atiyāja, a seer endowed with the thought "I sacrifice to the gods even more than Ṛjiśvan", be utterly diminished. ⟨NOTE:128⟩
notes: ಋಷಿಸ್ತದೀಯಂ ಯಜನಂ ನಿರಾಚಷ್ಟಾದ್ಯಯಾ: machine-read Sanskrit damaged

en: - तत् (*tat*)—the sacrificial act done by the seer Atiyāja
- दिवा (*divā*)—as fit to be joined with the gods of the heavenly world
- न अनु मन्ये (*na anu manye*)—I do not approve
- पृथिव्या (*pṛthivyā*)—as fit to approach the gods of the earth
- यज्ञेन (*yajñena*)—as equal to the sacrifice that I perform
- अभिः शमीभिः (*abhiḥ śamībhiḥ*)—as equal to the other works done by me
- सुभ्वः (*subhvaḥ*)—those who are in a lofty place
- पर्वतासः (*parvatāsaḥ*)—the gods who are with Indra
- अतियाजस्य (*atiyājasya*)—who is the representative of Atiyāja
- नि हीयतां (*ni hīyatāṃ*)—let him be utterly destroyed

I do not approve of the sacrificial act done by the seer Atiyāja as fit to be joined with the gods of the heavenly world. Nor do I approve of it as fit to approach the gods of the earth. It is certainly not equal to the sacrifice I perform. I cannot accept it as equal to the other works done by me. May the gods who are in a lofty place and are with Indra injure that seer Atiyāja. May the performer of the sacrifice, the representative of Atiyāja, meet with utter destruction.

I do not regard it as worthy (of the gods) of heaven, or (of those) of earth, as (fit to be compared) with the sacrifice (I offer), or with these (our) sacred rites: let, then, the mighty mountains overwhelm him; let the employer of Atiyaja be ever degraded.

In former times a seer named Atiyāja wished to become greater than the seer Ṛjiśva, the seer of this sūkta, and for that purpose tried to propitiate the gods with sacrifices and the like. Learning of it, Ṛjiśva became angry with that Atiyāja and reviles him and his sacrificial work. That very matter is stated in this Ṛk.

Addressing the Maruts, Sāyaṇa explains: the man who looks down on us, that is, who thinks himself superior even to us; and who would wish to disparage the hymn (or praise) that we perform — for that man let the energies (tapūṃṣi) be afflicting, harmful. As for the enemy who hates the hymn (brahmadviṣ), may Dyaus, the sun, scorch him, burn him on every side.
- अति मन्यते (*ati manyate*)—despises, and thinks himself higher than we are
- ब्रह्मद्विषं (*brahmadviṣaṃ*)—who hates our hymns and the like
- अभि शोचतु (*abhi śocatu*)—let him cause to decay

O Maruts, may your energies prove destructive to the lot of the man who despises us and thinks himself greater than we are, and who slanders the hymn that is performed by us. May Āditya cause that enemy, who hates our hymns and the like, to decay.
Maruts, may the energies of that man be enfeebld : may heaven consume that impious adversary who thinks himself superior to us, and who pretends to depreciate the worhip that we offer.

Sāyaṇa takes किमंग (*kimaṃga*) as two particles expressing what is well known. O Soma, those who know of old call you the protector (gopā) of the brahman, that is, of the mantra, or of the rite, or of the Brahmin class; and likewise they call you, and no other, the guardian of us against those who denounce us. Or else: अंग (*aṃga*) is a word of addressing; "O Soma, for what reason do they call you protector of the brahman, and for what reason do they call you our protector against calumny?"

"For what reason do you look on us, who are reviled by others? All call you alone the guardian of the brahman and the protector against enemies; therefore indifference on your part while we are reviled by others is unbecoming. So hurl and send forth your scorching weapon (hetiṃ) against him who hates the Brahmin or the brahman."
- ब्रह्मणः (*brahmaṇaḥ*)—of the mantra or of the rite
- किं आहुः (*kiṃ āhuḥ*)—why have they said
- अभिशस्तिपां (*abhiśastipāṃ*)—as one who protects from enemies
- ब्रह्मद्विषे (*brahmadviṣe*)—upon one who hates the praiser or the Brahmin

O divine Soma, why have the praisers called you the protector of the mantras and of the rite? Why have they praised you as the one who protects us from enemies? O Soma, why do you look on us indifferently while we are reviled by enemies? O Soma, hurl your burning weapon upon the enemy who hates the praiser or the Brahmin.

Why have they called you, Soma, the protector of pious prayer ? why (have they called you) our defender against calumny ? why do you behold us subjected to reproach ? cast your destroying weapon upon the adversary of the Brahman.

Let the dawns, as they are born, that is, appear, protect me. Likewise let the rivers, flowing and swelling, protect me; let the firm, unmoving mountains protect me. And let the fathers, the deities of the ancestors, who are present at the devahūti, that is, the sacrifice in which the gods are invoked, protect me.
- देवहूत् (*devahūt*)—who are in the sacrificial place where the gods are worshipped
- मा अवंतु (*mā avaṃtu*)—let them protect me

May the Dawn goddesses, who are born every day, protect me. May the rivers, which grow, protect me. May the firm mountains, and the deities of the ancestors who are in the sacrificial place where the gods are worshipped, protect me.
May the opening dawns preserve me : may the swelling rivers preserve me ; may the firm-set mountains preserve me : may the progenitors (present) at the invocation of the gods preserve me.

O gods, may we at all times be of good mind. The word नु (*nu*) is used in the sense of conjunction: may we also always behold the sun as he rises. Agni, the lord of the riches, the master of excellent wealth, bringing and conveying the gods by our oblation, the one who comes most readily, being thus endowed with these qualities, तथा करत् (*tathā karat*): may he make us such as described.
- सुमनसः (*sumanasaḥ*)—of good mind (that we may be)
- आगमिष्ठः (*āgamiṣṭhaḥ*)—coming graciously in accordance with the invocation
- तथा करत् (*tathā karat*)—may he do as we desire

O gods, may we at all times be of good mind, and may we also behold the sun who rises every day. May Agni, the excellent lord of all riches, bearing satisfaction to all the gods by our oblations and coming graciously in accordance with our invocation, fulfil our desire.

May we at all seasons be possessed of sound minds : may we ever behold the raising sun : such may the affluent lord of riches, (Agni), render us, ever most ready to come (at our invocation), charged with our oblation to the gods.

Let this Indra come nearest, that is, in the closest way, with his protection, as the one who comes most readily. Let Sarasvatī, in the form of a river, swelling with the flowing waters (sindhu), be the one who comes most readily. Let Parjanya, together with the plants, be a bringer of happiness (mayobhū) to us. And let Agni, like a father, be easily praised, that is, worthy of praise with ease, and easily invoked.
- नेदिष्टं (*nediṣṭaṃ*)—as one very near to us
- आगमिष्ठः (*āgamiṣṭhaḥ*)—let him be the one who comes
- सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*)—let the river Sarasvatī also graciously come
- मयोभुः (*mayobhuḥ*)—let him be a giver of happiness
- पितेव (*piteva*)—as a father is worthy of praise to his son
- सुहवः (*suhavaḥ*)—and worthy of an excellent invocation, let him be

May Indra come with his protection as one very near to us, and may Sarasvatī, who grows with the flowing waters, graciously come. May Parjanya be a giver of happiness to us by means of the plants. As a father is worthy of praise to his son, may Agni be worthy of our excellent praise and of our excellent invocation.
May Indra be most prompt to come nigh for our protection, and Saraswati dwelling with (tributary) rivers: may Parjanya, with the plants,
be a giver of happiness; and may Agni, worthily praised and earnestly invoked, (be to us) like a father.

At the Āgrayaṇa, this Ṛk is the anuvākyā for the Vaiśvadeva caru, and it is prescribed in the sūtra: विश्वे देवासः आ गत ये के च ज्मा महिनो अहिमायाः (*viśve devāsaḥ ā gata ye ke ca jmā mahino ahimāyāḥ*) (Ā. 2-9). O all gods, come; and having come, hear this my invocation; and having heard it, sit down on this spread sacred grass, be seated on the spread barhis.
- बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)—upon the seat of darbha grass
- आ नि षीदत (*ā ni ṣīdata*)—sit down
O All-gods, all of you graciously come here and hear our invocation. Sit down upon the seat of darbha grass spread out here.
Come, universal gods, hear this my invocation : sit down upon this sacred grass.

In the caru offering made to the All-gods at the Āgrayaṇa iṣṭi, this Ṛk, विश्वे देवास आ गत (*viśve devāsa ā gata*), is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra, according to the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra—विश्वे (*viśve*)
देवास आ गत ये के च ज्मा महिनो अहिमायाः (*devāsa ā gata ye ke ca jmā mahino ahimāyāḥ*)—this is explained by the sūtra so beginning (Ā. 2-9).
O gods, whatever man serves and attends upon you with an oblation from which ghee drips (sprinkled with ghee), all of you, the All-gods, approach that man; be present with him.
O gods, the sacrificer who adorns and worships all of you with oblations together with flowing ghee, that sacrificer, all of you approach and favour.
Come, gods, to him who honours you with the butter-dripping oblation.
Those who are the sons of the immortal, that is, death-free, Prajāpati, those gods, let them listen to our praises, and let them be gracious, thoroughly gladdening, to us.
- (O gods) अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*)—to Prajāpati, who is free from the nature of death
- सूनवः (*sūnavaḥ*)—are sons (all of you who are so)
O gods, all of you who are sons of Prajāpati, who is free from the nature of death, hear our praises. Be excellent givers of happiness to us.
May the sons of the immortal hear our praises, and be to us the givers of felicity.

The All-gods, augmenters of the ṛta, that is, of the sacrifice, who at the various special times (ṛtu) hear the invocation, that is, the praise, being praised at that and that time of sacrifice — let all of them, such as they are, enjoy and partake of the fitting milk, in the form of curd-milk (āmikṣā). Sāyaṇa adds that it is heard in the Śruti: तप्ते पयसि दध्यानयति सा वैश्वदेव्यामिक्षेति (*tapte payasi dadhyānayati sā vaiśvadevyāmikṣeti*) **GLOSS**
- हवनश्रुतः (*havanaśrutaḥ*)—who hear the praises of the sacrificers
- पयः (*payaḥ*)—the milk in the form of the oblation

May all the All-gods, who make the sacrifice grow and who at the various special times hear the praises of the sacrificer, enjoy the milk, in the form of the oblation, that is fit for their enjoyment.
Universal gods, augmenters of sacrifice, listening to praises (uttered) at due seasons, accept your appropriate milk-offering.
Indra, whose troop (gaṇa), that is, retinue, is the Maruts, together with Tvaṣṭṛ, and Mitra and Aryamā — let them enjoy our hymn and these oblations; let them partake of them.
- मरुद्दणः (*maruddaṇaḥ*)—who is accompanied by the hosts of the Maruts
- इमा हव्या (*imā havyā*)—these oblations offered now
May Indra, who is accompanied by the hosts of the Maruts and is with Tvaṣṭṛ, and Mitra and Aryamā, enjoy our hymn and the oblations now offered.
Indra, with he company of the Maruts, Mitra, with Twashtri and Aryaman, accept our praise and these our oblations.

O Hotṛ, Agni, summoner of the gods: knowing the divine host (daivya jana), the company that is to be worshipped, perform this our sacrifice, which is free from violence (adhvara), vayunaśaḥ, that is, in the order of knowledge, according to the sequence in which the gods stand in the mind; perform the sacrifice.
- होतः (*hotaḥ*)—who call the gods to the sacrifice
- दैव्यं (*daivyaṃ*)—belonging to the company of the gods
- वयुनशः (*vayunaśaḥ*)—according to the worthiness of the respective gods

O Agni, who call the gods to the sacrifice, you who fully know the divine people belonging to the company of the gods, perform the sacrifice in this our sacrifice according to the worthiness of the respective gods.
Agni, invoker of the gods, cognizant (which of) the divine assembly (is to be honoured), offer this our sacrifice according to the proper order.

This Ṛk, विश्वे देवा (*viśve devā*), is the yājyā of the Vaiśvadeva śastra, and the sūtra says: अश्रुत्यै श्वेति शस्त्रा जपेद्विश्वे देवाः शृणुतेमं हवं म इति याज्या (*aśrutyai śveti śastrā japedviśve devāḥ śṛṇutemaṃ havaṃ ma iti yājyā*) (Ā. 5-18). At the Vaiśvadeva animal offering also this same Ṛk is the yājyā, and the sūtra says: विश्वे देवाः शृणुतेमं हवं मे ये के च ज्मा महिनो अहिमायाः (*viśve devāḥ śṛṇutemaṃ havaṃ me ye ke ca jmā mahino ahimāyāḥ*) (Ā. 3-7). O All-gods, hear this my invocation, you who are in the atmosphere, you who are in the nearby earth-world, and you who are in heaven; you who are agnijihvāḥ, those whose tongue (the place of the tongue) is Agni; or else the Agnijihvas are so called because they are nourished by the tongue of Agni; and those who are worthy of worship (yajatrāḥ): all of you, sitting down on this spread barhis, rejoice, satisfy yourselves with Soma.
All of you, those worthy of worship, seat yourselves upon this spread barhis and rejoice; satisfy yourselves with Soma.
- अंतरिक्षॆ स्थ (*aṃtarikṣè stha*)—are in the atmosphere
- उप (*upa*)—are in the nearby earth-world (and also)
- अग्निजिह्वाः (*agnijihvāḥ*)—have Agni himself as the tongue for your Soma-drinking, all such of you
- यजत्राः (*yajatrāḥ*)—all of you who are worthy of sacrifice
- अस्मिन् बर्हिषि (*asmin barhiṣi*)—on this spread darbha seat
- मादयध्वं (*mādayadhvaṃ*)—obtain the satisfaction that consists in drinking Soma

O All-gods, those of you who are in the atmosphere, who are in the nearby region, the earth, who are in the heaven-world, you who have Agni himself as the tongue for your Soma-drinking, all such of you, hear this my invocation. Moreover, all of you who are worthy of sacrifice, seated on this spread darbha seat, obtain the satisfaction that consists in drinking Soma.

Universal gods, hear this my invocation, whether you be in the firmament or in the heaven : you who (receive oblations) by the tongue of Agni, or are to be (otherwise) worshipped : seated on this sacred grass, be exhilarated (by the Soma).

In the Vaiśvadeva śastra mantras, this Ṛk, विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*), is to be recited as the yājyā mantra, as explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, आश्रुत्यै त्वेति शस्त्रा जपेद्विश्वे देवाः शृणुतेमं हवं म इति याज्या (*āśrutyai tveti śastrā japedviśve devāḥ śṛṇutemaṃ havaṃ ma iti yājyā*) (Ā. 5-18). And in the animal offering made to the All-gods, this same Ṛk is to be recited as the yājyā mantra, as explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, विश्वे देवाः शृणुतेमं हवं मे ये के च ज्मा महिनो अहिमायाः (*viśve devāḥ śṛṇutemaṃ havaṃ me ye ke ca jmā mahino ahimāyāḥ*) (Ā. 3-7).

The All-gods, worthy of sacrifice, are to hear my hymn that is to be pondered. Likewise both heaven and earth, and Apāṃ Napāt, the fire of the middle region, are to hear our hymn. Then, addressing the gods directly: "O gods, I shall not utter to you hymns that are to be avoided, that is, I shall not speak them; rather, fitting ones. Therefore we, being closest to you, would rejoice in the happiness given by you."
- मन्म (*manma*)—this hymn, of the nature of meditation
- उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)—heaven and earth, both
- अपां नपात् च (*apāṃ napāt ca*)—and the fire of the atmosphere called Apāṃnapāt (let them hear our praise)
- मा वोचं (*mā vocaṃ*)—I shall not recite

May the All-gods, worthy of sacrifice, all hear this hymn of mine, of the nature of meditation. May heaven and earth, and the fire of the atmosphere called Apāṃnapāt, hear my praise. O gods, I shall not recite to you hymns that deserve contempt. May we, who are very near to you, remain in the greatest happiness and experience joy.

May the adorable, universal deities, and both heaven and Eath, and the graandson of the waters, hear my praise : let me not utter words to be disregarded, but let us (brought) most nigh unto you, rejoice in the happiness (you bestow).

At the Āgrayaṇa, the Ṛk beginning ये के च (*ye ke ca*) is the yājyā of the Vaiśvadeva offering, and the sūtra says: विश्वे देवास आ गत ये के च ज्ञा महिनो अहिमायाः (*viśve devāsa ā gata ye ke ca jñā mahino ahimāyāḥ*) (Ā. 2-9). It is also the yājyā of the Vaiśvadeva puroḍāśa; the sūtra has been cited. Mahinaḥ are the great ones; ahimāyāḥ: māyā is a name for knowledge (prajñā); those whose knowledge is keen (āhantṛ-prajñāḥ). Whatever gods of such a kind were born, appeared, on the earth, (jmā is a name of the earth); whichever were born from heaven, the world of Dyaus; whichever were born in the seat of the waters, together with the atmosphere, all those gods, for us, for the iṣi, that is, the son and the like (that which is desired is the iṣi),
and for him, all, whole, life (āyus), whether food or living, through all nights (kṣapaḥ) and all days (usrāḥ), at all times, without interruption, let them bestow.
- ये के च (*ye ke ca*)—whichever gods
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—who have appeared from the world of heaven
- अपां सधस्थॆ (*apāṃ sadhasthè*)—who have been born in the atmosphere

May all those gods who are possessed of great qualities and attained knowledge, whichever of them have been born on the earth, whichever have appeared from the world of heaven, whichever have been born in the atmosphere, favour our sons and the like with life of every kind, giving long life, through all nights and days.

May those mighty deities, having power to destroy, whether they have been manifested upon earth or in heaven, or in the abode of the waters, bestow upon us and our posterity, abundant sustenance both by night and day.

In the oblation made to the All-gods at the Āgrayaṇa iṣṭi, the Ṛk ये के च ज्मा (*ye ke ca jmā*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra, as explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, विश्वे देवास आ गत ये के च ज्मा महिनो अहिमायाः (*viśve devāsa ā gata ye ke ca jmā mahino ahimāyāḥ*) (Ā. 2-9). In the puroḍāśa oblation made to the All-gods also, this same Ṛk is to be recited as the yājyā mantra. The sūtra has been stated earlier.

O Agni and Parjanya, protect, or attend to, my dhī, my work in the form of the sacrifice. O you who are easily invoked, in this sacrifice protect also our excellent praise. Or else the verb अवतं (*avataṃ*) continues in the sense of hearing: hear. Of you two, the one, Parjanya, generates iḷā, food: for through rain plants and trees are born, and from them food is born. The other, Agni, generates the embryo: the food eaten by a man, cooked by the digestive fire, is transformed into the form of semen, and that itself becomes the embryo in a woman. Therefore, you two, place in us foods endowed with offspring; establish them.
- सुहवा (*suhavā*)—O gods, easy to be invoked with an excellent invocation
- अस्मिन् हवे (*asmin have*)—in this our invocation made for the sacrifice
- नः सुष्टुतिं (*naḥ suṣṭutiṃ*)—protect our excellent praise
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—produces the embryo that is the fruit of the essence of food
- (O Agni and Parjanya) प्रजावतीः (*prajāvatīḥ*)—accompanied by offspring

O gods Agni and Parjanya, protect my sacrificial act. O gods, easy to be invoked with an excellent invocation, protect our excellent praise in this our invocation made for the sacrifice. Parjanya, one of you, produces food. O gods Agni and Parjanya, fill us with food accompanied by offspring.

Agni and Parjanya, prosper my pious acts : (accept), you who are reverently invoked, our praise at this sacrifice : one of you generates food, the other posterity : grant us, therefore, food productive of descedants.

O All-gods, when the barhis, the bundle of darbha grass, is spread on the altar, and the fire is kindled, I serve you with this hymn and with great obeisance. O All-gods, worthy of worship, today in this our sacrifice rejoice with the oblation given by us; be satisfied.
- (O All-gods) बर्हिषि (*barhiṣi*)—the seat of darbha grass
- आ विवासे (*ā vivāse*)—I serve and worship you

O All-gods, when the seat of darbha grass is spread and the fire is kindled, I serve and worship you with a hymn and with obeisance. O All-gods, worthy of sacrifice, today attain joy with the oblations offered in this our sacrifice.

When the sacred grass is strewn ; when the fire is kindled, and when I worship (you) with a hymn, and with profound veneration, then. adorable universal gods, rejoice in the oblation (offered) to-day at this our sacrifice.
O Pathaspati, protector of the path, Pūṣan, for the sake of the work (dhī) and for the gaining of food (vājasāti), we yoke you, as one yokes a chariot in battle: we turn you towards us.
- पथस्पते (*pathaspate*)—who are the protector of the paths
- धिये (*dhiye*)—for the protection of our work
- वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*)—and for the gaining of our food
- रथं न (*rathaṃ na*)—as one takes refuge in a chariot in battle
- आयुज्महि (*āyujmahi*)—we take refuge in, and make you join with us

O divine Pūṣan, protector of all paths, for the protection of our work and for our gaining of food, as a warrior in battle takes refuge in his chariot and makes himself one with it, we take refuge wholly in you and make you one with us.
Pushan, lord of paths, we attach you to us like a chariot, for (the sake of) bringing food, and of (accomplishing our) solemnity.

O Pūṣan, wealth that is beneficial to men, that has been attained; one who is a hero, a sender-away (īrayitṛ), a remover in particular, of poverty; one who has given wealth to others before; or else one whose wealth, his gift, is pure; desirable: such a householder, a man of the household, lead us to; bring us to him.
- वीरं (*vīraṃ*)—who has the power to destroy poverty
- प्रयतदक्षिणं (*prayatadakṣiṇaṃ*)—who has wealth fit to be given
- गृहपतिं (*gṛhapatiṃ*)—to the master of the house

O divine Pūṣan, lead us and bring us together with a master of the house who has the power to destroy poverty, who has wealth fit to be given and who has attractive qualities, that we may obtain wealth beneficial to all men.
Conduct us to a gracious householder, friendly to man, liberal in (bestowing) wealth, the giver of pious donations.

O Aghṛṇa, Pūṣan, whose radiance has come to you: impel to give to us even the man who does not wish to give. Soften the mind, the heart, even of a trader, a usurer, a miser; make it soft for the purpose of giving.
- आघृणे (*āghṛṇe*)—who are possessed of exceedingly great radiance
- अदित्संतं चित् (*aditsaṃtaṃ cit*)—even a miser who has no nature of giving
- दानाय (*dānāya*)—to give and, as a benefactor of the world,
- पणेश्चित् मनः (*paṇeścit manaḥ*)—the mind also of the pani (the miser) who has a hard heart
- वि म्रद (*vi mrada*)—make it soft with compassion

O Pūṣan, possessed of exceedingly great radiance, impel even the miser who has no nature of giving, so that he gives and becomes a benefactor of the world. Make the mind of the pani (the miser), whose heart is hard, soft with compassion.
Resplendent Pushan, instigate the niggard to liberality, soften the heart of the miser.

O Pūṣan, whose strength is raised up and fierce: clear the paths for the winning of food. Make the paths purified, those by which we may go and gain wealth, that is, set such paths apart. Strike down the obstructors, thieves and the like; keep them off. And let our undertakings, the rites performed for the gaining of food, be accomplished and bear fruit.
- उग्र (*ugra*)—O Pūṣan, whose strength is exceedingly great and terrifying to enemies
- वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*)—so that food may come to us easily
- वि चिनुहि (*vi cinuhi*)—make them pure, free of thieves and the like
- मृधः (*mṛdhaḥ*)—the violent thieves and the like
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—the rites performed for the sake of food
- साधंतां (*sādhaṃtāṃ*)—may they attain the desired object

O Pūṣan, whose strength is exceedingly great and terrifying to enemies, so that food may come to us easily, make our paths pure, free of thieves and the like. Defeat and destroy the violent thieves and the like. May the rites performed for our gain of food attain the fulfilment of their desired objects.
Fierce Pushan, select (fit) roads for the passage of provisions : drive away all obstructors, (thieves, or the like), so that our holy rites may be accomplished.

O wise Pūṣan, with the goad, the ārā, pierce the hearts of the panis, the traders and misers, which are hard. The ārā is called a rod with a fine metal point, a prod. Pierce through with it, that is, remove the hardness that lies in the heart. Then make these panis subject to us.
- पणी नां (*paṇī nāṃ*)—of the panis, who have no nature of giving and are misers
- हृदया (*hṛdayā*)—the hardness that lies in the heart
- आरया (*ārayā*)—with the goad of fierce power
- परि तृंधि (*pari tṛṃdhi*)—destroy (make their hearts soft)
- रंधय (*raṃdhaya*)—make them submit and fulfil our prayers

O wise Pūṣan, destroy with the goad of fierce power the hardness in the hearts of the panis, who have no nature of giving and are misers, and make their hearts soft. Afterwards make these panis submit to us and become helpers to us.
Piercc with a goad the hearts of the avaricious, wise Pushan, and so render them complacent towards us.

O Pūṣan, pierce with the goad, the prod, the heart of the pani, the trader. In the heart of that pani, desire for us the dear, favourable wealth; that is, produce in him the wish that it must be given. Then make these men subject to us.
- आरया (*ārayā*)—with your goad of fierce power
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—the wish to do us good
- रंधय (*raṃdhaya*)—subdue them and impel them to help us
O Pūṣan, torment the heart of the pani with your goad of fierce power. In that same heart produce the desire to do us good. Afterwards subdue these same panis and impel them to help us.
Pierce with a goad. Pushan, the heart of the avaricious ; generate generosity in his heart, and so render him complacent towards us.
O wise Pūṣan, scratch the hearts of the panis, the traders, and having scratched them make them scattered, loosened; that is, make them soft. The rest has been explained already.
- आ रिख (*ā rikha*)—rub them as one whets on a whetstone
- किकिरा (*kikirā*)—so that they give up their hardness and become soft

O wise Pūṣan, rub the hard hearts of the panis as one whets on a whetstone. Make them give up their hardness and become soft. Make these same misers submit to our prayer and fulfil our desired objects.
Abrade, wise Pushan the hearts of the avaricious ; relax (their hardness), and so render them complacent towards us.

O Pūṣan, whose radiance has come to you: the goad that you carry in your hand, which impels the Brahman (the prayer or food), the ārā, with it scratch the heart of every miserly person, and make the scattered, loosened ones, that is, make them soft.
- अघृणे (*aghṛṇe*)—O one possessed of exceedingly great radiance
- आ रिख (*ā rikha*)—rub it so that they become soft

O Pūṣan, possessed of exceedingly great radiance, with the very goad that you possess, which impels food, rub the hearts of all the miserly people and make them attain softness, so that they show compassion towards us.
Resplendent Pushan, with that food-propelling goad which you bear, abrade the heart of every miser and render it relaxed.

O Pūṣan, whose radiance has come to you: that goad of yours, which is gopaśā. Those that lie near are the opaśāḥ; she whose opaśāḥ are cows is of that kind. Therefore she is the accomplisher of cattle, the one who brings cattle about. Of that goad of yours we beg the happiness that belongs to it.
- पशुसाधनी (*paśusādhanī*)—that is the guide and protector of cattle
- या अष्टा (*yā aṣṭā*)—which goad there is
O Pūṣan, of marvellous radiance, your goad, which gives shelter to cows and is the guide and protector of cattle: from that same goad we ask the happiness that is to be obtained.
Resplendent Pushan, we ask of you the service of that your weapon, which is the guide of cows, the director of cattle.

And further, O Pūṣan: make our intellect or rite (धियं (*dhiyaṃ*)), which is the bestower of cows, the bestower of horses, the bestower of food, and which is possessed of men (or else: the giver of men), fit for our eating and enjoyment (वीतये (*vītaye*)).
- अश्वसां (*aśvasāṃ*)—that which helps towards the gaining of horses
- नृवत् (*nṛvat*)—that which helps towards sons, grandsons and the like
O Pūṣan, make our rite, which increases cows, helps towards the gaining of horses and nourishes with food, fit for our enjoyment.
Make our pious worship productive of cows, of houses, of food, of

O Pūṣan, nourishing god, bring us together with that knowing man who directly, by the straight way, instructs us in the means of regaining what is lost, and who says, "This is your lost wealth", that is, who shows the lost wealth.
- पूषन् (*pūṣan*)—O Pūṣan, nourisher of the world
- अंजसा (*aṃjasā*)—walking in the excellent straight path
- अनुशासति (*anuśāsati*)—who teaches us too that same straight path
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—this deed is to be performed
- विदुषा (*viduṣā*)—with such a man of discerning knowledge

O Pūṣan, nourisher of the world, unite us with that wise man who, walking in the excellent straight path, teaches us too that same straight path, and who, saying "In this very manner such a deed is to be performed", makes known the discernment of what is to be done and what is not to be done.
Bring us, Pushan, into communication with a wise man who may
rightly direct us, who may even say, this is so.
Favoured by Pūṣan, may we meet that man who points out the houses in which our lost cattle stand, shows them to us face to face, and who says, "These cattle of yours stand just so."
- गृहान् (*gṛhān*)—the houses in which our cattle are hidden
- एव (*eva*)—stand thus, having been carried off
- ब्रवत् (*bravat*)—says; with such a man of discerning knowledge
- पूष्णा (*pūṣṇā*)—we who are favoured by the god Pūṣan

May we, favoured by the god Pūṣan, come together with that man of discerning knowledge who shows us the houses in which our cattle are hidden, and who tells us, "Your cattle stand thus, having been carried off."
May we, by the favour of Pushan, come in communication with (the
man) who may direct us to the houses (where our goods are sacreted), and
may say, verily these are they.

The discus, the weapon, of Pūṣan the nourisher is not destroyed; and the sheath of this discus does not fall away, is not lost; and the edge, the blade, of this weapon does not suffer, that is, does not become blunt. The sense is: with that discus kill the thieves and bring our wealth to light.
- पूष्णः (*pūṣṇaḥ*)—of the god Pūṣan, nourisher of the world
- कोशः (*kośaḥ*)—the sheath of that weapon also
- न अव पद्यते (*na ava padyate*)—does not come to destruction
- नो व्यथते (*no vyathate*)—does not become blunt

The weapon called the discus, of the god Pūṣan, nourisher of the world, is not destroyed. The sheath in which that weapon is placed does not come to destruction either. The edge of this god's weapon does not become blunt.
The discus of Pushan does not destory ; its sheath is not discarded,

The sacrificer who serves this Pūṣan with an oblation, cooked grain, cakes and the like, him Pūṣan does not injure even in the least (the word अपि (*api*) has the sense of "slightly"). And that man, being first, the chief, wins wealth.
- न अपि मृष्यते (*na api mṛṣyate*)—does not destroy
The sacrificer who offers worship to this god Pūṣan by offering oblations, that sacrificer the god Pūṣan does not destroy. That same sacrificer obtains wealth as the most eminent of all.
Pushan inflicts not the least injury on the man who propitiates him
by oblations : he is the the first who acquires wealth.
May Pūṣan, the nourishing god, follow our cattle, going after them for their protection. May that same Pūṣan protect our horses from thieves. And may Pūṣan bestow food on us.
- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—the god Pūṣan, nourisher of the world
May the god Pūṣan, nourisher of the world, follow our cows for their protection. May that same god Pūṣan protect our horses. May the god Pūṣan provide us with food.
May Pushan come to (guard) our cattle, may Pushan protect our houses : may Pushan give us food.⟨NOTE:134⟩
notes: printed English "houses" where the Kannada and the bhāṣya have ಅಶ್ವಗಳನ್ನು (horses)

en: O Pūṣan, go after the cattle of the sacrificer who is pressing the Soma, for their protection; and go also after the cattle of us who sing your praise.
- सुन्वतः (*sunvataḥ*)—who presses the Soma juice (to offer to you)
- अनु प्र इहि (*anu pra ihi*)—follow for their protection
- आस्माकं (*āsmākaṃ*)—follow also for the protection of us
O god Pūṣan, follow for their protection the cows of the sacrificer who presses the Soma juice to offer to you, and follow also for the protection of us who praise you.
Come, Pushan, to (guard) the cattle of of the institutor of the rite
presenting libations, and also of us repeating (your) praises

O Pūṣan, let our cattle-wealth not perish (माकिर्नेशत् (*mākirneśat*)). Let it not be injured by tigers and the like (माकीं रिषत् (*mākīṃ riṣat*)). And let it not be shattered by falling into a well (केवटे (*kevaṭe*)); let it not be harmed even by a fall into a pit. This being so, come in the evening together with the cows that have been left unharmed.
- माकीं रिषत् (*mākīṃ riṣat*)—let it not be injured by tigers and the like
- माकीं सं शारि (*mākīṃ saṃ śāri*)—let it not slip and fall
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—graciously come at evening time
O Pūṣan, let our cattle-wealth not perish. Let it not be injured by tigers and the like. Let it not slip and fall into wells. After protecting them, come at evening time with the cows left unharmed.
Let not, Pushan, our cattle perish; let them not be injured; let them not
be hurt by falling into a well ; come, therefore, along with them unharmed.
We beg for riches from the god Pūṣan, who hears our hymns, who is the remover of poverty (इर्यं (*iryaṃ*)), whose wealth is undestroyed (अनष्टवेदसं (*anaṣṭavedasaṃ*)), the lord of all.
- अनष्ट वेदसं (*anaṣṭa vedasaṃ*)—who has wealth that is free of destruction
- ईशानं (*īśānaṃ*)—who is the master of all
We ask the god Pūṣan, who hears our praises, who destroys poverty, whose wealth is free of destruction and who is the master of all, for wealth.
We solicit riches of Pushan, who hears (our eulogies); who is the averter (of poverty); the preserver of that which is not lost, the ruler (over all).

In the Cāturmāsya sacrifices, at the Vaiśvadeva parvan, this Ṛk पूषन्तव व्रते (*pūṣantava vrate*) is the anuvākyā for the oblation to Pūṣan; it is laid down by the sūtra वाममद्य सवितर्वाममु श्वः पूषन्तव व्रते वयं (*vāmamadya savitarvāmamu śvaḥ pūṣantava vrate vayaṃ*) (Ā. 2-16). O nourishing Pūṣan, we who are engaged in your rite shall never at any time be harmed. Such as we are, here in this rite we are your praisers.
- व्रते (*vrate*)—engaged in your rite of worship
- न रिष्येम (*na riṣyema*)—may we not suffer harm
- स्तोतारः स्मसि (*stotāraḥ smasi*)—are we not your praisers?
O nourishing god Pūṣan, may we, engaged in your rite of worship, never be subject to harm. In this sacrificial rite are we not your praisers?
May we never suffer detriment when engaged, Pushan, in your worship : we are at this time your adorers.

In the sacrifice called Cāturmāsya, at the Vaiśvadeva parvan, in the oblation made to the deity Pūṣan, this Ṛk beginning पूषन् तव (*pūṣan tava*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra: this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra वाममद्य सवितर्वाममु श्वः पूषन्तव व्रते वयं (*vāmamadya savitarvāmamu śvaḥ pūṣantava vrate vayaṃ*) (Ā. 2-16).

May the nourishing god Pūṣan place his own right hand around, as a barrier, to keep back our cattle-wealth that goes to a distant place, to another region inhabited by thieves, tigers and the like⟨NOTE:135⟩. And may he bring back to us again our lost cattle-wealth; may he come with it, may he cause it to come.
notes: ಸುಸಂಚಾರಾದನ್ಯಸ್ಮಿನ್ printed in the bhāṣya; sense unclear

en: - परस्तात् (*parastāt*)—over our cows that roam in forest tracts and the like, full of tigers and others
- परि दधातु (*pari dadhātu*)—let him place over them (so that those cows may not go to an unprotected region)
- आजतु (*ājatu*)—let him bring and join it to us

May the god Pūṣan place his right hand over our cows that roam in forest tracts and the like, full of tigers and others, to prevent them from going to unprotected regions. May he bring again to us our stolen cattle-wealth.
May Pushan put forth his right hand (to restrain our cattle) from going astray : may he bring again to us that which has been lost.

O descendant of Vimuc: Vimuk is Prajāpati, who at the time of creation sends out all creatures from himself. O Aghṛṇa, Pūṣan, whose radiance has come to you, son of Prajāpati! वां (*vāṃ*) is the praiser, he who goes, that is, reaches the praise. Come to me, the praiser who goes to you. And let us two be united. Being such, be for us the swift leader (रथीः (*rathīḥ*)) of the rite (ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)), the sacrifice; in that case the oblation there will be received by you also.
- विमुचः (*vimucaḥ*)—of Prajāpati, who creates all beings at the time of creation
- आघृणे (*āghṛṇe*)—O Pūṣan, who have marvellous radiance
- सं सचावहै (*saṃ sacāvahai*)—let us be united and stay together

O Pūṣan, son of Prajāpati, who at the time of creation brings out into the light all beings hidden within himself, and possessed of marvellous radiance: come graciously to me, your praiser. Let us two be united and stay together. Be the leader of our sacrifice.
Come illustrious grandson of Prajapati to (me, your) worshipper :
let us be associated : become the conveyer of our sacrifice.⟨NOTE:136⟩
notes: printed English "grandson" where ಭಾವಾರ್ಥ and the bhāṣya have ಪುತ್ರ (son)

en: अफ्घणे (*aphghaṇe*)—for this word Yāska has given the explanation:
आघृणिरागतहृणिः आघृणे सं सचावहै । आगशहृणे सं सेवावहै ॥ (*āghṛṇirāgatahṛṇiḥ āghṛṇe saṃ sacāvahai | āgaśahṛṇe saṃ sevāvahai ‖*) (Ni. 5-9) **GLOSS**

Durgācārya, commenting on this, has explained the meaning: आगतदीप्तिरागतक्रोधो वाभिधेयः (*āgatadīptirāgatakrodho vābhidheyaḥ*), that is, one who has blazing radiance, or one who has anger. Although the word आफृणि (*āphṛṇi*) is read both among the names expressing radiance, such as हरः हृणिः (*haraḥ hṛṇiḥ*), and among the names expressing anger, such as हेळः हरः हृणिः (*heḷaḥ haraḥ hṛṇiḥ*), here for the word आफृणि (*āphṛṇi*) the meaning "radiance", that is, "one who has radiance", is the fitting one.

रथीतमं (*rathītamaṃ*) is the one who is the greatest charioteer; or else, the one who is the supreme swift leader. कपर्दिनं (*kapardinaṃ*): kapardaḥ is the hair-knot (cūḍā); he who has it. राधो (*rādho*) is wealth, that by which one prospers. Pūṣan is lord, owner, of great wealth, and our friend; of him, such as he is, we beg riches.
- कपर्दिनं (*kapardinaṃ*)—who has an attractive tuft of hair
- सखायं (*sakhāyaṃ*)—who is a friend to us; Pūṣan
We ask the god Pūṣan, the supreme leader, who has an attractive tuft of hair, who is lord of great wealth and a friend to us, for wealth.
We solicit riches of our friend, (Pushan), the chief of charioteers, the wearer of a braid (of hair), the lord of infinite wealth.

O Pūṣan, shining one, you are the stream of wealth: that is, you give much wealth to your praisers without interruption. Ajāśva means one whose horses, doing the work of horses, are goats. O Pūṣan, such as you are, you are also the heap and the assembly of wealth; the whole mass of wealth dwells in you alone. You are the companion and friend of every man who offers praise.
- धारा असि (*dhārā asi*)—you yourself are the stream
- अजाश्व (*ajāśva*)—O Pūṣan, whose horses have the form of goats

O radiant Pūṣan, for all wealth you yourself are the stream. O Pūṣan, whose horses have the form of goats, for all wealth you yourself are the heap. To every kind of praiser you yourself are the friend.
Illustrious Pushan, you are a torrent of riches: you, who have a goat for your steed, are a heap of wealth ; the friend of every worshipper.

We now praise Pūṣan, the nourisher, the god who has the goat as his vehicle and who is possessed of food or of strength. The Pūṣan who is called the paramour of his sister Uṣas, that Pūṣan is the one to be understood as praised.
- अजाश्वं (*ajāśvaṃ*)—who has a vehicle in the form of goats
- उप स्तोषाम (*upa stoṣāma*)—let us praise and worship

The god Pūṣan who is renowned as the paramour of his sister Uṣas, who has a vehicle in the form of goats, who is possessed of strength and is the nourisher, that god Pūṣan let us now praise and worship.
We glorify Pushan, the rider of the goat, the giver of food, him who is called the gallant of his sister.

I praise Pūṣan, the husband of the mother, that is, of Night, the creator. May Pūṣan, who is also the paramour of his sister Uṣas, hear our praises. May Pūṣan, the brother of Indra, born together with him, be a friend to me, the praiser.
- मातुः (*mātuḥ*)—to Night, the creator of the world
I praise Pūṣan, the husband of Night, the creator of the world. May Pūṣan, the paramour of his sister Uṣas, hear our praises. May Pūṣan, the brother of Indra, be a friend to me, the praiser.
I glorify Pushan, the husband of his mother : may the gallant of his sister hear us ; may the brother of Indra be our friend.

The goats, harnessed together, those goats well known as the vehicles of Pūṣan and bearers of him, carrying in the chariot the god Pūṣan, who goes to the host of worshippers, let them bring him hither.
- जनश्रियं (*janaśriyaṃ*)—who comes near to the praiser
May the goats, which draw the chariot together and are the vehicles of Pūṣan, seat in the chariot the god Pūṣan, who comes near to the praiser, and bear him and bring him hither.
May the harnessed goats, drawing the deity in his car bring hither Pushan, the benefactor of man.

The praiser who declares this Pūṣan, the nourisher, to be the eater of karambha, that is, of barley-meal mixed with ghee, by that man no other god is indicated, no other god is to be directed to or praised. Because all desired wealth is obtained from Pūṣan alone, he does not praise another deity.
- एनं पूषणं (*enaṃ pūṣaṇaṃ*)—with reference to this god Pūṣan
- करंभात् (*karaṃbhāt*)—the eater of barley-meal mixed with ghee
- न आदिशे (*na ādiśe*)—is certainly not indicated
The praiser who, with reference to this god Pūṣan, praises and proclaims "This god is the eater of karambha", by that praiser no other god than Pūṣan is indicated.
No (other) deity is indicated by him who declares the offering of mixed meal and butter to be intended for Pushan.

And that Indra, who is renowned as the slayer of enemies, the greatest of charioteers, the great charioteer, the protector of the good, being joined with Pūṣan as his friend and ally, kills the enemies. The meaning is that Pūṣan is the helper even of Indra.
- सः (*saḥ*)—he who is renowned as the destroyer of enemies
- रथीतमः (*rathītamaḥ*)—the one most excellent among charioteers
- युजा (*yujā*)—who helps him in battle and the like, Pūṣan

Indra, who is renowned as the destroyer of enemies, the great charioteer, the protector of good men, joined with the god Pūṣan, who is his friend and who stays by him and helps him in battle and the like, kills his enemies.
He, the chief of charioteers, the protector of the virtuous, Indra, destroys his foes, with his friend Pushan for his ally.

Pūṣan, the impeller and the greatest of charioteers, or the supreme leader, drives on in the radiant sun, the gauḥ (the one who goes), that golden wheel of his chariot, made of gold. Parus means that which has joints or which shines; gau is the sun, since it goes. He drives it on continually.
- रथीतमः (*rathītamaḥ*)—the supreme leader, the god Pūṣan
- अदः चक्रं (*adaḥ cakraṃ*)—that wheel of the chariot
The god Pūṣan, the impeller of all and the supreme leader, yokes in the radiant sun the golden wheel of the chariot.
He, the impeller, the chief of charioteers, (Pushan), ever urges on that golden wheel (of his car) for the radiant sun.

Gavi: in the sun. On the meaning of the word gau as the sun, Yāska says: आदित्योऽपि गौरुच्यते । उतादः परुषे गवि । पर्ववति भास्वतीत्यौपमन्यवः ॥ (*ādityo 'pi gaurucyate | utādaḥ paruṣe gavi | parvavati bhāsvatītyaupamanyavaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 9-6).

Thus he has given the etymology. The sun too has the name gauḥ, because he is of a moving nature and does not stay even for a moment in one place but is always in motion; so gavi means in the sun. Because he shines with a mass of radiance, gauḥ (gauḥ also means a ray) is the sun or Āditya: this is the opinion of the teacher named Aupamanyava, as Yāska explains.
O Pūṣan, praised by many sacrificers, beautiful to behold, possessed of knowledge, today we praise you for the sake of a wealth; accomplish for us, produce, that wealth worthy of our thought.
- पुरुष्टुत (*puruṣṭuta*)—who is praised by many sacrificers
- मंतुमः (*maṃtumaḥ*)—who has abundant knowledge, O god Pūṣan
- अद्य (*adya*)—at this time of the sacrifice
- यत् (*yat*)—for the sake of which wealth
- मन्म (*manma*)—which is fit for our meditation

O god Pūṣan, who are praised by many sacrificers, who have an attractive form and abundant knowledge, at this time of the sacrifice produce for us that same wealth, worthy of our meditation, for the sake of which we praise you. Provide it for us.
Since, intelligent Pushan, of goodly aspect, the praised of many, we celebrate you to-day, therefore grant us the desired wealth.
O Pūṣan, for our gain, accomplish for this company of men, who are seekers of cows, what they desire. O Pūṣan, you are renowned and famous even in a distant place.
- इमं च गणं (*imaṃ ca gaṇaṃ*)—this company of sacrificers
O god Pūṣan, satisfy this our company of sacrificers, who are searching for cows for the gaining of cows. O god Pūṣan, you are renowned even in very distant places.
Gratify this our assembly, desirous of cattle by their acquistion : you. Pushan, are renowned afar.

O Pūṣan, we beg of you well-being, that is, welfare and protection to be given by you, far from evil, which is attended by wealth; this we ask today and at the time to come, for the sake of the sacrifice (sarvatāti), the sacrifice being so called because it is extended by all the officiating priests and sacrificers ⟨NOTE:137⟩. Or else it is for the spreading of all enjoyments. And tomorrow, on another day also, for the sake of the sacrifice, always, for the sake of all, we ask and entreat.
notes: ಸರ್ವೈರ್ಯುತ್ವಿಗ್ನಿಸ್ತಾಯತ printed; text seems damaged, read as "by all ṛtvijs"

en: - अद्य च (*adya ca*)—today, in the present
- सर्वतातये (*sarvatātaye*)—for the sake of the sacrifice that is performed
- सर्वतातये (*sarvatātaye*)—for the sake of the sacrifices that are performed

O god Pūṣan, so that the sacrifice to be performed today and the sacrifices to be performed in the days to come may be performed without obstacle, we ask abundantly the well-being that is free from sin, that gives wealth and that is bestowed by you.
We deserve of you well-being, remote from evil, approximate to wealth, both for the sake of general sacrifice to-day, for the sake of general sacrifice to-morrow.

The words Indra and Pūṣan are both in the dual because of their mutual conjunction. We now call, that is, invoke and praise, the two gods Indra and Pūṣan, for our well-being, for the sake of an excellent friendship, and for the obtaining and enjoyment of food or strength.
Now we pray to the gods Indra and Pūṣan and invite them, for our well-being, for winning friendship with them and for the obtaining of food.
We invoke you, Indra and Pushan, for your friendship, for our well-being, and for the obtaining of food.
One of the two, Indra, comes and sits near to drink the Soma pressed on the two pressing-boards. The other, Pūṣan, desires to eat the karambha, an offering of barley-meal sprinkled with ghee.
- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—of the two, Indra and Pūṣan, one, Indra
- करंभं (*karaṃbhaṃ*)—the offering mixed with ghee and in the form of barley-meal

Of the two, Indra and Pūṣan, Indra sits down to drink the Soma juice pressed by the pressing-boards that press out the Soma juice. The other, Pūṣan, desires to eat the offering which is mixed with ghee and is in the form of barley-meal.
One (of you) approaches to drink the Soma poured out into ladles, the other desires the buttered meal.

Of these two, Indra and Pūṣan, the one, Pūṣan, has goats as his bearers, his carrying steeds. The other, Indra, has the two well-nourished, strong horses of the name Hari as his bearers. And that Indra, with those two, kills the enemies.
- अन्यस्य (*anyasya*)—to Pūṣan (one of the two, Indra and Pūṣan)
- हरी (*harī*)—the horses called Hari are the vehicle
notes: ತಾಭ್ಯಾಂ glossed ಅವರಿಬ್ಬರಲ್ಲಿ "among the two"; Sāyaṇa has "with those two"

en: Of the two, Indra and Pūṣan, Pūṣan has vehicles in the form of goats. The other, Indra, has as his vehicle the well-grown horses called Hari. Of the two, Indra kills all enemies.
Goats are the bearers of the one, two well-fed horses, of the other, and with them he destroys his foes.

When Indra, the greatest of showerers, brings to this world the great, flowing waters, that is, the waters of the rain, then Pūṣan, the nourishing god, becomes his companion; he becomes Indra's helper.
- वृषंतमः (*vṛṣaṃtamaḥ*)—who sends down rain in abundance
When Indra, who sends down rain in abundance, brings to this world the flowing waters of great power, at that time the god Pūṣan is with him.
When the showerer Indra sends down the falling and mighty waters, there is Pushan along with him
We lay hold of, resort to, that renowned good mind, the gracious thought, of Pūṣan the nourisher and of Indra, as one lays hold of a strong, firm branch of a great tree.
- प्र वयां इव (*pra vayāṃ iva*)—as one resorts to a firm branch
As a man caught in a flood and similar calamities resorts to a firm branch of a great tree, so we resort to the renowned gracious mind of the god Pūṣan and of Indra.
We depend upon the good-will of Pushan, and of Indra, as (we cling) to the branches of a tree.

We draw up, that is, we call to ourselves, Pūṣan the nourisher and Indra for great well-being, for protection. Drawing up means pulling. An example is given: as a charioteer, the driver, pulls to him the reins that serve to bind the horses.
- अभीशूनिव (*abhīśūniva*)—as he pulls the reins toward himself
- उद्युवामहे (*udyuvāmahe*)—we draw to us and make come
As the driver of the chariot pulls the reins (the ropes) toward himself, so we draw Pūṣan and Indra toward us for great welfare and make them come.
We draw to us, for our great welfare, Pushan and Indra, as a charioteer (pulls tight) his reins.

O Pūṣan, one of your forms is white, that is, the day. Another, which is yajata (here the verb yaj has the sense of association): to be joined with, that is, in itself dark, and not shining, is the night, called rāta. Thus the two, the day and the night, are of different forms, white and dark, by your greatness. Or else: one form of yours is white, pure, the producer of the day; the other form of yours is only to be worshipped, not shining, the producer of the night. Hence the day and the night are of unequal forms. It may be asked: the making of day and night is the work of the sun, how does it come to Pūṣan? He answers: you are like heaven, that is, as the sun is the illuminator, so you are the illuminator. Why? O lord of svadhā, possessor of food, because you protect all the wisdoms, therefore you are like the sun. May your auspicious gift be here with us. Yāska says (Ni. 12-17): शुक्रं ते अन्यल्लोहितं ते अन्यदृज्जियं ते अन्यदयज्जियं ते अन्यदिति ना विषमरूपे अहनी कर्मणा द्यौरिव चासि । सर्वाणि च प्रज्ञानान्यवस्यन्नवन् । (*śukraṃ te anyallohitaṃ te anyadṛjjiyaṃ te anyadayajjiyaṃ te anyaditi nā viṣamarūpe ahanī karmaṇā dyauriva cāsi | sarvāṇi ca prajñānānyavasyannavan |*) **GLOSS**
- अन्यत् (*anyat*)—one of your forms, the day
- ते अन्यत् (*te anyat*)—the other, in dark colour, is in the form of night
- अदनी (*adanī*)—day and night, which are your own forms

O god Pūṣan, one of your forms, the day, is of white colour. Another form of yours, to be worshipped, is in the form of night, of dark colour. The day and the night, which are your own forms, are of different forms. You are shining like the sun. O Pūṣan, possessed of food, you protect all creatures. May your auspicious gift be with us
One of your forms, (Pushan), is luminous, one is venerable; so that the day is variously complexioned : for you are like the sun: verily. best-
ower of food, you protect all intelligences: may your auspicious liaberality be manifested on this occasion.

On this ṛk Yāska gives an etymological explanation: शुक्रं ते अन्यल्लोहितं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यद्यज्ञियं ते अन्यद्विषमरूपे अहनी कर्म द्यौरिव चासि सर्वाणि प्रज्ञानान्यवस्यन्नवन् भाजनवती ते पूषन्निह दत्तिरस्तु ॥ (*śukraṃ te anyallohitaṃ te anyadyajataṃ te anyadyajñiyaṃ te anyadviṣamarūpe ahanī karma dyauriva cāsi sarvāṇi prajñānānyavasyannavan bhājanavatī te pūṣanniha dattirastu ‖*) (Ni. 12-17). O god Pūṣan, one of your forms is of red colour, or exceedingly luminous. Another form is worthy of sacrifice, that is, fit to be worshipped with sacrifices and the like. Your two forms, day and night, are of mutually opposed character: that is, since the day is luminous and the night is accompanied by darkness, the one is opposed to the other. Again, like Āditya, or like the light of Āditya, you are pervasive everywhere. You protect all wise people (or all wisdom, or the Śāstras). Besides, you are the possessor of food, that is, the one who provides food to all. Therefore, O god Pūṣan, may a gift of auspicious food and the like be given to us also: this is the chief purport of the explanation. ⟨NOTE:141⟩
notes: ಈ ಮುಕ್ತಿಗೆ printed; read as "to this ṛk"

en: Ajāśva: one whose vehicle is a goat. ⟨NOTE:142⟩ Paśupāḥ: the protector of animals. Vājapasya: one in whose house, pasya, there are foods, vājāḥ. Dhiyaṃjinva: dhiyaḥ are the worshippers or the rites; he is the one who gratifies them. He has been placed by Prajāpati, as the nourisher, in the whole world. Such a Pūṣan, the nourishing god, brandishing the goad held loosely in his own hand, observing all the worlds or all beings, and illuminating them in the form of the Sun, goes, that is, moves in the sky.
notes: the first words of the bhāṣya are damaged: ಆಜಾಶ್ವಶ್ಭಾಗವಾಹನಃ

en: - अजाश्वः (*ajāśvaḥ*)—he who has a horse of goat form
- वाजपस्यः (*vājapasyaḥ*)—he whose house is full of abundance of food
- अर्पितः (*arpitaḥ*)—he who is placed as nourisher
notes: ಪಶುಪಾತಿಃ printed in the gloss; the Saṃhitā and bhāṣya have ಪಶುಪಾಃ
ಕುಲಿಶ (ಅಂಕುಶ) in the gloss; Sāyaṇa glosses ಅಷ್ಟಾಂ as ಆರಾಂ

en: The god Pūṣan, who has a horse of goat form, the herdsman of animals, whose house is full of abundance of food, who satisfies the worshippers, and who is placed as the nourisher in all the worlds, moves about brandishing the loosely held thunderbolt and observing all the worlds.

The rider of the goat, the protector of animals, in whose dwelling food is abundant, the propitiated by sacred rites, who has been placed over the whole (world) the divine Pushan, brandishing his loosened goad, proceeds (in the sky), contemplating all beings.

For the vapā and the puroḍāśa of the animal belonging to Pūṣan, the two ṛks beginning यास्ते पूषन् (*yāste pūṣan*) are anuvākyā verses. This is laid down in the Sūtra (Ā. 3-7). O Pūṣan, those golden, beneficial and delightful ships of yours that move within the ocean, in the sky: with those ships you go on the errand of Sūrya as his messenger. Once, when Sūrya had set out with the gods to slay the Asuras, his wife became anxious about her husband. Sūrya sent Pūṣan to her, and therefore Pūṣan is praised here. Moreover, you desire the food that is the oblation, śravas, and you have been brought under control by the worshippers through their desire, directed to cattle and the like.
- श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)—the food in the form of the oblation

O god Pūṣan, with those vessels made of gold that move in the sky, which is as the middle of the ocean, you carry out the duty of Sūrya. Desiring the food in the form of the oblation, you are brought under control by the oblation offered willingly.

With those your golden vessels, which navigate within the ocean-firmament, you discharge the office of messenger of the sun: desirous of the sacrificial food, you are propitiated by (that which is) willingly offered.

When the vapā and puroḍāśa offerings are made in the animal sacrifice performed for the deity Pūṣan, the two ṛks beginning यास्ते पूषन् (*yāste pūṣan*) (this ṛk and the next) are to be recited as anuvākyā mantras. This is set out by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: यास्ते पूषन्नावो अंतः समुद्र इति द्वे पूषेमा आशा अनु वेद सर्वाः (*yāste pūṣannāvo aṃtaḥ samudra iti dve pūṣemā āśā anu veda sarvāḥ*) (Ā. 2-7). ⟨NOTE:145⟩
notes: reference ಆ ೨-೭ here; the bhāṣya has ಆ. ೩-೭

en: Pūṣan, the nourishing god, is a good kinsman of heaven and of earth. Likewise he is the lord of iḷā, food, and maghavā: magha is a name for wealth, and he possesses it; or else the word magha comes from the root mahate, which is in the sense of giving, and the word is formed with the sense of the act itself: he is a giver. He is dasmavarcāḥ: varcas is a name for form, and dasma means to be looked at; he is one whose form is pleasing to look at. Him, Pūṣan, all the gods gave to Sūryā, who is Sūrya's wife, or else to Sāvitrī under the name Sūryā, for the choosing of the Aśvins. ⟨NOTE:146⟩ It is heard: पुत्रः पितराववृणीत पूषा (*putraḥ pitarāvavṛṇīta pūṣā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-14). ⟨NOTE:147⟩ What kind of Pūṣan? One brought under control by the worshippers through desire directed to cattle and the like; strong, or grown great; svañc, that is, moving well. The construction is: the Pūṣan whom they gave, such a Pūṣan is the good kinsman.
notes: ಆಶ್ವಿನೋರ್ವರಣಾಯಾದದುಃ: the exact construction is unclear
abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ. printed

en: - दिवि आ (*divi ā*)—to the whole heaven
notes: ಒಂಭುವೂ printed; read as ಬಂಧುವೂ "kinsman"

en: Him who has been carried by oblations and the like to the control of the sacrificer ⟨NOTE:149⟩, who is full of strength and of excellent movement, the god Pūṣan whom all the gods offered to the daughter of Sūrya: such a Pūṣan, the lord of food, the wealthy one, of attractive lustre, is a good kinsman to the whole heaven and to the earth.
notes: ಯಜಮಾನನ ವರಕ್ಕೆ printed; ವರಕ್ಕೆ doubtful

en: Pushan is the kind kinsman of heaven and earth, the lord of food, the possessor of opulence, of goodly from; whom the gods gave to Surya, vigorous, well-moving, propitiated by (that which is) willingly offered.

O Indra and Agni, the heroic deeds that you two have done, those deeds of yours I quickly proclaim at the Soma pressings, in our sacrifice. He shows that very heroism. O Indra and Agni, the Asuras, whose destroyers, enemies, are the gods, and who are pitaraḥ, injurers (the root pī has the sense of injuring, and this is its form): such Asuras were slain by you two. But you two live: you are living, that is, not harassed by the Asuras.
- वां (*vāṃ*)—all those heroic deeds of yours
- सुतेषु (*suteṣu*)—when the Soma juice is pressed
- प्रवोच (*pravoca*)—I recite, O Indra and Agni
- देवशत्रवः (*devaśatravaḥ*)—who are as enemies to all the gods

O Indra and Agni, all the famous heroic deeds that you have done, I quickly recite as soon as the Soma juice is pressed. O Indra and Agni, the Asuras, who are as enemies and injurers to all the gods, have been slain by you two. But you two alone have lived unharmed.
When the libation is effused I celebrate, Indra and Agni, your heroic exploits: the Pitris, the enemies of the gods, have been slain by you, and you survive.

O Indra and Agni, your greatness is thus; बट् (*baṭ*) means truth. Whatever is declared concerning your birth and greatness is all as it truly is. Panishtha, the most praiseworthy Prajāpati, is one and the same begetter of you both. Therefore you two are brothers. Moreover you are twins, born together, and इहेहमातरा (*ihehamātarā*): you are such that your mother is here and here, that is, everywhere. For Aditi is the mother of these two, and she is the wide earth; thus it is heard, in the word इहेहमातरा (*ihehamātarā*).
- इहेहमातरा (*ihehamātarā*)—are possessed of mothers who stand everywhere (the earth)
O Indra and Agni, it is indeed true that your greatness is of this kind. The most venerable Prajāpati is the one and only father of you both. You two are brothers.
You two, born together, are possessed of mothers who stand everywhere. Aditi, the mother of the gods, who pervades everywhere, is your mother.
Your greatness, Indra and Agni, is after this fashion, and is most deserving of praise: the same is your progenitor: twin brothers are you, having a mother everywhere present.

यमौ इहेहमातरा (*yamau ihehamātarā*)—here यमौ (*yamau*) means twins, children born together. Indra and Agni are described here as twins, because Prajāpati himself is the father of Indra and Agni and Aditi, the mother of the gods, is their mother. Therefore Indra and Agni are brothers to each other, and since they were born together at one time, they are twins. Since Aditi is also said to be this wide earth, one may say that the earth is their mother. Yāska, for the subject of twins, has cited as an example the very sentence of this ṛk, यमाविहेहमातरा (*yamāvihehamātarā*) (Ni. 10-21).

O Indra and Agni, when the Soma is pressed, you two together come together, are united. An illustration is given: as two swift-moving horses come together at their food, their fodder. Now, today, we here in this sacrifice call such Indra and Agni, for the purpose of protection. What are Indra and Agni like? They are armed with the thunderbolt, as weapon, and they are gods endowed with qualities such as generosity.
- सप्ति (*sapti*)—(O Indra and Agni,) of swift-moving
- आदने (*ādane*)—as they gather together for eating
- सुते (*sute*)—at the time when the Soma juice is pressed
- ओकिवांसा (*okivāṃsā*)—and become possessed of one place

O Indra and Agni, as swift-moving horses gather together to eat grass, so at this time when the Soma juice is pressed you two come together and become possessed of one place. Now, in this sacrifice, for our protection, we call with prayer Indra and Agni, the holders of the thunderbolt weapon, who are of divine nature.

You approach together, when the libation is effused, like two fleet coursers to their forage: we invoke to-day Indra and Agni, deities armed with the thunderbolt, to this ceremony for our preservation.

O Indra and Agni, augmenters of ṛta, that is, of truth or of the sacrifice: the worshipper who, when the Soma is pressed, praises you ill, in those Soma offerings speaks a जोषवाकं (*joṣavākaṃ*), a speech that is to be made pleasing, that ought to be done as a cause of pleasure, but is itself not pleasing: of that worshipper, of his Soma, O you of famous praise-sound…

…that is, those whose pajra, famous, hoṣa, sound of praise, is such; O gods, you two do not eat, you do not consume his Soma. The word चन (*cana*) is a filler of the line. Here he cites the Nirukta: जोषवाकमित्यविज्ञातनामधेयं जोषयितव्यं भवति । य इंद्राग्नी सुतेषु वां सोमेषु स्तौति तेष्टृतस्य वर्धयितारौ न तस्याश्नीथः । योऽयं जोषवाकं वदति विजंजपः प्रार्जितहोषिणौ देवौ न तस्याश्नीथः । (*joṣavākamityavijñātanāmadheyaṃ joṣayitavyaṃ bhavati | ya iṃdrāgnī suteṣu vāṃ someṣu stauti teṣṭṛtasya vardhayitārau na tasyāśnīthaḥ | yo 'yaṃ joṣavākaṃ vadati vijaṃjapaḥ prārjitahoṣiṇau devau na tasyāśnīthaḥ |*) (Ni. 5-22). **GLOSS**
- पज्रहोषिणा (*pajrahoṣiṇā*)—possessed of famous sound of praise
- सुतेषु (*suteṣu*)—at the time when the Soma juice is pressed
- जोषवाकं (*joṣavākaṃ*)—a sentence of praise that does not give satisfaction
- न भसथः (*na bhasathaḥ*)—you do not eat the oblation
notes: ಯತಾವೃಧಾ printed; the Saṃhitā has ಋತವೃಧಾ

en: O Indra and Agni, augmenters of the sacrifice, possessed of famous sound of praise, of divine nature: at the time when the Soma juice is pressed, among those worshippers who praise you both ill, and among those who praise with a sentence of praise that does not give satisfaction, you do not eat the oblation.

Divine Indra and Agni, augmenters of sacrifice, by whom the acclamation (of praise) is received, you partake not of the (Soma) of him who, when the libation is effused, praises you (improperly), uttering unacceptable eulogies.

अप्रीतिकरं वाक्यं (*aprītikaraṃ vākyaṃ*): a sentence without love. To explain the meaning of this word जोषवाकं (*joṣavākaṃ*), Yāska has given an etymological explanation on this ṛk: जोषवाकमित्यविज्ञा तनामधेयं जीषयितव्यं भवति । य इंद्राग्नी सुतेषु वां स्तवत्तेष्टृतावृधा । जोषवाकं वदतः पज्रहोषिणा न देवा भसथश्चन ॥ य इंद्राग्नी सुतेषु वां सोमेषु स्तौति तस्याश्नीथोऽथ योऽयं जोषवाकं वदति विजञ्चपः प्रार्जितहोषिणौ न देवौ तस्माश्नीथः ॥ (*joṣavākamityavijñā tanāmadheyaṃ jīṣayitavyaṃ bhavati | ya iṃdrāgnī suteṣu vāṃ stavatteṣṭṛtāvṛdhā | joṣavākaṃ vadataḥ pajrahoṣiṇā na devā bhasathaścana ‖ ya iṃdrāgnī suteṣu vāṃ someṣu stauti tasyāśnītho 'tha yo 'yaṃ joṣavākaṃ vadati vijañcapaḥ prārjitahoṣiṇau na devau tasmāśnīthaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 5-22). ⟨NOTE:153⟩

O Indra and Agni, as soon as the Soma juice is pressed, whichever worshipper praises you both, you accept and eat the oblation, or the Soma, that he offers. But the worshipper who, while praising, recites what is not known to himself or what is not pleasing, and so praises: what he offers you do not accept and eat. This is the chief purport of the explanation.

There is a slight difference between Sāyaṇa's explanation and Yāska's with regard to the first half of this ṛk. Sāyaṇa has taken the meaning to be that they do not eat the oblation of the man who praises Indra and Agni ill, that is, with blame, with fault, in the form of contempt. But Yāska has explained that they eat the oblation of the worshipper who praises after the pressing of the Soma, but that if there is blame in that praise, or sentences without love, they do not eat his oblation. Here there is room for both kinds of meaning.
notes: ಜೀಷಯಿತವ್ಯಂ and ತಸ್ಮಾಶ್ನೀಥಃ printed in the Nirukta quotation

en: O shining gods Indra and Agni, which mortal, which man, would know this deed of you two? That is, none would. What is that deed? One of you two, Indra, who exists in the form of Sūrya, yoking horses that go in diverse directions, in a single common path that serves both, goes, that is, approaches the whole world. Or else: yoking horses of diverse forms, pervasive, in a common car of one form, which is in the form of the year, one of you two, Indra in the form of Sūrya, comes, approaches. Who could truly know this deed of yours is the sense.
- समाने रथे (*samāne rathe*)—seated in the one car common to both of you
- आ ईयते (*ā īyate*)—while he travels in the form of Sūrya
- अस्य (*asya*)—this deed in the form of travelling

O shining Indra and Agni, when one of you two, Indra, seated in the one car common to both of you, having yoked to the car horses that go everywhere, travels in the form of Sūrya, what man indeed can know this deed of yours, in the form of travelling, and its aim?
What mortal, divine Indra and Agni, is a judge of that (your act), when one of you, harnessing his diversely-going horses, proceeds in the common car.

O Indra and Agni, this Uṣas, who is footless, comes first, before the footed creatures that are asleep; so, having come first, she sets in motion the heads of living beings. Or else: having given up her head, herself headless, with the tongue that is situated in living beings, her own…

…by which organ of speech she moves, making a loud sound, not speaking. Thus moving, Uṣas traverses thirty steps, that is, the thirty muhūrtas that are her parts; she passes over them in one day. And this is the deed of you two: who could know it? This is the connection with the preceding verse.
- पद्वतीभ्यः (*padvatībhyaḥ*)—than the creatures that have feet
- पूर्वा (*pūrvā*)—as the one who comes first
- जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)—through the speech-organs of living beings
- त्रिंशत् पदा (*triṃśat padā*)—as far as thirty steps (as long as thirty muhūrtas)

O Indra and Agni, this goddess Uṣas, who is without feet, appears and comes even before the creatures that have feet. Hiding her head, moving and causing sound to be made through the speech-organs of living beings, she becomes visible for thirty muhūrtas. All this is the power of Indra and Agni. What man can know it?

This footless (dawn), Indra and Agni, comes before the footed sleepers, animating the head (of living beings with consciousness), causing them to utter loud sounds with their tongues, and passing onwards she traverses thirty steps.

O Indra and Agni, the warriors, the men, stretch the bows in their arms, that is, they make them strung. And you two, in this great-wealth combat, one that is endowed with great wealth to be won, in the seekings of cows, do not abandon us. ⟨NOTE:154⟩
notes: ಸಂಗಾ ಮೇ printed in the bhāṣya; the sense required seems to be "in the battle"

en: - आ तन्वते हि (*ā tanvate hi*)—have stretched and hold, have they not
- आस्मिन् महाधने (*āsmin mahādhane*)—in this battle fought for abundant wealth
- गविष्टिषु (*gaviṣṭiṣu*)—while we are engaged in the effort to seek cows
- मा परा वर्क्तं (*mā parā varktaṃ*)—do not abandon, and do not let us fall into the power of enemies

O Indra and Agni, men engaged in battle have stretched and hold their bows with their arms, have they not! In this battle fought for the gain of abundant wealth, while we are engaged in the effort to seek cows, do not abandon us and do not let us fall into the power of enemies.
Indra and Agni, men verily stretch their bows with their arms, but do not desert us contending for cattle in the great combat.

O Indra and Agni, the murderous ones, the attackers, the enemy armies, harass me. Drive them away. Likewise the haters, the enemies who hate us, separate from the sight of the sun. Separate them, and do so that they do not see the sun; the sense is, kill them.
- अप आ कृतं (*apa ā kṛtaṃ*)—drive them far away
- सूर्यादधि (*sūryādadhi*)—from the sight of the sun
- युयुतं (*yuyutaṃ*)—separate them (make it so that they have neither sight of the sun nor the light of the sun)
notes: ಹಿಸಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ printed; read as ಹಿಂಸಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ

en: O Indra and Agni, the enemies, who are sinful and fall upon us, harass me. Drive them far away. Separate the enemies who hate us from the sight of the sun, that is, make it so that they have no light of the sun.
Indra and Agni, murderous, aggressive enemies harass us: drive away my adversaries: separate them from (sight of) the sun.

O Indra and Agni, the treasures that are in heaven and those on earth, belonging to the two worlds, all of them are truly yours alone. For that reason, here in this sacrifice, bestow wealth upon us. What kind of wealth? विश्वायुपोषसं (*viśvāyupoṣasaṃ*): आयव (*āyava*) is a name for men; wealth that is sufficient for the nourishment of all men. Or else: able to nourish the whole life.
- दिव्यानि (*divyāni*)—that which is in the world of heaven
- पार्थिवा (*pārthivā*)—and that which is on earth
- वसु अपि (*vasu api*)—all the riches as well
- इह (*iha*)—at the time of this sacrifice
- आ प्र यच्छतं (*ā pra yacchataṃ*)—provide and give
O Indra and Agni, all the riches that are in the world of heaven and those that are on earth belong to you two alone. At the time of this sacrifice, provide for us wealth that nourishes all men.
Indra and Agni, yours are both celestial and terrestrial treasures: bestow upon us, on this occasion, life-sustaining riches.

O you who are borne by loud praises, O you who hear the invocation, the call: O Indra and Agni, such as you are, come with the praises, with all the speeches in the form of śastras, which are the means. For what purpose? For the drinking of this Soma of ours.
- उक्तवाहसा (*uktavāhasā*)—you who are borne by the recited mantras
- स्तोमेभिः (*stomebhiḥ*)—by praises in the form of stomas
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—speeches in the form of śastras (being drawn)
- आ गतं (*ā gataṃ*)—be pleased to come

O Indra and Agni, who are borne by the recited mantras and who hear our praises, drawn by the praises in the form of stomas and by all the speeches in the form of śastras, be pleased to come to drink the Soma offered in this sacrifice.
Indra and Agni, who are to be attracted by hymns; you, who hear our invocation (accompanied) by praises and by all adorations, come hither to drink of this Soma libation.
