That man smites (श्नथत् (*śnathat*), he kills) the enemy Vṛtra, the obstructer, and also wins food or strength (वाजं (*vājaṃ*)), who would serve Indra and Agni, the two overcomers of enemies. The dual is used in both places by the mutual connection of the two deities, as before. Of what kind are Indra and Agni? They are lords (इरज्यंता (*irajyaṃtā*)) of abundant wealth (वसव्यस्य (*vasavyasya*)), that is, of a multitude of treasures; or the word for wealth is formed with an added suffix, and the two are its masters, since इरज्यति (*irajyati*) is a verb of lordship. They overcome enemies most mightily (सहस्तमा (*sahastamā*)) by strength (सहसा (*sahasā*)). Desiring food (वाजयंता (*vājayaṃtā*)) for themselves ⟨NOTE:157⟩; or else, desiring the food that is to be given to the worshippers.
notes: ದನಿರ್ಲಕ್ಷಣಮನ್ನಂ: machine-read, sense doubtful

en: - वाजयंता (*vājayaṃtā*)—who desire food in the form of oblation
- सहुरी (*sahurī*)—who crush and defeat the enemies
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—the deities who are Indra and Agni
- वृतं (*vṛtaṃ*)—the enemy who has besieged him

The man who worships the deities Indra and Agni, who are lords of the whole abundant mass of wealth, who confront enemies with exceeding strength, who desire food in the form of oblation, and who crush and defeat enemies, strikes down and kills the enemy who has besieged him. And he obtains food as well.
He overcomes his enemy, and acquires food, who worships the victorious Indra and Agni, the lords of infinite opulence, most powerful in strength, desirous of (sacrificial) food.

O Indra, O Agni, you two fought (योधिष्टं (*yodhiṣṭaṃ*)) with the Asuras, having in view the cows, the waters, the sun and the dawns, which had been carried off by the Paṇis; the word नूनं (*nūnaṃ*) serves only to fill out the pāda. O Indra, you unite (युवसे (*yuvase*)) the quarters, east and the rest, the sun, the dawns, the wonderful waters and the cows carried off by the Paṇis, with this world. Or else: having slain the Asuras who had enclosed the quarters and the rest, you removed the covering and set them apart; this is the sense. O Agni, possessed of the Niyut horses, you too did the same.
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—for the sake of the waters
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—for the sake of gaining the sun
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—with the aim of obtaining the dawn
- अभि योधिष्टं (*abhi yodhiṣṭaṃ*)—you fight with the enemies
- दितः (*ditaḥ*)—the quarters, east and the rest
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the cows carried off by the Paṇis
- युवसे (*yuvase*)—you set in their respective places
- नियुत्वान् (*niyutvān*)—you, who have the horses named Niyut, have also accomplished the same deeds

O Indra, O Agni, you two have certainly fought with the enemies for the cows carried off by the Paṇis, for the waters, for the gaining of the sun, and with the aim of obtaining the dawn. O Indra, you set in their respective places the quarters, east and the rest, the sun, the dawns, the attractive waters and the cows carried off by the Paṇis. O Agni, you too, who have the horses named Niyut, have accomplished the same deeds.

Indra and Agni, verily you have combated for (the recovery of) the cows, the waters, the sun, the dawns that had been carried away (by the Asuras): you reunite, Indra, (with the world), the quarters of the horizon, the sun, the wonderful waters, the dawns, the cattle, and so do you, Agni, who have the Niyut steeds.

This ṛk, आ वृत्रहणा (*ā vṛtrahaṇā*), is the anuvākyā for the vapā-oblation of the animal offered to Indra and Agni. It is laid down in the Sūtra: आ वृत्रहणा वृत्रहभिः शुष्मैरा भरतं शिक्षतं वज्रबाहू (*ā vṛtrahaṇā vṛtrahabhiḥ śuṣmairā bharataṃ śikṣataṃ vajrabāhū*) (Ā. 3-7). O slayers of Vṛtra, the Asura, O Indra, O Agni, come (यातं (*yātaṃ*)) towards us, facing us, together with strengths (शुष्मैः (*śuṣmaiḥ*)) that are the killers of Vṛtra, that is, that serve to slay Vṛtra, and with the foods that are to be given to us (नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)). O Indra, O Agni, be manifest (भवतं (*bhavataṃ*)) among us together with blameless, great and most excellent riches.
- नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)—and with the foods that we need, endowed
- आ यातं (*ā yātaṃ*)—be so kind as to come

O Indra and Agni, slayers of enemies, be so kind as to come facing us, endowed with strengths that destroy enemies and with the foods that we need. O Indra, O Agni, appear and show yourselves before us together with riches that are not blameworthy and are praiseworthy.
Slayers of Vritra, Indra and Agni, come down with foe-subduing energies, (to be invigorated) by (our) offerings: be manifest to us, Indra and Agni, with unblameable and most excellent riches.

At the offering of the vapā in the animal sacrifice made to Indra and Agni, this ṛk beginning आ वृत्रहणा (*ā vṛtrahaṇā*) is to be recited as an anuvākyā mantra; this is set out by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, आ वृत्रहणा वृत्रहभिः शुष्मैरा भरतं शिक्षतं वज्रबाहू (*ā vṛtrahaṇā vṛtrahabhiḥ śuṣmairā bharataṃ śikṣataṃ vajrabāhū*) (Ā. 3-7).

On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the morning pressing, in the śastra of the Acchāvāka, the tṛca beginning ता हुवे (*tā huve*) is the ṣaḍaha-stotriya. It is laid down in the Sūtra: ता हुवे ययोरिदमियं वामस्य मन्मनः (*tā huve yayoridamiyaṃ vāmasya manmanaḥ*) (Ā. 7-2). In the Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava ṣaḍahas, for the increase of the stoma, the nine ṛks beginning with ता हुव (*tā huva*) are for insertion (āvāpa). It is laid down: ता हुवे ययोरिदमिति नवेयं वामस्य मन्मन इत्येकादश (*tā huve yayoridamiti naveyaṃ vāmasya manmana ityekādaśa*) (Ā. 7-5).

I call (हुवे (*huve*)) those two, Indra and Agni, such as they are, of whom all this heroic deed, done in former time and proclaimed in the earlier ṛks, is praised (पप्ने (*papne*)) by the seers. The construction is: I call those Indra and Agni. And may those two not harm (न मर्धतः (*na mardhataḥ*)) the one who praises them; hence may they protect us who have called them; this is the sense. The verb मर्धति (*mardhati*) denotes harming. ⟨NOTE:158⟩
notes: ಅತೋಽಸ್ಥಾನಪ್ಯಾಹೂತ್ ರಕ್ಷತಾಮಿತಿ ಭಾವಃ — machine-read, damaged; sense taken as "protect us who have called"

en: - न मर्धतः (*na mardhataḥ*)—do not harm us
We pray and invoke those renowned Indra and Agni, by whom all the heroic deeds performed in all former times and described by the earlier mantras have been praised. Do not harm us.
I invoke those two, the whole of whose deeds of old have been celebrated : Indra and Agni harm us not.

On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, at the morning pressing, among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Acchāvāka, the three ṛks beginning with ता हुवे (*tā huve*) (ṛks 4–6 of this sūkta) are to be recited as the ṣaḍaha-stotriya tṛca; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the Sūtra ता हुवे ययोरिदमियं वामस्य मन्मनः (*tā huve yayoridamiyaṃ vāmasya manmanaḥ*) (Ā. 3-2) ⟨NOTE:159⟩. And in the sacrifices called Pṛṣṭha and Abhiplava ṣaḍaha, for the increase of the stoma, the nine ṛks beginning with ता हुवे (*tā huve*) (ṛks 4–12 of this sūkta) are to be recited as āvāpa mantras; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the Sūtra ता हुवे ययोरिदमिति नवेयं वामस्य मन्मन इत्येकादश (*tā huve yayoridamiti naveyaṃ vāmasya manmana ityekādaśa*) (Ā. 7-5).
notes: ಆ. ೩-೨ printed; the bhāṣya block cites ಆ. ೭-೨ for the same sūtra

en: We call (हवामहे (*havāmahe*)) Indra and Agni, who are fierce (उग्रा (*ugrā*)), that is, of uplifted strength, and for that very reason are the special slayers (विघनिना (*vighaninā*)) of enemies (मृधः (*mṛdhaḥ*)). May those two, Indra and Agni, in such a battle as this, make us happy (मृळातः (*mṛḷātaḥ*)). Or else: the verb मृळति (*mṛḷati*) denotes compassion; may they show compassion to us.
- उग्रा (*ugrā*)—who have strength terrible to enemies
We pray and invoke Indra and Agni, who have strength terrible to enemies and who destroy enemies. May those same Indra and Agni make us happy in such a battle.
We invoke the fierce Indra and Agni, the slayers of enemies: may they give us success in similar warfare.

Those two, Indra and Agni, destroy (हतः (*hataḥ*)) the afflictions (वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)) that have arisen as troubles caused by the Āryas, the performers of rites. Likewise they, as protectors of the good (सत्पती (*satpatī*)), destroy the troubles (दासानि (*dāsāni*)) made by the Dāsas, the enemies who are without rites. And further, they utterly destroy all hostile (द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)) creatures who are enemies. The sense is: therefore may they do just so for us also.
- आर्या (*āryā*)—done by the Āryas, the performers of rites
- सत्पती (*satpatī*)—those same Indra and Agni, protectors of the good
- दासानि (*dāsāni*)—also the troubles caused by enemies who are without rites
Indra and Agni destroy all the afflictions caused either by the Āryas, the performers of rites, or by the enemies who are in the form of Dāsas, without rites. And they destroy all hostile people.
Counteract all oppressions (committed) by the pious : counteract all oppressions (committed) by the impious : protectors of the virtuous, destroy all those who hate us.

On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the morning pressing, in the śastra of the Acchāvāka, the tṛca beginning इंद्राग्नी युवां (*iṃdrāgnī yuvāṃ*) is the ṣaḍaha-stotriya. It is laid down in the Sūtra: इंद्राग्नी युवामिमे यज्ञस्य हि स्थ ऋत्विजेत्यच्छावाकस्य (*iṃdrāgnī yuvāmime yajñasya hi stha ṛtvijetyacchāvākasya*) (Ā. 7-2). O Indra and Agni, these praisers (स्तोमाः (*stomāḥ*)) glorify (अभ्यनूषत (*abhyanūṣata*)) you. O Śaṃbhuvā, you two who cause happiness, drink (पिबतं (*pibataṃ*)) my Soma that has been pressed (सुतं (*sutaṃ*)).
- शंभुवा (*śaṃbhuvā*)—O Indra and Agni, who bring happiness
O Indra and Agni, these praisers glorify you both. O Indra and Agni, who bring happiness, drink this pressed Soma juice.
Indra and Agni, these hymns glorify you both ; drink, bestowers of of happiness, the libation.

On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, at the morning pressing, among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Acchāvāka, the three ṛks beginning with इंद्राग्नी युवां (*iṃdrāgnī yuvāṃ*) (ṛks 7–9 of this sūkta) are to be recited as the ṣaḍaha-stotriya tṛca; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the Sūtra इंद्राग्नी युवामिमे यज्ञस्य हि स्थ ऋत्विजेत्यच्छावाकस्य (*iṃdrāgnī yuvāmime yajñasya hi stha ṛtvijetyacchāvākasya*) (Ā. 7-2).

O leaders, Indra and Agni, those Niyut horses (नियुतः (*niyutaḥ*)) that are your own, much desired (पुरुस्पृहः (*puruspṛhaḥ*)) by many, and have come into being for the sacrificer who has given oblations (दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)), with those Niyuts, O Indra and Agni, come (आ गतं (*ā gataṃ*)).
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—produced for the sacrificer who offers oblations
- आ गतं (*ā gataṃ*)—be so kind as to come
O Indra and Agni, leaders of the world, be so kind as to come with those horses of yours that are desired by many and are produced for the sacrificer who offers oblations.
Indra and Agni, leaders (of rites), whose Niyut steeds are desired by many, come with them to the donor (of the libatation.)

O leaders, Indra and Agni. Savana is Soma, since it is pressed (सूयते (*sūyate*)). The words इदं सवनं (*idaṃ savanaṃ*) mean this Soma that has been pressed, and उप (*upa*) means towards. Or else: इदं (*idaṃ*) refers to this morning pressing, and the sense is towards the Soma pressed at this pressing,
come with those Niyut horses. For what purpose? For the drinking (सोमपीतये (*somapītaye*)) of that Soma.
- इदं सवनं उप (*idaṃ savanaṃ upa*)—facing this Soma juice
- आ गच्छतं (*ā gacchataṃ*)—be so kind as to come
O Indra and Agni, leaders, for the drinking of this Soma that has been pressed and made ready, be so kind as to come, with your horses, facing this juice:
Come with them, leaders (of rites), to the effused libation, to drink, Indra and Agni, of the Soma.

O praiser, praise (ईळिष्ट (*īḷiṣṭa*)) that Agni who, with his flame, his brilliance in the form of fire, embraces (परिष्वजत् (*pariṣvajat*)) all forests, that is, wraps them round on every side; and who, having burnt those forests with his tongue, the flame, makes them black (कृष्णा (*kṛṣṇā*)).
- जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)—with his tongue in the form of flame
- कृष्णा (*kṛṣṇā*)—all those forests black in colour
O praiser, praise that Agni who with his brilliance envelops all the forests, and with his tongue in the form of flame makes all those forests black in colour.
Glorify that Agni who envelopes all the forests with flame, who blackens them with (his) tongue.

The mortal, the man, who into the kindled (इद्दे (*idde*)), blazing fire presents (आविवासति (*āvivāsati*)) a pleasing (सुम्मं (*summaṃ*)) oblation for Indra, for that mortal's shining food Indra makes the waters (अपः (*apaḥ*)), that is, rain, easy to cross (सुतराः (*sutarāḥ*)); this is the word to be supplied.
- इद्दे (*idde*)—when the sacrificial fire is kindled
- द्युम्नायॆ (*dyumnāyè*)—for the attainment of shining food
- सुतराः (*sutarāḥ*)—that carry the sacrificer easily across distress

To that mortal sacrificer who, when the sacrificial fire is kindled, presents a pleasing oblation to Indra, Indra gives the waters of rain, which carry him easily across distress, for the gaining of shining food.
The mortal who presents the gratifying (oblation) to Indra in the kindled (fire), to him (Indra grants) acceptable waters for his sustenance.

O Indra and Agni, you two, grant us (पिपृतं (*pipṛtaṃ*), fill, bestow) the food-rich (वाजवतीः (*vājavatīḥ*)) wished-for rain (इषः (*iṣaḥ*)). Or else: vāja is strength, and the इषः (*iṣaḥ*) endowed with it are foods; and grant us swift-going (आशून् (*āśūn*)) horses (अर्वतः (*arvataḥ*)). For what purpose? In order to carry (वोळ्हवे (*voḷhave*)) Indra and Agni, that is, to convey you with oblations.
- इंद्रमग्निं च (*iṃdramagniṃ ca*)—to you, who are Indra and Agni
O Indra and Agni, renowned as you are, provide us with horses that are supplied with food, endowed with strength and swift-going, for bearing the oblation to you, who are Indra and Agni.
May those two grant us strengthening food, and swift horses to convey (our offerings).

This ṛk, उभा वां (*ubhā vāṃ*), is the anuvākyā for the oblation of the animal offered to Indra and Agni. It is laid down in the Sūtra: उभा वामिंद्राग्नी आहुवध्यै शुचिं नु स्तोमं नव जातमद्य (*ubhā vāmiṃdrāgnī āhuvadhyai śuciṃ nu stomaṃ nava jātamadya*) (Ā. 3-7). O Indra and Agni, both of you, being together, I call (हुवे (*huve*)) you. For what purpose? In order to sacrifice before you (आहुवध्यै (*āhuvadhyai*)). Likewise I call you both, in order that together, at one and the same time, you may be gratified (मादयध्यै (*mādayadhyai*)) and satisfied with the accomplishing oblation (राधसः (*rādhasaḥ*)). If it is asked what is the reason for calling you two when all the gods are present, it is said: both of you are givers of foods (इषां (*iṣāṃ*)) and of riches (रयीणां (*rayīṇāṃ*)). For that reason I call you both for the sharing (सातये (*sātaye*)) of food (वाजस्य (*vājasya*)).
- आ हुवध्यै (*ā huvadhyai*)—to offer the oblation

O Indra and Agni, I pray and invoke you both, who are together, to offer the oblation. With oblations may you both enjoy satisfaction at one and the same time. You both are givers of foods and of riches. I call you both, who are together, for the attainment of food.

I invoke you both, Indra and Agni, to be present at the sacrifice ; and both together to be exhilarated by the (sacrificial) food ; for you are both donors of food and riches, and therefore I invoke you both for the obtaining of sustenance

In the animal sacrifice made for Indra and Agni, when the oblation is offered, this ṛk beginning उभा वां (*ubhā vāṃ*) is to be recited as an anuvākyā mantra; this is set out by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, उभा वामिंद्राग्नी आहुवध्यॆ शुचिं नु स्तोमं नवजातमद्य (*ubhā vāmiṃdrāgnī āhuvadhyè śuciṃ nu stomaṃ navajātamadya*) (A. 3-7) ⟨NOTE:160⟩.
notes: abbreviation ಅ. printed; the bhāṣya block of this ṛk has ಆ. ೩-೭

en: O Indra and Agni, come towards us, facing us, together with herds of cows (गव्येभिः (*gavyebhiḥ*)), troops of horses (अश्वैः (*aśvaiḥ*)) and masses of wealth (वसवैः (*vasavaiḥ*)). You are friends (सखायौ (*sakhāyau*)) of equal renown, gods endowed with qualities such as generosity, Śaṃbhuvā, producers of happiness. Those same Indra and Agni we call (हवामहे (*havāmahe*)) for the sake of friendship (सख्याय (*sakhyāya*)).
- आगच्छतं (*āgacchataṃ*)—be so kind as to come

O Indra and Agni, be so kind as to come facing us with herds of cows, troops of horses and abundant riches. We pray and invoke you, Indra and Agni, who are friends, divine in nature, bringers of happiness and renowned, for the gaining of friendship.
Come to us with herds of cattle, with troops of horses, with ample treasures, divine friends, Indra and Agni : givers of happiness, we invoke you as such for your friendship.

O Indra and Agni, hear the invocation (हवं (*havaṃ*)), the praise, of the sacrificer who is pressing (सुन्वतः (*sunvataḥ*)) the Soma. Having heard, desire (वीतं (*vītaṃ*)) his oblations. Having desired them, come (आ गतं (*ā gataṃ*)). And having come, drink (पिबतं (*pibataṃ*)) the sweet Soma (मधु (*madhu*)).
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—the praise in the form of an invocation
- आ गतं (*ā gataṃ*)—be so kind as to come to receive them

O Indra and Agni, hear the praise in the form of an invocation of the sacrificer who presses the Soma juice. Desire the oblations offered by him and be so kind as to come to receive them. Drink the sweet juice consisting of Soma.
Hear, Indra and Agni, the invocation of the institutor of the rite as he offers the libation : partake of the offering : come, quaff the sweet Soma beverage.

This Sarasvatī gave (अददात् (*adadāt*)) to the sacrificer Vadhryaśva, who had given oblations (दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)), a son named Divodāsa, swift (रभसं (*rabhasaṃ*)), a liberator from debt (ऋणच्युतं (*ṛṇacyutaṃ*)), that is, one who frees from the Vedic debt owed to the gods, seers and fathers and from the worldly debt. She is the Sarasvatī who struck down (आचखाद (*ācakhāda*)) the numerous Paṇi, a trader by nature, a man who gives nothing to others, an Avasa, one who gratifies only himself. The construction is: that same Sarasvatī gave. Then, making her present, he praises her: O goddess Sarasvatī, those gifts of yours, such as the giving of a son, are great (तविषा (*taviṣā*)).
- अवसं (*avasaṃ*)—who thought only of his own welfare
- पणिं (*paṇiṃ*)—and was a miser, the Asura
- ऋणच्युतं (*ṛṇacyutaṃ*)—who discharges the debts to gods, seers and fathers
- ता (*tā*)—the gift of a son given by you
- दात्राणि (*dātrāṇi*)—and the gifts of wealth and the like

The Sarasvatī who destroyed the Asura who greatly thought only of his own welfare and was selfish and extremely miserly, that same Sarasvatī has given a son named Divodāsa, swift and a discharger of the debts to gods and fathers, to the seer named Vadhryaśva, who offers oblations. O Sarasvatī, the gift of a son and the gift of wealth that are favoured by you bear great fruit.

She gave to the donor of the oblations, Vadhryaswa, a son, Divodasa endowed with speed, and acquitting the debt (due to gods and progenitors); she who destroyed the churlish niggard, (thinking) only of himself : such are your great bounties, Saraswati.

Sarasvatī exists both in the form of a deity and in the form of a river. In the form of a deity she has been praised; now with this ṛk he praises Sarasvatī in the form of a river. This river-form Sarasvatī, with her own strengths that dry things up (शुष्मैः (*śuṣmaiḥ*)), with great (तविषेभिः (*taviṣebhiḥ*)) waves (ऊर्मिभिः (*ūrmibhiḥ*)), breaks (अरुजत् (*arujat*)) the peaks (सानु (*sānu*)) of the mountains that adjoin her banks, like (बिसखा इव (*bisakhā iva*)) a digger of lotus fibre: as he breaks the mud for the sake of the fibre, so she. Her, the Pārāvataghnī, the destroyer even of a tree and the like that stands in a distant place, we serve (आ विवासेम (*ā vivāsema*)) with praises (सुवृक्तिभिः (*suvṛktibhiḥ*)) and with rites (धीतिभिः (*dhītibhiḥ*)) for protection (अवसे (*avase*)). Or else: पारावतघ्नीं (*pārāvataghnīṃ*) means the destroyer of both banks, the far and the near. And it is said: पारावतघ्नीं पारावारघातिनीं (*pārāvataghnīṃ pārāvāraghātinīṃ*) (Ni. 2-24). **GLOSS**
- इयं (*iyaṃ*)—this goddess Sarasvatī in the form of a river
- बिसखा इव (*bisakhā iva*)—easily, as one digs mud for the lotus stalk
- पारावतघ्नीं (*pārāvataghnīṃ*)—who brings down trees and the like (or banks) that are in a distant place

This goddess Sarasvatī in the form of a river easily breaks through the lofty places of the mountains with her powerful and great waves, as one digs mud for the lotus stalk. Let us worship, for protection, with excellent praises and with excellent rites, this goddess Sarasvatī, who brings down trees and the like and the banks that are in a distant place.

With impetuous and mighty waves she breaks down the precipices of the mountains, like a digger for the lotus fibres : we adore for our protection, with praises and with sacred rites, Saraswati the underminer of both her banks.

For this ṛk Yāska has given an etymology: इयं शुष्मैः शोषणैः । शुष्ममिति बलनाम शोषयतीति सतः । बिसं बिस्मतेर्भेदनकर्मणो वृद्धिकर्मणो वा । सानु समुच्च्रितं भवति समुन्नु- (*iyaṃ śuṣmaiḥ śoṣaṇaiḥ | śuṣmamiti balanāma śoṣayatīti sataḥ | bisaṃ bismaterbhedanakarmaṇo vṛddhikarmaṇo vā | sānu samuccritaṃ bhavati samunnu-*) **GLOSS**

न्नमिति वा । महद्भिरूर्मिभिः पारावतघ्नीं पारावारघातिनीं । पारं परं भवति । अवारमवरं । अवनाय सुप्रवृत्ताभिः शोभनाभिः स्तुतिभिः सरस्वतीं नदीं कर्मभिः परिचरेम ॥ (*nnamiti vā | mahadbhirūrmibhiḥ pārāvataghnīṃ pārāvāraghātinīṃ | pāraṃ paraṃ bhavati | avāramavaraṃ | avanāya supravṛttābhiḥ śobhanābhiḥ stutibhiḥ sarasvatīṃ nadīṃ karmabhiḥ paricarema ‖*) (Ni. 2-24)

"Śuṣka" means strength. For the word शुष्क (*śuṣka*) is formed from the root शोषयति (*śoṣayati*), which has the sense of pressing down; since it presses down everything by its own strength, the sense "strength" has become established for the word.⟨NOTE:162⟩

बिसं (*bisaṃ*) means lotus stalk. This word is formed from the root बिस्कृति (*biskṛti*), which has the sense of cutting, breaking into pieces, or growing. The word सानु (*sānu*) means a high place, an elevated place, a summit. This river Sarasvatī, with her huge, that is, great waves, breaks away and destroys her two banks, as one easily cuts through the tender lotus stalk. That is, because of the current of the river the two banks collapse and fall and become mingled with the water of the river. पारं (*pāraṃ*) means that which is different (परं (*paraṃ*)) or that which is far away. अवरं (*avaraṃ*) means that which is near. पारावारं (*pārāvāraṃ*) means the two banks, the one far away (the opposite one) and the one near. The chief purport of the etymology is: let us serve with offerings of worship the river Sarasvatī, flowing between such two banks, for our protection, with well-composed praises recited clearly and with proper accents, or with excellently performed rites of worship and the like.
notes: ಶುಷ್ಕ printed in the Kannada for the ಶುಷ್ಮ of Yāska's text; also ಬಿಸ್ಕೃತಿ for ಬಿಸ್ಮತಿ

en: "O Sarasvatī, you have destroyed the Asuras who revile the gods, and you have slain the offspring of the all-pervading Bṛsaya, the possessor of māyā." Bṛsaya is a name of Tvaṣṭṛ; you slew the offspring of Tvaṣṭṛ, that is, his son, the Asura Vṛtra. The meaning is that Indra slew him with your help. And, O Sarasvatī, possessed of food, you obtained for men the lands carried off by the Asuras, and you caused water to flow for these men. Or else: the Asura peoples are meant by क्षितयो (*kṣitayo*); from them you obtained the lands, you gained them; and having slain them, you caused to flow for these Asuras poison, a deadly venom, the cause of death.
- देवनिदः (*devanidaḥ*)—the Asuras who revile the gods
- मायिनः (*māyinaḥ*)—of the one endowed with power
- प्रजां (*prajāṃ*)—you have also slain the son, Vṛtra
- अवनीः (*avanīḥ*)—the lands carried off by the Asuras

O goddess Sarasvatī, you have destroyed the Asuras who revile the gods. You have slain Vṛtra, the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, who is all-pervading and endowed with power; and, O Sarasvatī, endowed with food, you have provided again to men the lands carried off by the Asuras. For these very men you have caused water to flow.

Destory, Saraswati the revilers of the gods, the offspring of the universal deluder, Vrisaya : giver of sustenance, you have acquired for men the lands (seized by the Asuras), and have showered water upon them.

"Devī" means she who is endowed with qualities such as generosity. वाजिनीवती (*vājinīvatī*): vāja is food; the rite in which there is food is vājinī; she is endowed with that. धीनां (*dhīnāṃ*) means of the meditators, that is, of the worshippers; अवित्री (*avitrī*) means the protectress. May Sarasvatī, so characterised, protect us with वाजेभिः (*vājebhiḥ*), that is, with foods; may she satisfy us abundantly.
- प्र अवतु (*pra avatu*)—may she protect fully, or may she satisfy
May Sarasvatī, who is divine, endowed with food, and the protectress of the worshippers, protect us with foods; may she fully satisfy us.
May the divine Saraswati, the acceptress of (sacrificial) food, the protectress of her worshippers, sustain as with (abundant) viands.
"O goddess Sarasvatī, the worshipper who, in the battle for wealth, wealth being the occasion, praises you as one praises Indra, him protect": thus the sentence is to be completed.
- धने हिते (*dhane hite*)—for the sake of wealth
- इंद्रं न (*iṃdraṃ na*)—as one praises Indra
- त्वा उपब्रूते (*tvā upabrūte*)—praises you (protect such a worshipper)
O divine Sarasvatī, the worshipper who, in battle, for the sake of wealth, praises you just as he praises Indra, protect such a worshipper.
Divine Saraswati, protect him engaged in conflict for the sake of wealth, who glorifies you like Indra.

"O goddess, endowed with qualities such as generosity; O वाजिनि (*vājini*)": vāja is strength or food, and she is endowed with that. "O Sarasvatī, protect us in the वाजेषु (*vājeṣu*), that is, in battles. And, like Pūṣan, the nourishing god, रद (*rada*) for us the wealth that is to be shared": रद (*rada*) means विलिख (*vilikha*), that is, bestow.
- देवि (*devi*)—O one endowed with qualities such as generosity
O Sarasvatī, endowed with qualities such as generosity and endowed with power, protect us in battles. Like Pūṣan, the nourishing god, provide us with wealth fit to be enjoyed.
Divine Saraswati, abounding in food, protect us in combat, and, like Pushan, give us gifts.

And that well-known Sarasvatī is fierce, causing fear to enemies, and हिरण्यवर्तनिः (*hiraṇyavartaniḥ*): वर्तनी (*vartanī*) is that by which one goes, a chariot; she whose chariot is of gold is so called. She is वृत्रघ्नी (*vṛtraghnī*), the slayer of the वृत्राणां (*vṛtrāṇāṃ*), that is, of enemies. May Sarasvatī, so characterised, desire and welcome our beautiful praise.
- हिरण्यवर्तनिः (*hiraṇyavartaniḥ*)—possessed of a chariot made of gold
May the goddess Sarasvatī, the well-known, terrible to enemies, possessed of a chariot made of gold, the destroyer of enemies, desire our excellent praise.
May the fierce Saraswati, ridiing in a golden chariot, the destructress of enemies, be pleased by our earnest laudation.

Of that Sarasvatī whose might (अमः (*amaḥ*), strength) is endless, that is, without limit and unmeasured, unharmed or not crooked, radiant (त्वेषः (*tveṣaḥ*) means shining), and चरिष्णुः (*cariṣṇuḥ*), of a moving nature; that is, its course is unobstructed everywhere. It is अर्णवः (*arṇavaḥ*), possessed of water, that is, a giver of water. Being so, it moves, makes a great sound. The connection is with the following "sā no viśvā" of the next verse.
- चरति (*carati*)—moves (may that might protect us from enemies)
May that might of Sarasvatī, which moves, immeasurable, unharmed by enemies, radiant, going everywhere, full of water and making a great sound, protect us from enemies.
May she whose might, infinite, undeviating, splendid, progressive, water-shedding, proceed, loud-sounding.

May that Sarasvatī lead us across all the द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*), the hating, that is, hostile, peoples; may she carry us beyond. Likewise may she carry us beyond the other rivers, the self-flowing or co-born ones that are ऋतावरीः (*ṛtāvarīḥ*); ऋत (*ṛta*) is a name for water, and they are endowed with it. Or else: may the water-bearing sisters, the other rivers, the Gaṅgā and the rest, carry us beyond the enemies. Here is an illustration: the sun, the impeller of all, the Āditya, constantly moving, as he swiftly leads the days across, so may they do.⟨NOTE:163⟩
notes: ಸಂಹಿತಾ ಸ್ವಸ್ವರನ್ಯಾ, ಪದಪಾಠ ಸ್ವಸ್ಥಾಃ, ಭಾಷ್ಯ ಸ್ವಸ್ಯಃ differ; ಪದಪಾಠ ಋಶವರೀ for ಋತಾವರೀ; ಭಗಿನ್ನೋ in bhāṣya

en: - सा (*sā*)—Sarasvatī, endowed with the qualities stated above
- अति नयतु (*ati nayatu*)—may she carry across
- अहेव (*aheva*)—as he swiftly brings the day to an end
- अति नयतु (*ati nayatu*)—may they bring the enemies to an end

May Sarasvatī, endowed with the qualities stated above, carry us across all the hostile peoples. As the sun, moving swiftly, swiftly brings the day to an end, may the other river-goddesses too, those flowing of themselves (or the sisters of the river Sarasvatī) and endowed with water, bring our enemies to an end.
Overcome all our adversaries, and bring to us her other water-laden sisters, as the ever-rolling sun (leads on) the days.

In the Daśarāta rite, on the third day, in the Praūga, the tṛca beginning उत नः प्रिया (*uta naḥ priyā*) is the Sārasvata. It is laid down in the Sūtra: उत नः प्रिया प्रियास्वित्यौष्ठिहं प्रउगं (*uta naḥ priyā priyāsvityauṣṭhihaṃ praugaṃ*) (Ā. 7-10). In the Pavitreṣṭi the ṛk beginning उत नः प्रिया (*uta naḥ priyā*) is the anuvākyā of the oblation addressed to Sarasvatī. It is laid down: उत नः प्रिया प्रियास्तिमा जुह्वाना युष्मदा नमोभिः (*uta naḥ priyā priyāstimā juhvānā yuṣmadā namobhiḥ*) (Ā. 2-12). Further: among those who are dear to us, she is the dearest; she is सप्तस्वसा (*saptasvasā*), one whose sisters are the seven metres beginning with Gāyatrī; but as a river, her sisters are the seven rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā. She is सुजुष्णा (*sujuṣṇā*), well served by the ancient seers. May the goddess Sarasvatī, so characterised, be worthy of praise.
- सप्तस्वसा (*saptasvasā*)—she who has seven sisters, the Gaṅgā and the rest
May the river Sarasvatī, who is the object of the greatest love among all those dear to us, who has seven sisters beginning with the Gaṅgā, and who is served by the seers, be worthy of our praise.
May Saraswati, who has seven sisters, who is dearest amongst those dear to us, and is fully propitiated be ever adorable.

On the third day of the sacrifice called Daśarātra, when the Praūga śastra mantras are recited, the three ṛks beginning उत नः प्रिया (*uta naḥ priyā*) (ṛks 10-12 of this sūkta) are to be recited as a tṛca addressed to the deity Sarasvatī; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, उत नः प्रिया प्रियास्वित्वा हं प्रउगं (*uta naḥ priyā priyāsvitvā haṃ praugaṃ*) (Ā. 7-10). And in the Pavitreṣṭi, this ṛk beginning उत नः प्रिया (*uta naḥ priyā*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra in the oblation offered to the deity Sarasvatī; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, उत नः प्रिया प्रियास्विमा जुह्वाना युष्मदा नमोभिः (*uta naḥ priyā priyāsvimā juhvānā yuṣmadā namobhiḥ*) (Ā. 2-12).

Here the word सप्तस्वसा (*saptasvasā*) must be explained in two ways. When Sarasvatī is praised as the goddess of speech, सप्तस्वसा (*saptasvasā*), "having seven sisters," means the seven metres beginning with Gāyatrī; when she is praised as a river, it means the seven rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā.
The goddess Sarasvatī, having filled with her own radiance the earthly worlds, vast and extensive, and the sky, the space bounded in between, may protect us from the reviling enemy.
- पार्थिवानि (*pārthivāni*)—belonging to the world of the earth
- आ पप्रुषी (*ā papruṣī*)—she who has pervaded
May the goddess Sarasvatī, who has pervaded the vast worlds belonging to the earth and the sky, protect us from the enemies who revile.
May Saraswati, filling (with radiance) the vast expanse of earth and heaven, defend us from the reviler.

त्रिषधस्था (*triṣadhasthā*): abiding together in the three worlds, that is, pervading the three worlds. सप्तधातुः (*saptadhātuḥ*): she whose seven constituents, the metres beginning with Gāyatrī or the rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā, are her members. पंच जाता (*paṃca jātā*): the five born ones, the four varṇas together with the Niṣāda as the fifth, or the Gandharvas and the rest; वर्धयंती (*vardhayaṃtī*): making them grow. May Sarasvatī, so characterised, be to be invoked in every battle, in every conflict.
- त्रिषधस्था (*triṣadhasthā*)—she who pervades the three worlds
- सप्तधातुः (*saptadhātuḥ*)—she who has seven constituents, the Gaṅgā and the rest
- पंच जाता (*paṃca jātā*)—the people born in five ways, beginning with the Niṣādas
- हव्या भूत् (*havyā bhūt*)—she becomes worthy of our invocation and praise

Sarasvatī, who pervades the three worlds, who has seven constituents beginning with the Gaṅgā, and who nourishes the people born in five ways beginning with the Niṣādas, becomes in every battle worthy of our invocation and praise.
Abiding in the three worlds, comprising seven elements, cherishing the five races (of beings), she is ever to be invoked in battle.

She who by her majesty, her greatness, is great, endowed with splendid glories or foods, is pre-eminently known among these rivers or deities. And she who, among the other swift rivers, is the most swift; and she who, like a chariot, for the sake of all-pervasiveness is made great, pre-eminent, superior in qualities, created by Prajāpati: that Sarasvatī is to be approached with praise by the singer of praise who knows.
- अन्याः अपसां (*anyāḥ apasāṃ*)—among the other rivers with currents
- अपस्तमा (*apastamā*)—the one with the most exceedingly swift current
- चिकितुषा (*cikituṣā*)—worthy of the knowledge of the singer of praise

The goddess Sarasvatī who by her greatness has a great form and is endowed with radiant food, who is known pre-eminently among these river-goddesses, who among the other rivers with currents has the most exceedingly swift current, and who, growing great so as to be all-pervading, has been created by Prajāpati as a chariot is made: she is worthy of the knowledge of the singer of praise and worthy of his praise.

She who is distinguished amongst them as eminent in greatness and in her glories ; she who is the most impetuous of all other streams : she who has been created vast in capacity as a chariot, she Saraswati, is to be glorified by the discreet (worshipper).⟨NOTE:164⟩
notes: ಋಕ್ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ೧೬ printed after the Saṃhitā; ೧೩ in the Padapāṭha

en: O Sarasvatī, lead us to the most excellent wealth. Do not make us unprosperous; the verb that means to grow is here used in the opposite sense under the force of the prefix. Likewise do not burn us, do not oppress us, with excess of water. And accept our friendships, the acts of friends, and the entrances; and may we not go from you to the unpleasant, low fields; may we not reach them; rather, may we reach only pleasant ones.
- माप स्फरीः (*māpa spharīḥ*)—do not obstruct our growth
- पयसा (*payasā*)—with the irresistible flood of water
- मा आ धक् (*mā ā dhak*)—do not harm
- मा गन्म (*mā ganma*)—may we not reach

O goddess Sarasvatī, provide us with praiseworthy wealth. Do not obstruct our growth. Do not harm us with an irresistible flood of water. Accept our friendship and our dwellings. May we not come to fields joyless to you; or, do not make us receive joyless fields from you.

Guide us, Saraswati, to precious wealth ; reduce us not to insignificance ; overwhelm us not with (excess of) water ; be pleased by our friendly (services) and access to our habitations, and let us not repair to places unacceptable to you.
वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ (*vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖*) **GLOSS**

इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराज परमेश्वर वैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तक श्री वीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये चतुर्थाष्टके ऽष्टमोऽध्यायः समाप्तः ॥ (*iti śrīmadrājādhirāja parameśvara vaidikamārgapravartaka śrī vīrabukkabhūpālasāmrājyadhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇācāryeṇa viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe ṛksaṃhitābhāṣye caturthāṣṭake 'ṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ ‖*) **GLOSS**
Here ends the eighth adhyāya, in the fourth aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, together with Śrī Sāyaṇa's bhāṣya and the Kannada translation.
यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्ववेत् । तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोस्तुते ॥ (*yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ tu yadvavet | tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namostute ‖*) **GLOSS**
वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे । यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननं । (*vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānāmupakrame | yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanaṃ |*) **GLOSS**
यस्य निश्वसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् । निर्ममे तमहं वंदे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरं । (*yasya niśvasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat | nirmame tamahaṃ vaṃde vidyātīrthamaheśvaraṃ |*) **GLOSS**
वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्यायी सदाशिवः । तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥ (*vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyī sadāśivaḥ | tasmātsarvaprayatnena vedameva sadā japet ‖*) **GLOSS**
Ṛgveda-saṃhitā with Sāyaṇa's bhāṣya (with the Kannada translation and explanation).
The first adhyāya in the fifth aṣṭaka. The sixty-second sūkta of the sixth maṇḍala.

"I praise the Aśvins, the two leaders of the world of heaven and the two lords, the rulers, of this world, accompanied by horses; singing their praise with stotras accomplished by sung mantras and with śastras accomplished by mantras recited for worship, I call them." Of what sort? They who are immediately उस्रा (*usrā*), warders-off of enemies; who at dawn, at the end of the night, keep separating all round to the ends, the limits, of the earth the vast वरांसि (*varāṃsi*), the darknesses that hinder form. Or else: the वरांसि (*varāṃsi*) are splendours, and they spread them out all round by removing the darkness.⟨NOTE:166⟩
notes: ಪದಪಾಠ closes the Ṛk with ೫೨ for ೧

en: - सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*)—as soon as it is willed
- उस्रा (*usrā*)—who are warders-off of enemies, and
- युयूषतः (*yuyūṣataḥ*)—who separate and drive far away, such ones

Praising with venerable mantras the Aśvin deities, who have the power to destroy enemies as soon as it is willed, who at the time of dawn destroy in all places the pitch-dark glooms that cover the earth all around, who are the leaders of the world of heaven and the lords of the earth, I call them.

I praise the two leaders of heaven, the presiders over this world : I invoke the Aswins, glorifying them with sacred hymns, them who are ever the discomfiters (of foes), who at dawn scatter the investing glooms to the ends of the earth.

Further, those well-known Aśvins, coming to our sacrifice with their own pure splendours (रजोभिः (*rajobhiḥ*)), make the lustre of their own chariot shine; for Yāska has said: रजो रजतेर्जोती रज उच्यते (*rajo rajaterjotī raja ucyate*) (Ni. 4-19) **GLOSS**. And creating many, immeasurable splendours that remove darkness, they drive their own horses, for the sake of water, over the desert regions.

The well-known Aśvin deities, coming to our sacrifice, increase the lustre of their chariot with their pure splendours. Creating immeasurably abundant splendours that remove darkness, they drive their horses, for the sake of water, throughout the deserts.
Coming to the sacrifice with their bright splendours, they light up the lustre of (their) car; emitting vast and infinite radiance: they drive their horses over deserts (refreshing them) with water.

You two, indeed, fierce Aśvins, go to the house of the sacrificer which is अरध्रं (*aradhraṃ*), unprosperous, in order to make it prosperous. And in this manner you always carry, that is, bring to heaven, the धियः (*dhiyaḥ*), the praisers, with your own desirable horses, swift as the mind.⟨NOTE:167⟩ May the harmer of the mortal man, the sacrificer who offers, be brought by you to lie down all round, to long sleep.
notes: ಭಾಷ್ಯ ಸ್ತೋತ್ಯನ್ read as the praisers; the Kannada gives ಕರ್ಮಕರ್ತರಾದ ಯಜಮಾನರನ್ನು, the sacrificers who perform the rites

en: - ता ह (*tā ha*)—(O Aśvin deities) the well-known ones
- उग्रा (*ugrā*)—you who have a terrible power
- यत् वर्तिः (*yat vartiḥ*)—to the house of which sacrificer (you come to make it prosperous)
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—the sacrificers who perform the rites
- व्यथिः (*vyathiḥ*)—the enemy who is a harmer
- परिशयध्यॆ (*pariśayadhyè*)—may he be thrown down to sleep long

O Aśvin deities, well-known and possessed of a terrible power, from whichever house lacking prosperity you come to fill it with wealth, from that same house, with that same pride, with the help of attractive horses swift as the mind, you always carry the sacrificers who perform the rites to heaven. May the harming enemy of the sacrificer, the man who offers the oblation, be dead and thrown down to sleep long.

Fierce Aswins, from that humble mansion to which (you have repaired), you have ever borne with your desirable horses, as swift as thought, the pious worshippers in some manner (to heaven) : Let the injurer of the liberal man (be consigned by you) to (final) repose.

Those Aśvins, harnessed to the chariot with horses (युयुजानसप्ति (*yuyujānasapti*)), bearing beautiful food (पयः पृक्ष (*payaḥ pṛkṣa*): pṛkṣa is read among the names of food), nourishment and sap, approach the stotra, the mantra to be pondered, of the newer praiser; or else they are near the stotra. And further, may the invoker of the gods, Agni, who is non-hostile, dear, ancient, old, sacrifice to those two ever-young ones.
- युयुजानसप्ति (*yuyujānasapti*)—having yoked their horses to the chariot
- होता (*hotā*)—he who calls the deities to the sacrifice

The Aśvin deities, having yoked horses to their chariot and having filled themselves with excellent and auspicious food, nourishment, and sap that gives strength, come towards the meditative praise of the new praiser. May Agni, who calls the ever-young Aśvin deities to the sacrifice, the beloved one (who has no treacherous mind), the ancient, worship them.

Harnessing their horses, bringing excellent food, nourishment, and strength, they approach (to receive) the adoration of their recent worshipper ; and may the benevolent ancient inquirer of the gods (Agni) sacrifice to the ever youthful (deities).

They who for the one who praises with śastras, and for the one who praises with stotras, are शंभविष्ठा (*śaṃbhaviṣṭhā*), causers of the greatest happiness or of the nature of the greatest happiness for the man; and who have become givers of wondrous gifts to the one who praises with worldly praises: those two, वल्लू (*vallū*), charming, lovely, पुरुषाकतमा (*puruṣākatamā*), of the greatest many deeds or of many helpers, प्रत्ना (*pratnā*), ancient (प्रश्नं प्रदिव (*praśnaṃ pradiva*) are read among the names of the ancient), दस्रा (*dasrā*), the Aśvins lovely to behold, I serve with a newer speech, a praise.
- गृणते (*gṛṇate*)—to the one who praises with worldly words of praise
- चित्रराती (*citrarātī*)—who give gifts of many kinds
- पुरुशाकतमा (*puruśākatamā*)—who are doers of the greatest deeds
- दस्रा (*dasrā*)—who have attractive beauty, the Aśvin deities

I serve with a new praise the Aśvin deities, who give the greatest happiness to the extoller and to the praiser who praises with śastra mantras and the like, and who give gifts of many kinds to him who praises with worldly words of praise, who have a charming form, who are doers of the greatest deeds, who are ancient and who have attractive beauty.

I worship with a new hymn those two quick-moving good-loooking ancient (Aswins), the achievers of many exploits, who are the givers of great felicity to him who prays to (them); or praises (them); bestowers of wondrous gifts on him who adores (them).

You two Aśvins, protecting Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, whose ship was broken in the middle of the sea, brought him out of the lap of the water, from the ocean, from the waters: by horses that fly, that is, that move like birds, yoked to the chariot, through the aerial paths (रजोभिः (*rajobhiḥ*)) that are free from dust. The expression "from the ocean, from the waters" is like saying "he goes from the house of his mother".
- ता (*tā*)—(O Aśvin deities) you well-known ones
- रजोभिः (*rajobhiḥ*)—that move along the aerial paths
- योजनेभिः (*yojanebhiḥ*)—that are yoked to the chariot
- पतत्रिभिः (*patatribhiḥ*)—that run with the speed of birds
- समुद्रात् अद्भ्यः (*samudrāt adbhyaḥ*)—from the deep water of the ocean
- नि ऊहथुः (*ni ūhathuḥ*)—you lifted him up

O Aśvin deities, you well-known ones, by the help of horses that move along the dust-free aerial paths, that are yoked to the chariot and that run with the speed of birds, protecting Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, you lifted him up out of the midst of the water of the very deep ocean.

They bore up from the waters, from the ocean, by the winged horses attached to their car, (passing) by roads unsoiled by dust, Bhujyu, the son of Tugra ; they (bore him) from out of the lap of the water.

We have explained the matter that the Aśvin deities rescued Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, in the midst of the ocean, in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 8, p. 812, and in Part 9-194, 9-369, 9-467, 13-523, 13-616, and other places.

O charioteers, Aśvins riding in the chariot, with your victorious chariot you pierced the mountain standing in the way; the root meaning "to go" has here the sense of striking. So also another passage of the Veda: विभिंदुना नासत्या रथेन वि पर्वता अजरयू आयातं । (*vibhiṃdunā nāsatyā rathena vi parvatā ajarayū āyātaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-20)⟨NOTE:168⟩ **GLOSS**. O showerers of desires, you heard the call of Vadhrimatī, who desired a son. Granting desires to the praisers, you filled with milk the cow for Śayu who praises you, her calving having ceased. So also another passage: शयवे चिन्नासत्या शचीभिर्जसुरये स्तर्यं पिप्यथुर्गा० । (*śayave cinnāsatyā śacībhirjasuraye staryaṃ pipyathurgā0 |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-22) **GLOSS**. Thus going with सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*), good praise, be you भुरण्यू (*bhuraṇyū*), goers everywhere or supporters of the sacrifice.⟨NOTE:169⟩
notes: abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ. printed
ಸುಮತಿಂ: ಭಾಷ್ಯ ಸುಷ್ಟುತಿಂ "good praise"; the Kannada gives ಅನುಗ್ರಹ ಬುದ್ಧಿಯನ್ನು "benevolent mind"

en: - रथ्या (*rathyā*)—O Aśvin deities, riders in the chariot
- जयुषा (*jayuṣā*)—with the help of your victorious chariot
- अद्रिं (*adriṃ*)—the mountain that stood in the middle of the road
- वि यातं (*vi yātaṃ*)—you pierced and entered
- वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*)—O Aśvin deities, showerers of desires
- वध्रिमत्याः (*vadhrimatyāḥ*)—of Vadhrimatī, who desired a son
- दशस्यंता (*daśasyaṃtā*)—granting to the praisers what they desire
- गां (*gāṃ*)—the cow that did not bear a calf

O Aśvin deities, riders in the chariot, with the help of your victorious chariot you pierced and entered the mountain that stood in the middle of the road. O Aśvin deities, showerers of desires, you heard the call of Vadhrimatī, who desired a son. Granting to the praisers what they desire, you filled with milk the cow that did not bear a calf, for Śayu the praiser. In this very manner, displaying a benevolent mind, be goers to every sacrifice.

Riders in your car, you have penetrated the mountain by your trimphant chariot : showerers (of benefits) you heard the invocation of Vadhrimati : you have nourished, bountiful givers, the cow for Sayu— and in this manner displaying benevolence are you everywhere present.
The matter of the bestowal of a son named Hiraṇyahasta on the woman named Vadhrimatī is in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 9, pp. 252 and 408; and the barren cow of the sage named Śayu was made to bear a calf and give
milk is explained in Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-736, 9-294, 9-440, 13-509 (part and pages).

Sāyaṇa takes the vocatives in order: Heaven and Earth, the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Maruts, who are the sons of Rudra. Among mortals, that is, among the attendants (worshippers) of the Aśvins, there is a great wrath of the gods. He explains that this wrath is scorching, burning. Make that scorching wrath a striking harm (a smiting calamity) for the one who is joined with Rākṣasas, that is, for the lord of the Rākṣasas, their instigator. "Make" is the sense of the verb dadhāta. Or else: make a striking harm for the sacrificer who is joined with Rākṣasas.
- रुद्रियासः (*rudriyāsaḥ*)—O Maruts, the sons of Rudra
- मर्त्यत्रा (*martyatrā*)—upon the men who worship the Aśvin deities
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—that which is directed by the gods
- रक्षोयुजे (*rakṣoyuje*)—to the man who is united with Rākṣasas
O Heaven and Earth, O Ādityas, O gods called Vasus, O Maruts, sons of Rudra: upon the men who worship the Aśvin deities, from the atmosphere, that wrath which is directed by the gods
and endowed with exceeding power, which there is, that scorching same wrath make so as to become the destroyer of the man who is united with Rākṣasas.
Heaven and Earth, Adityas, Vasus, Maruts, render that dread anger of the gods which (has) of old (been directed) against mortals, destructive and fatal to him who is associated with the Rakshasas.

The man who in due season serves the two Aśvins, who are the lords of the whole world (Sāyaṇa adds that Yāska says the worlds are called rajāṃsi), him Mitra and Varuṇa know: that is, Mitra, Varuṇa and the other gods know him. Moreover this attendant hurls his weapon, a destructive arm, at the deep, that is, mighty, rakṣas, the Rākṣasa; and at malicious speech of man, speech that relates to men and is aimed at injury, he hurls his weapon as though by speech itself, for he attacks it to the injury of men.⟨NOTE:170⟩
notes: ವಚಸೇ ಚಿತ್ ವಚನಾಯ್ಕೆವ ಹೇತಿಮಸ್ಯತಿ । ಮನುಷ್ಯಾಣಾಮಭಿದ್ರೋಹಾಯ್ಕೆನಮಾಸ್ಕಂದತೀತಿ — machine-read text damaged (ವಚನಾಯ್ಕೆವ, ಅಭಿದ್ರೋಹಾಯ್ಕೆನಂ); sense of the last two sentences uncertain

en: - ऋतुथा (*ṛtuthā*)—in accordance with the respective times of sacrifice
- वचसे चित् (*vacase cit*)—even upon reviling words he can hurl it

The man who worships in accordance with the respective times of sacrifice these Aśvin deities, the lords of the whole world, him Mitra and Varuṇa know well. This same worshipper can hurl a destructive weapon upon the asura of exceeding strength. He can hurl it also upon the reviling words employed by the man who practises treachery.
Mitra and Varuna recognize him who of all the world worships the royal (Asvins) in due season; he hurls his weapon against the strong Rakshasa, against the malignant menaces of man.

O Aśvins, come to our house, to give a son, with a chariot that has excellent wheels, wheels that are not inferior, that is shining, and that has a leader, that is, a charioteer; or else a chariot that is yoked with horses, because पतंगा नर (*pataṃgā nara*) is read among the names of the horse. Moreover, with the wrath that is helpful to the head, wrath being the meaning of the word tyajas (because हृणिस्तेज (*hṛṇisteja*) is read among the names of wrath), cut off the heads of those who afflict the mortal, the man who worships you. Sāyaṇa adds that Yāska says the verb vanuṣyati is a verb of killing. The word vavṛktam means "cut off".
- तनयायु (*tanayāyu*)—for the gift of a son
- आ यातं (*ā yātaṃ*)—be gracious to come
- मर्त्यस्य (*martyasya*)—for the man who worships you
- वनुष्यतां (*vanuṣyatāṃ*)—of the asuras who do harm

O Aśvin deities, come to our sacrificial house with a chariot endowed with excellent wheels, radiant, and endowed with an excellent charioteer, and grant us the gift of a son. Cut off, with the anger that stays hidden and is not shown outwardly, the heads of the asuras who do harm to the man who worships you.

Come with your shining and well-guided chariot, (fitted) with excellent wheels, to our dwelling, (to bestow upon us) male offspring : cut off with secret indignation the heads of those obstructing (the adoration)) of the mortal (who worships you).

O Aśvins, come toward us with the best draught-teams, and also with the middling and the inferior ones. Sāyaṇa then begins to speak of the firmly fixed, the sentence continuing in the next part of the text.⟨NOTE:171⟩
Open the doors of the cow-pen, the stall that has cows, even though it is firm. Moreover, be givers of various gifts to me, the praiser.
notes: ದೃಳ್ಹಸ್ಯ ಚಿದ್ದೃಳ್ಹಾ ವಿಧಾನಸ್ಯಾಪಿ — the block breaks off at the page end; ದೃಳ್ಹಾ ವಿಧಾನಸ್ಯ unclear

en: - परमाभिः (*paramābhiḥ*)—(O Aśvin deities) the most excellent
- आ यातं (*ā yātaṃ*)—be gracious to come
- दृळस्य चित् (*dṛḷasya cit*)—even though very firm
- चित्रराशी (*citrarāśī*)—be givers of many kinds of gifts

O Aśvin deities, be gracious to come facing us with steeds, the most excellent, the middling and the very inferior. Open the doors of the cow-pen that has cows, even though it is very firm. Grant many kinds of gifts to me, the praiser.
Come down, whether with the most excellent, or middling, or inferior Niyut steeds; set open the doors of the fast-shut stall of the cattle : be bountiful to him who praises you.

Where, in what place, are those two Aśvins, lovely and called by many? The stoma, such as the Pañcadaśa, joined with an offering, has found them today like a sent messenger; Sāyaṇa glosses namasvān as joined with an offering, since नम अयुरित्यन्ननामसु (*nama ayurityannanāmasu*) — nama and ayu are read among the names of food. The stoma that turns the Nāsatyas, the Aśvins, toward us: O Aśvins, you are the dearest to this praiser's praise; asathaḥ means "you are".⟨NOTE:174⟩
notes: ವಲ್ಲೂ ರುಚಿರ್ — gloss of valgū ends in a broken form ರುಚಿರ್; ವಿಂದೇಶ್ also broken

en: - आ ववर्त (*ā vavarta*)—is able to turn; such
- स्तोमः (*stomaḥ*)—the stoma such as the Pañcadaśa
- दूतो न (*dūto na*)—like a messenger sent to seek them
- अस्य (*asya*)—(O Aśvin deities) of this praiser
- मन्मन् (*manman*)—in the matter of the praise
- प्रेष्णा हि (*preṣṇā hi*)—as the most dear

The stoma, such as the Pañcadaśa, which is able to turn the Aśvin deities so that they face us, such a stoma, joined with oblations, like a messenger sent to seek them, is able at this time to find out in what place those Aśvin deities are, who are of lovely form, called by many, and renowned. O Aśvin deities, be most loving in the matter of the praise of this praiser.

Where may our praise and oblations find to-day, for a messenger, those two splendid (Aswins), the invoked of many, and bring the Nasatyas to our presence? Be propitiated (Aswins) by the adoration of this (your worshipper).

O Aśvins, come in full measure to this my invocation, that is, to my call; being praised, drink the Soma, the andhas, in the manner in which you drink it. Go round on all sides that house of mine for the sake of the harming enemy, so that neither a far-off enemy nor one who is near may do it harm.

Or else: go round that house of ours, to protect it against the harming enemy; let neither the one who is far off nor the one who is near injure it. This is the sense: as neither one who is far away nor one who is near may harm our house, so give it protection.
- गृणाना (*gṛṇānā*)—(O Aśvin deities) you who are to be praised
- परः (*paraḥ*)—the enemy who is at a distance
- त्यत् वर्तिः (*tyat vartiḥ*)—that same house (in the same manner)

O Aśvin deities, you who are worthy of praise: because you drink the Soma juice in the manner you do, be gracious to come in a satisfying manner to this my praise. In the manner in which neither an enemy at a distance nor an enemy near can harm our house, protect it completely from the harming enemy.

Praised, that you may drink the (sacrificial) beverage, you come promptly upon this my invocation: keep guard around the dwelling against (all) adversaries, so that neither one that abides at a distance nor a neighbour may do us harm.

For the two of you, whatever work there is in the extended pressing and the rest of the Soma, the andhas, has been done. The softest sacred grass has been strewn. The hotṛ, with raised and joined hands, desiring you, praises you. The pressing stones, reaching you, have made the Soma manifest on all sides.
- नां (*nāṃ*)—(O Aśvin deities) with you in view
- युवयः (*yuvayaḥ*)—the hotṛ who seeks your presence
- आ आंजन् (*ā āṃjan*)—press out the Soma juice

O Aśvin deities, with you in view the pressing rite of the Soma juice has been performed. The very soft sacred-grass seat is spread widely. The hotṛ, who seeks your presence, praises you with hands raised and joined. For you the extended pressing stones press out the Soma juice.

(What is essential) for the copious effusion of (the sacrificial) food has been done for you : the very delicate sacred grass has been strewn ; the (priest with) uplifted hands desirous of your presence praises you ; the stones-express (the Soma juice), designing it for you.

For the sake of your sacrifice Agni has stood upright. In the sacrifices he goes forth: kindled, he goes to the Āhavanīya. The rāti, wealth, is the oblation, which is forward-moving; Sāyaṇa supports this by Yāska's words जूर्णिर्जवतेर्वा (*jūrṇirjavatervā*) (Ni. 6-4) **GLOSS**. Ghṛtācī means anointed with ghee, that is, sprinkled over what is spread. Moreover, the hotṛ who makes wide ⟨NOTE:175⟩ becomes one whose mind is set on exertion, the hotṛ who yokes the Nāsatyas, the Aśvins, to the invocation, to the praise.
notes: ಹೋತೋರಾಣ ಉರು ಕುರ್ವಾಣಃ — text damaged

en: - प्र एति (*pra eti*)—moves about, going round
- हवीमन् (*havīman*)—with praise in the form of an invocation
- प्र गूर्तमनाः (*pra gūrtamanāḥ*)—and possessed of a mind intent on worship

O Aśvin deities, for your worship Agni stands blazing in a raised place. He moves about, going round in all the sacrificial places. The oblation sprinkled with ghee flows swiftly. The hotṛ who yokes the Aśvin deities with praise in the form of an invocation is possessed of wide devotion and of a mind intent on worship.

Agni is above for you : he is present at (your) sacrifices : the oblation flows diffusive and redolent of ghi : diligent and zealous is the ministrant priest who is engaged, Nasatyas, in your invocation.

O Aśvins, protectors of many, Sūryā, the daughter of Sūrya, has mounted, for refuge, your chariot, which has many protections or many goings. Moreover, at this appearance of the gods worthy of sacrifice, you two, with māyās, that is, acts of wisdom, because शची मायेति प्रज्ञानामसु (*śacī māyeti prajñānāmasu*) is read among the names of wisdom, be wise, leaders, and dancers. Or else: O wise leaders, dancing Aśvins, at this appearance of the gods worthy of sacrifice you have surpassed by your māyās, that is, by wisdom or by skill, the god who is most wise.⟨NOTE:176⟩ Sāyaṇa says this sense is made clear by the passage beginning प्रजापतिर्वै सोमाय राज्ञॆ दुहितरं प्रायच्छत्सूर्यां सावित्रिं । (*prajāpatirvai somāya rājñè duhitaraṃ prāyacchatsūryāṃ sāvitriṃ |*) (Ai. Brā. 4 7) **GLOSS**.
notes: ಪ್ರಾಜ್ಞತಮಮ್ಯಾದಿಕಂ ದೇವಂ — text damaged

en: - पुरुभुजा (*purubhujā*)—O Aśvin deities, who are protectors of many
- अधि तस्थौ (*adhi tasthau*)—has mounted and sits
- मायिना (*māyinā*)—O Aśvin deities, endowed with wisdom
- अत्र जनिमन् (*atra janiman*)—manifested in this sacrifice
- यज्ञियानां (*yajñiyānāṃ*)—among the gods worthy of worship
- नृतू (*nṛtū*)—you yourselves, possessed of exceeding skill⟨NOTE:177⟩
notes: ನೃತೂ glossed as 'skilful'; Sāyaṇa glosses ನೃತ್ಯಂತೌ 'dancing'

en: O Aśvin deities, protectors of many, Sūryā, the daughter of Sūrya, taking refuge in you, has mounted and sits in your chariot, which protects hundreds of devotees. O Aśvin deities, endowed with wisdom and leaders, among the gods worthy of worship who are manifested in this sacrifice, be, by your wisdom, you yourselves possessed of exceeding skill and supreme.

Protectors of many the daughter of Surya ascended your chariot, the defence of hundreds, for refuge : sagacious leaders and guides, you have excelled by your devices (all others) at this appearance of the adorable (deities).
For a detailed explanation of the matter of Sūrya's daughter having mounted the chariot of the Aśvin deities, see Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 9, pp. 365 and 471.

O Aśvins, you two have brought to Sūryā, your wife, for beauty, fullness, by these beautiful, splendid lustres of fortune, or by radiances. Moreover, your horses have flown forward for splendour. And, O Aśvins, worthy of praise, the well-made praise of the seers has reached you.
- ऊहथुः (*ūhathuḥ*)—you have caused to be obtained
- प्र अनु पप्तन (*pra anu paptana*)—run hither exceedingly
- धिष्ण्या (*dhiṣṇyā*)—O Aśvin deities, worthy of praise

O Aśvin deities, you both have caused to be obtained for the goddess Sūryā, with these attractive splendours, fullness for her auspiciousness. Your horses run hither, for splendour and exceedingly. O Aśvin deities, worthy of praise, the speech of the seers, directed to you and in the form of praise, reaches you.

You have provided with these beautiful splendours, gratification for the enjoyment of Surya, your horses have descended for felicity, deserving of praise, the laudation (of the sages) has reached you glorified.
O Nāsatyas, let your horses, the best bearers, who are goers, bring to us the food in the form of Soma; let them convey it. Your chariot, swift as the mind.

The chariot, swift as the mind, has poured forth for you, one after another, the foods and the Soma drinks. Sāyaṇa glosses pṛkṣaḥ as संपर्चनीया (*saṃparcanīyā*), iṣidhaḥ as desirable, and pūrvīḥ as many; the verb prāsarji means "has been poured out".
- प्रयः अभि (*prayaḥ abhi*)—toward the food in the form of Soma
- आ वहंतु (*ā vahaṃtu*)—let them bring you
- मनोजवाः (*manojavāḥ*)—having the speed of the mind
- अनु प्र असर्जि (*anu pra asarji*)—has poured out

O Aśvin deities, let your horses, swift goers and exceedingly strong bearers of you, bring you toward the food in the form of Soma. Your chariot, which has the speed of the mind, has poured out abundant, desirable and copious food.
May your rapid burden-bearing steeds bring you Nasatyas to the (sacrificial) food : your chariot swift as thought has dispensed substantial, d sirable, abundant food.
O protectors of many, or full-armed ones: the wealth to be given by you is indeed abundant. For that reason give us a nourishing cow, one that does not pass over to anyone else but me,

Asakrā means "not passing over"; Sāyaṇa supports this by Yāska's saying असक्रामसंक्रमणीं (*asakrāmasaṃkramaṇīṃ*) (Ni. 6-29). Give us food. Or else, the construction is: give a desirable cow of food. Moreover, there are praisers; and, O delighting Aśvins, among the praisers there is an excellent praise; and there are Soma juices, which have come to the place of sacrifice in view of your gift. This is the sense: having heard the excellent praise and having drunk the Soma juices that have come to the place of sacrifice, grant the desires of the praisers; this is what is to be supplied.
- पुरुभुजा (*purubhujā*)—O Aśvin deities, protectors of many
- देष्णं (*deṣṇaṃ*)—the wealth that is to be given
- आसक्रां (*āsakrāṃ*)—and not passing over to another
- धेनुं न (*dhenuṃ na*)—like a cow (that is, never diminishing)
- माध्वी (*mādhvī*)—O Aśvin deities, givers of joy
- सुष्टुतिः च (*suṣṭutiḥ ca*)—among the praisers there is also an excellent praise
- रातिं अनु (*rātiṃ anu*)—in view of the gift
- आग्मन् (*āgman*)—have reached the house of the gods
- रसाः च (*rasāḥ ca*)—such Soma juices too are ready

O Aśvin deities, protectors of many, the wealth to be given by you is very abundant. Therefore provide us food that satisfies and never diminishes. O Aśvin deities, givers of joy, the praisers praise you. Among the praisers there is also an excellent praise. The Soma juices that have reached the house of the gods in view of your gift are also ready.

Protectors of many, vast (wealth) is to be distributed by you : give us then nutritious and invariable food. Givers of delight, there are to you, adorers, and fit praise, and libations, which are prepared to acknowledge your liberality

For this word asakrām Yāska gives the etymology धेनुं न इषं पिन्वतमसक्रां । असंक्रमणीं (*dhenuṃ na iṣaṃ pinvatamasakrāṃ | asaṃkramaṇīṃ*) (Ni. 6-29). The meaning is: provide us food like a cow that never stops giving milk,
that is, food that never wastes away and never diminishes.

Moreover, the two straight-going and swift mares that belong to Puraya, a man of that name, have become mine, who praise the Aśvins. A hundred cows that were with King Sumiḷa have become mine. The cooked foods that were with King Peruka have been mine. And King Śāṇḍa should give to the praisers of the Aśvins ten golden chariots or horses of excellent appearance, ten in number, and obedient men, overcomers of enemies, men fair to look upon; let him give them.
- पुरयस्य (*purayasya*)—belonging to the king named Puraya
- मे (*me*)—let them be for me, who praise the Aśvin deities
- शतं (*śataṃ*)—let the hundred cows also be mine
- पक्वा (*pakvā*)—let the cooked foods be mine
- दात् (*dāt*)—let him give to us who worship you

O Aśvin deities, let the horses that belong to the king named Puraya, going straight and swift-going, be for me, who praise the Aśvin deities. Let the hundred cows that are with Sumiḷa and the cooked foods that are with Peruka be mine. Let the king named Śāṇḍa give to us, your worshippers, ten chariots of excellent form and made of gold, and horses suited to them, and obedient men, destroyers of enemies.

May the two straight-going, light-moving, (mares) of Puraya be mine; may the hundred cows belonging to Sumitha, may the dressed viands prepared by Peruka be for me : may Sanda bestow upon me ten handsome golden chariots, and obedient, valiant, and well-favoured (dependants).

O Nāsatyas, Aśvins: the king named Puruṣanthā should give to your praiser, gīḥ meaning one who utters praise, hundreds and thousands of horses.⟨NOTE:178⟩ O heroic Aśvins, let him give quickly also to me, Bharadvāja, who praise you. And, O Aśvins, doers of many deeds, by your favour let the Rākṣasas be slain.
notes: ಪುರುಷಂಥಾ in the bhāṣya and Pratipadārtha, ಪುರುಪಂಥಾಃ in the verse

en: - पुरुदंससा (*purudaṃsasā*)—O Aśvin deities, doers of many deeds

O Aśvin deities, let the king named Puruṣanthā give to your praiser horses numbering hundreds and thousands. O mighty Aśvin deities, let him give them quickly also to Bharadvāja, who praises you. O Aśvin deities, doers of many deeds, let all the Rākṣasas be slain.
May Purupantha, Nasatyas, grant to him who praises you. hundreds and thousands of horses: may he give them, heroes, to Bharadwaja : achievers of great deeds, may the Rakshasas be slain.

O Aśvin, in the vast happiness, the wealth given by you two that brings happiness (he supports this by जलाषं सुम्ममिति सुखनामसु (*jalāṣaṃ summamiti sukhanāmasu*), since sumna is read among the names of happiness), may I be on every side together with the learned, my sons and the rest.
- वां (*vāṃ*)—with the help of the wealth given by you
- आ स्यां (*ā syāṃ*)—may we be everywhere
O Aśvin deities, with the help of the wealth given by you, may we, with learned sons, live in very extended happiness.
May I be associated with the pious in the abundant felicity bestowe I by you.

The shining ones (rocamānā) are the radiant, and the rushantaḥ are those of white colour; Yāska says (Ni. 2-20) that "rushat" is a name for colour. For the beauty of the world, or else to pervade the world, the dawns rise up like the waves connected with water. What follows then passes into the singular: Uṣas makes all places have good roads, that is, easy to travel with ease. Further, the wealthy Uṣas becomes praiseworthy and a bringer of abundant prosperity.
- रुशंतः (*ruśaṃtaḥ*)—and the ones of pure white colour
- श्रिये (*śriye*)—to give lustre to the world
- दक्षिणा (*dakṣiṇā*)—as one who brings about abundance of prosperity

The dawns, of attractive form and pure white colour, arise like the waves of the waters to give lustre to the world. Uṣas makes all places have excellent roads and be suitable for easy travel. The wealthy Uṣas becomes praiseworthy and a bringer of abundant prosperity.

The white and shining tints of the dawn have spread like the waves of the waters, for the beautifying (of the world); she renders all good roads easy to be traversed; she who is replete with delight, excellence, and health.

O goddess Uṣas, you are seen as auspicious, and you shine broad and far-spread. Your bright flames, that is your rays, have flown up into the sky. Further, O goddess Uṣas, shining and radiant with your splendours, you make your own form manifest.
- वि भासि (*vi bhāsi*)—you shine with lustre

O goddess Uṣas, you are visible to the whole world in an auspicious form. With an exceedingly extensive form you shine with lustre. Your bright rays have spread, pervading the whole sky. O goddess Uṣas, shining with your splendours and with an attractive form, you reveal your form.
Divine Ushas, you are seen auspicious : you shine afar: your bright rays spread over the sky, lovely and radiant with great (splendours), you display your person.

The ruddy, that is red-coloured, and shining cows are rays, since "kiraṇāḥ" and "gāvaḥ" are read among the names of rays. They carry this goddess Uṣas, who is of good fortune, broad, and spreading far. This goddess Uṣas drives darkness away, like a hero, that is like a thrower who hurls at his enemies. Just as a swift-moving leader of an army harasses enemies, so she harasses the darknesses.
- शत्र्यान् (*śatryān*)—like one who strikes and drives away enemies
- वोळ्हा न (*voḷhā na*)—like a leader of an army

The golden-hued and resplendent rays carry this goddess Uṣas, who is the bestower of auspiciousness, of extensive form and renowned. As a valiant archer strikes and drives away enemies, the goddess Uṣas strikes and drives away the darkness. Like a swift-moving leader of an army, she afflicts the darkness.
Ruddy and resplendent cows bear the auspicious, expanding, illustrious dawn : like a warrior, who, casting his darts, or a swift charger scattering enemies, she drives away the glooms.

O goddess Uṣas, in mountains, that is in inaccessible places, and in places without means of passage, good paths that are easy to travel with ease are yours. O self-luminous one, you cross the "apaḥ", that is the sky, since "āpaḥ" is read among the names of the sky; or else you cross the waters of the ocean. O you of the wide chariot, O beautiful one, O daughter of heaven, that is of the sky, goddess Uṣas: you, such as you are, bring to us the wealth that is to be desired.
- अवाते (*avāte*)—in the inaccessible places which have no means of passage
- दिवो दुहितः (*divo duhitaḥ*)—O Uṣas, daughter of the sky
- सा (*sā*)—you who have such auspicious qualities
- ऋष्टे (*ṛṣṭe*)—and having an attractive form: in your chariot which is such

O goddess Uṣas, the excellent paths and the means of easy travel that exist in the mountains and in the inaccessible strongholds without means of passage belong to you. O self-luminous goddess, you cross the sky. O Uṣas, daughter of the sky, you who have such renowned auspicious qualities, bring to us in your chariot, which has a wide expanse and an attractive form, the wealth that we desire.

Yours are good roads and easy to be traversed in mountains and inaccessible places : you pass self-irradating over the waters : bring to us, daughter of heaven, in your spacious and beatiful chariot, desirable riches.

O Uṣas, such as you are, bring excellent wealth to me. You who, unobstructed, bear excellent wealth for the singers according to their pleasure, that is their delight, with oxen or else with horses. Further, O daughter of heaven, that is of the sky, you who are a goddess, shining, in the first invocation, the Prātaranuvāka, are (continued below).
You are worthy of worship, and such as you are, be worth seeing: so the construction is made.
- आ वह (*ā vaha*)—come, bearing it for me
- दिवो दुहितः (*divo duhitaḥ*)—O Uṣas, daughter of the sky
- पूर्वहूतौ ह (*pūrvahūtau ha*)—in the very first sacrifice
- मंहना (*maṃhanā*)—are worthy of worship (such as you are)

O goddess Uṣas, you who, unobstructed, bear dear wealth upon your vehicles, which have the form of bulls, such as you are, bring me excellent wealth. O Uṣas, daughter of the sky, you who, shining and venerable, are worthy of worship in the very first sacrifice (in the Prātaranuvāka), such as you are, be of a form worth seeing.

Ushas, bring me opulence, for unopposed you bear with your oxen (wealth to your worshippers), according to your satisfaction : daughter of heaven, you who are divine, who are lovely, are to be worshipped at the first (daily) rite.

O goddess Uṣas, when your dawning has taken place, even the birds fly up from their dwelling-place. Those who are sharers in oblations, or earners of food, since "pitu" is read among the names of food, the men, they too rise up. Further, O goddess Uṣas, you bring abundant desired wealth to the mortal who is near, the giver of oblations.
- नरः च (*naraḥ ca*)—men also, awakened, rise and move about

O goddess Uṣas, at the time of your manifestation even the birds fly away from their dwelling-places. Men engaged in earning food also awake, rise and move about. O divine Uṣas, bring abundant desired wealth to the sacrificer who is near you and offers oblations to you.

At your dawning, divine Ushas, the birds spring up from their nests, and men who have to gain their sustenance (arise) : you divine Ushas, bring ample wealth to the mortal who is near you, the offerer of the oblation.

This Uṣas is born of heaven and therefore is the daughter, the child of heaven. For us she drives away the darknesses and rouses the human peoples; "ajīgaḥ" means that she makes them manifest, that is she illumines them, and Yāska is cited for this (Ni. 6-8). She who, joined with a shining ray, in the nights, "rāmyā" being explained as "yāmyā", puts into the shade the lights of the stars and the like, and the darknesses as well, is seen as such.
- राम्यासु (*rāmyāsu*)—that were in the night times
- अज्ञायि (*ajñāyi*)—becomes visible, such as she is
- दुहिता (*duhitā*)—and the daughter of the heavenly world

The renowned goddess Uṣas, born of the heavenly world and daughter of the heavenly world, who becomes visible by her bright rays, concealing the stars and the like that shone in the night time, and likewise the darkness, destroys the darkness for us and illumines the human peoples.

This heaven-bron daughter (of th sky), driving away the darkness for us, makes visible humau beings : she who with bright lustre is perceived dissipating the glooms, and (extinguishing) the planets (shining) in the nights.

"Chandrarathāḥ" means those whose chariots are radiant; Yāska is cited for the sense of "candra" (Ni. 11-5). Those Uṣases, at that time, in the morning, bring forward the front, the head, of the great, growth-natured sacrifice, and go forth widely with horses of red colour.
They also shine wonderfully. "Ūrmyā" is read among the names of night, as is "aktu"; so they drive away the darkness of the night, that is they remove it completely.
- चंद्ररथाः (*caṃdrarathāḥ*)—those who have chariots of attractive radiance
- वि ययुः (*vi yayuḥ*)—they move about at will

The dawns, who have chariots of attractive radiance, in the morning time itself, securing the front part of the sacrifice, which is of vast nature, move about at will with horses of red colour. Shining in manifold ways, they destroy completely the darkness of the night time.

The Dawns in beautiful chariots drawn by purple steeds in pairs, shine gloriously as they proceed (along the heaven) : bringing on the commencement of the great (morning) sacrifice, they disperse the darkness of the night.

notes: ಸಂಹಿತಾಪಾಠ ends ॥ ೮ ॥; the Padapāṭha of the same ṛk has ॥ ೩ ॥

en: O Uṣases, to the mortal who gives oblations you bear fame, strength, food and sustenance; being wealthy and going forth today, bestow constantly on me, who serve you, food together with heroes, that is with sons, grandsons and the like, and wealth as well. "Sinam" and "avaḥ" are read among the names of food, and "śvātram" and "ratnam" are read among the names of wealth.
- विधते (*vidhate*)—to me also who worship you
- वीरवत् (*vīravat*)—together with heroic sons and the like

O goddesses Uṣas, you who bear fame, strength, food and sap to the man who offers oblations, going about as wealthy ones, give at this time completely, to me also who worship you, food together with heroic sons and the like, and wealth.

Dawns, bringing fame, and food, and sustenance, and strength to the mortal, the donor (of the oblation). abounding in wealth, and proceeding (through the sky), bestow upon the worshipper to-day food, with male descendants and riches.

O Uṣases, even now, at this very moment, you have wealth to give to the one who serves you. At this very moment you have wealth to give to the hero, the impeller, the giver of oblations, the sacrificer. At this very moment you have wealth to give to the sage, the wise one who praises you. In whom the stotras called ukthas exist, to that sacrificer, who is like me, bring that wealth. Even before this, wealth was given to me.
- विधते (*vidhate*)—to give to the one who offers worship
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer (you have wealth to give)
- जरते (*jarate*)—and the praiser, to the sacrificer, there is wealth to give
- मावते (*māvate*)—to that sacrificer also, who is like me
- पुरा चित् (*purā cit*)—you gave to me even before

O goddesses Uṣas, now itself there is wealth to give to the one who offers worship to you. Now itself there is wealth to give to the sacrificer who offers oblations. Now itself there is wealth to give to the sacrificer who is wise and a praiser. O Uṣases, to the sacrificer who, like me, has stotras of the called kind, bring and fill wealth, just as you gave it to us before.

Verily, Dawns, there is at present wealth to give to your worshipper, to the man offering (oblations), to the sage repeating your praise ; if the praises (are accepted), then bring to him who is like me such wealth as has been formerly bestowed (upon myself).

O Uṣas, you of honoured summit, by your grace, now itself, the Aṅgirases release the herds of cattle. So another Vedic passage says गवां गोत्रमुदसृजो यदंगिरः (*gavāṃ gotramudasṛjo yadaṃgiraḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-23-18)⟨NOTE:182⟩ **GLOSS**. With the worshipful brahma, that is the stotra, they also split the darknesses. The invocation of the gods, the praise directed to the gods, of those leaders, the Aṅgirases, became true, that is fruitful with truth.⟨NOTE:183⟩
notes: abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ. printed
ಅದ್ರಿಸಾನೋ: Sāyaṇa takes it as a vocative addressed to Uṣas (ಆದೃತಸಾನೋ); the Kannada gloss takes it as "from the mountain peaks"

en: - अद्रिसानो (*adrisāno*)—from the peak regions of the mountain
- गवां गोत्रा (*gavāṃ gotrā*)—the herd of cattle
- ब्रह्मणा च (*brahmaṇā ca*)—with the stotra also
- वि बिभिदुः (*vi bibhiduḥ*)—they have destroyed the darkness
- देवहूतिः (*devahūtiḥ*)—the praise directed to the gods

O goddess Uṣas, by your grace the Aṅgirases release now itself the herds of cattle from the peak regions of the mountain. With the stotra worthy of worship also they have destroyed the darkness. The praise directed to the gods, of the leaders, the Aṅgirases, became possessed of the fruit of truth.
Verily, Ushas. the Angirasas through your (favour) recover the herd of cattle from the summit of the mountain : by adoration and prayer they
have divided (the rock) : unfailing was the praise of the gods uttered by the leaders (of rites).

O Uṣas, daughter of heaven, as for the ancients, so for us drive away the darkness. O wealthy one, to me who serve you, as to Bharadvāja: the word "bharadvājavat" implies that there is yet another Bharadvāja, and so a Brāhmaṇa says प्राणो वै भरद्वाजवदिति (*prāṇo vai bharadvājavaditi*) **GLOSS**.
