To me who offer praise give wealth together with excellent sons, grandsons and the like. Further, bestow upon us in abundance food, which is to be sung by many; give more.
- दिवो दुहितः (*divo duhitaḥ*)—O goddess Uṣas, daughter of the heavenly world
- प्रत्नवत् (*pratnavat*)—just as you favoured in the past
- मघोनि (*maghoni*)—O goddess Uṣas who are possessed of wealth
- भरद्वाजवत् (*bharadvājavat*)—just as you gave in the past to Bharadvāja
- विधते (*vidhate*)—to me too who offer worship to you
- सुवीरं (*suvīraṃ*)—together with heroic sons and the like

O goddess Uṣas, daughter of the heavenly world, as you favoured in the past, so for us also destroy the darkness and bring about light. O goddess Uṣas, who are possessed of wealth, as you gave in the past to Bharadvāja, so give to me also, who offer worship to you and praise you, wealth together with heroic sons and the like. Provide us also with food that is praised by many.

Daughter of hevan, dawn upon us, as upon those of old : possessor of riches (dawn) upon the worshipper, as (you have done upon) Bharadwaja : grant to him who glcrifes you, wealth with male decendants : give to us food that may be distributed to many.

That well-known form is the same, that is, of one form; the Maruts are always of the same form. So another Vedic passage says अजेष्ठासो अकनिष्ठास एते (*ajeṣṭhāso akaniṣṭhāsa ete*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-60-5)⟨NOTE:187⟩ **GLOSS**. "Nāma" is the namer even of those who are firm. The pleasing, ever-moving form of the Maruts: may it quickly be manifest to the knowing praiser; "cid" is a filler. Further, that form, among mortals, in the mortal world, makes the herbs, trees and the like other than man swell, so as to yield desires. Further, from the mention of the Maruts alone, Pṛśni, the atmosphere, once in the year, in the rains, milks the bright udder, that is the water, that is, lets it flow.⟨NOTE:188⟩
notes: abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ. printed
ನಾಮ: Sāyaṇa glosses ನಾಮ ಸ್ಥಿರಾಣಾಮಪಿ ನಾಮಕಂ; the Kannada gloss reads "that which makes strong enemies submissive"

en: - नाम (*nāma*)—that which makes strong enemies submissive
- अस्तु (*astu*)—let it be visible and appear (that same troop of Maruts)
- अन्यत् (*anyat*)—the herbs, trees and the like
- दोहसे (*dohase*)—for the accomplishment of the desired ends of man
- पीपाय (*pīpāya*)—it makes grow (by the will of these Maruts)
- सकृत् (*sakṛt*)—at the respective time of the year

The renowned form of the Maruts, which is of one form, makes powerful enemies submissive, is pleasing and ever moving, becomes visible before the wise praiser. That same troop of Maruts makes the herbs, trees and the like in the human world grow for the accomplishment of the desired ends of man. By the will of these Maruts, the atmosphere also, in the rainy season of the year, milks bright-coloured water.

May the like-formed, benevolent, all-pervading, all-humiliating troop (of the Maruts) be promptly with the prudent man : the troop that ever cherishes, all that amongst mortals is designed to yield (them) advantage and (at whose will) Prishni gives milk from (her) bright udder once (in the year).
The Maruts shine like fires that are being kindled; they grow twofold and threefold, that is they increase as they wish. The chariots of these Maruts are free of dust (continued below).

and have golden fittings; that is, the Maruts' chariots are golden and ornamented with gold. Those Maruts appear together with riches and with strengths. So another Vedic passage says ये पृषतीभिर्यष्टिभिः (*ye pṛṣatībhiryaṣṭibhiḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-37-2)⟨NOTE:189⟩ **GLOSS**.
notes: abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ. printed

en: - हिरण्ययासः (*hiraṇyayāsaḥ*)—and made of gold (these same Maruts)

The chariots of the Maruts, who blaze and shine like fires and who increase twofold and threefold, are free of dust and made of gold. Those same Maruts manifest themselves together with riches and with powers.

Unsoiled by dust the golden chariots of those Maruts, who are shining like kindled fires, enlarging themselves (at will) twofold and three-fold, and (charged) with riches and virile energies, are manifest.

The Maruts who are sons of Rudra, the sprinkler, the supporting Pṛśni, that is the atmosphere, is able to bear them. "Vide hi" means that it is known to all that the mother of these great ones, that Pṛśni, is great. Further, that Pṛśni has conceived the germ, that is the water, for the good existence of men.
- पुत्राः (*putrāḥ*)—who are in the form of sons
- दाधृविः (*dādhṛviḥ*)—the atmosphere, the supporter, becomes able
- विदे हि (*vide hi*)—this is a matter known to all
- सा इत् पृश्निः (*sā it pṛśniḥ*)—that same Pṛśni
- सुभ्वे (*subhve*)—to bring about the welfare of all men

The Maruts who are in the form of sons of Rudra, the showerer of rain, and whom the atmosphere, the supporter, is able to bear: it is a matter known to all that Pṛśni, the mother of such great Maruts, is of great form. That same Pṛśni has received and borne the water to bring about the welfare of all men.

They (who are) the sons of the showerer Rudra, whom the nursing (firmament is able) to sustain, and of whom, the mighty ones, it is known that the great Prishni has received the germ for the benefit (of man).

The well-known Maruts do not go to the people who praise them by any means of going. Is there then no going because there is no one to be protected? He says no: being within, dwelling in the hearts of all, they purify the sins. And so another Vedic passage says प्राणा वै मरुतः स्वापयः (*prāṇā vai marutaḥ svāpayaḥ*) (Ai. Brā. 3-16) **GLOSS**. Therefore, because they dwell in the hearts of all beings, they have no going. Thereby their standing in the self in the form of vital breaths is shown, while their swift-going is to be understood as belonging to their form as deities. When the shining Maruts milk out the water in accordance with the desire of the praisers, then, accompanied by splendour, making their own body shine, they sprinkle the earth. Or else: they sprinkle the earth in such a way that it is broad; this is the meaning.⟨NOTE:190⟩
notes: ಸ್ತೋತ್ಕೃನ್ಯಾಯಾಯೇನ damaged in the first sentence; read as ಸ್ತೋತೄನ್ and ಅಯೇನ

en: - अंतः संतः (*aṃtaḥ saṃtaḥ*)—being within the hearts of all people
- अया (*ayā*)—in the means of going, chariots and the like
- न ईषंते नु (*na īṣaṃte nu*)—there is no toil of having to go
- जोषमनु (*joṣamanu*)—in accordance with the wish of the praisers
- निः दुह्रे (*niḥ duhre*)—milk out rain in abundance, then
- उक्षमाणाः (*ukṣamāṇāḥ*)—they are those who pour rain

The Maruts, who being within the hearts of all people purify all the sins of each, such purifying Maruts have no toil of having to go to the praising people in chariots, the means of going. When the shining Maruts milk out rain in abundance in accordance with the wish of the praisers, then, accompanied by splendour and making their own body shine, they are those who pour rain.
They who approach not to men by any conveyance, being already
in their hearts, purifying their defects : when brilliant they supply their
milk (the rain) for the gratification (of their worshippers) : they are
watering the earth (manifesting their collective) form with splendour.

Among those well-known Maruts, the worshippers who approach them and recite the assailing (धृष्णु (*dhṛṣṇu*)) Marut-named śastra are quickly able to milk out, that is, to obtain, their desires. The particle "na" is used here in the sense of "now". Those who are thieves or hidden plunderers of the worshippers' wealth become runaways, and they are also endowed with greatness. Such fierce, angry ones are pacified by the sacrificer, the giver of good oblations: he makes them free of anger. ⟨NOTE:191⟩
notes: ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯ ಅಪಗತಕ್ರೋಧಾನ್ ಕರೋತಿ "makes them free of anger", whereas the Kannada ಪ್ರತಿಪದಾರ್ಥ/ಭಾವಾರ್ಥ says ನಾಶಮಾಡಲು ಶಕ್ತನಾಗುತ್ತಾನೆ "becomes able to destroy" the enemies

en: - येषु (*yeṣu*)—in regard to those very Maruts
- दोहसे (*dohase*)—become able to obtain their desired ends
- अव यासत् (*ava yāsat*)—becomes able to destroy

Those very Maruts: the worshippers who approach them, reciting the enemy-restraining, Marut-named śastra-mantra, are quickly able to obtain their desired ends. The thieves, plunderers of wealth, who run away, and those who are terrible by their greatness, such enemies the excellent giver, the sacrificer, becomes able to destroy.

Approaching nigh to whom, and repeating the mighty name of the Maruts, (the worshipper is able) quickly to obtain (his wishes): the liberal donor pacifies the angry Maruts, who are otherwise in their might the the resistless plunderers (of their wealth).
Those fierce Maruts, endowed with strength and speed and having assailing armies, join together the two beautiful ones, heaven and earth. The intention is that by raining they gratify the earth.

And moreover, in these Maruts, the two worlds, who are the wife of Rudra, that is, the speech of the middle region, are self-radiant; in these mighty ones the obstructing light does not stand, that is, it does not come forth at all.
- धृष्णुषेणाः (*dhṛṣṇuṣeṇāḥ*)—possessed of an army that overcomes enemies
- उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)—both heaven and earth
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—the goddess of the middle region, speech, wife of Rudra
- न आ तस्थौ (*na ā tasthau*)—cannot exist

Those very Maruts, terrible to enemies and possessed of an army that overcomes enemies, endowed with strength, join together both heaven and earth, which are of beautiful form. Moreover, the goddess of the middle region, the wife of Rudra, self-radiant, abides in these very Maruts. In these mighty Maruts the power that obstructs light cannot exist.
Those fierce and powerfully arrayed (Maruts) unite by their strength
the two beautiful (regions) heaven and earth ; in them, the self-radiant,
heaven and earth abide : the obstruction (of light) dwells not in those

O Maruts, may your chariot be free of sin, that is, may it appear free of fault. Moreover, the chariot which a worshipper drives, impels, even though he is no charioteer (a charioteer is one who drives; he who is not is an "arathī"), is without horses, without provisions for the journey, without reins; it urges the water, accomplishes the desires of the worshippers, and travels variously through heaven and earth and the paths of the firmament. ⟨NOTE:192⟩
notes: ಅನವಸಃ: Sāyaṇa glosses ಪಥ್ಯಧನರಹಿತಃ "without provisions for the journey"; the Kannada ಪ್ರತಿಪದಾರ್ಥ says ತೃಣಾದಿರಹಿತವಾದ ಮಾರ್ಗಗಾಮಿ "going on a road without grass etc."

en: - अरथीः चित् (*arathīḥ cit*)—even though he is not a charioteer
- अनवसः (*anavasaḥ*)—which travels a road free of grass and the like
- सादन् (*sādan*)—which fulfils the desires of the praisers
- पथ्याः (*pathyāḥ*)—and on the path of the firmament

O Maruts, even without a charioteer, the worshipper, by your favour, can impel your chariot. That chariot, which is without horses, travels on a road free of grass and the like, is without traces, impels water, fulfils the desires of the praisers and travels especially in heaven and earth and on the path of the firmament, is free of sin.

May your chariot, Maruts, be devoid of wickedness ; that which (the worshipper) impels, and which without driver without horses, without provender, without traces, scatter watering and accomplishing (desires) traverses heaven and earth and the paths (of the firmament).

O Maruts, the man whom you protect in battle has no one to impel him (or hinder him), and no destroyer. Moreover, the man whom you protect, with regard to son, grandson, wealth, cows or waters, becomes in the decisive battle the one who breaks up the herd of cattle, the collection of cows, of the enemy, even though that enemy be fiery or eager for victory. ⟨NOTE:193⟩
notes: ವರ್ತಾ: Sāyaṇa ಪ್ರೇರಕಃ "impeller"; the Kannada ಪ್ರತಿಪದಾರ್ಥ has ನಿರ್ಬಂಧಕಾರನು "hinderer"

en: - तोके (*toke*)—for the sake of a son
- तनये (*tanaye*)—for the sake of a grandson
- गोषु वा (*goṣu vā*)—or on account of cows
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—even though the enemy is strong in power

O Maruts, the man whom you protect in battle has no hinderer and no destroyer. The man whom you protect for the sake of a son, a grandson, or on account of cows, or for the sake of water, is able, even though the enemy in battle is strong in power, to scatter his herd of cattle.

There is no propeller, no obstructer, of him, whom Maruts, you protect in battle : he whom (you prosper) with sons, grandsons, cattle, and water, is war the despoiler of the herds of his ardent (foe).

O Agni, to the host of Maruts, who are praising or being praised, swift, and possessed of their own strength, bring forth a wonderful, beautiful अर्कं (*arkaṃ*), that is, food, an oblation, since it is read among the names of food. "Bring forth" is said to Agni and to the priests who are his helpers: all of you bring it forth. As in the world, when many are engaged in one task, a prayer addresses the chief one alone and says "you all do thus", so here too Agni alone, the chief, is addressed and yet the plural is used. The Maruts are those who overcome the powers of enemies by their own strength; from fear of those honourable Maruts the earth trembles. The word for the Maruts' host, though the Maruts are included within it, takes them separately in thought, and so "who" refers back to them. He quotes as an example the Mahābhāṣya, अथ शब्दानुशासनं (*atha śabdānuśāsanaṃ*) followed by केषां शब्दानां (*keṣāṃ śabdānāṃ*) (M. 1.1-1) ⟨NOTE:194⟩, and the example from the world: when "a king's man" is said, one asks "whose kingdom?"
notes: abbreviation ಮ. printed, reference ಮ. ೧.೧-೧ as printed

en: - मखेभ्यः (*makhebhyaḥ*)—from fear of the venerable Maruts
O Agni, to the host of Maruts, those who defeat the powers of enemies by their own strength, such noise-making, swift-moving, endowed with their own strength, the attractive and venerable
food (oblation) that is attractive and venerable: offer it. From fear of the venerable Maruts the earth trembles.

Offer to the loud-sounding, quick-moving, self invigorating company of the Maruts, excellent (sacrificial) food : (to them) who overcome strength by strength : the earth trembles, Agni, at the adorable (Maruts).

The Maruts shine like a sacrifice; they are swift-moving. Like the flames of Agni they are radiant and full of splendour; they are venerable. Like shakers of rivals, causing them to tremble, they are heroes, brave ones, of shining body, and they are unassailed, not overcome by others.
- धुनयो न (*dhunayo na*)—like those who make enemies tremble
- भ्राजज्जन्मानः (*bhrājajjanmānaḥ*)—having a body full of lustre

The swift-moving Maruts give light to the sacrifice. They possess a venerable form. They make enemies tremble, they are possessed of valour, they have a body full of lustre, and they shine unassailed by enemies.
The Maruts are resplendent as if illuminators of the sacrifice,
(bright) as the flames of Agni, entitled are they to adoration, and like
heroes making (adversaries) tremble : brilliant are they from birth, and

That well-known, growing host of Maruts, who are the sons of Rudra and have shining lances, I serve with praise. Moreover, the pure praises of the worshipper, fierce and uplifted, for the strength of the Maruts (it is read among the names of strength) are pervading, as clouds do (it is read among the names of cloud), and they vie with one another.
- रुद्रस्य सूनुं (*rudrasya sūnuṃ*)—the one in the form of Rudra's sons
- शर्धायॆ (*śardhāyè*)—offered to the host of Maruts
- गिरियो न (*giriyo na*)—like the clouds that cause rain

I serve with praise the well-known host of Maruts, which grows, has shining weapons and is in the form of the sons of Rudra. The praiser's pure praises, possessed of great strength, offered to the host of Maruts and pervading it, vie like the clouds that cause rain.
I worship with oblations that exalted company of the Maruts,
the progeny of Rudra, armed with shining lances: the pure and earnest
praises of the devout (adorer) are emulous in the invigoration (of the
Muruts), as the clouds (vie in the emission of the rain).

Among all existing beings, O Mitra and Varuṇa, the most senior, I have set about to increase you with praises. You two together are "uneven", that is, unequal; that your unevenness is another matter is shown by another passage: त्रिरश्रिं हंति चतुरश्रिरुग्रः (*triraśriṃ haṃti caturaśrirugraḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-152-2) **GLOSS** ⟨NOTE:195⟩. You two, the best restrainers, hold the people together with your own arms, as one holds horses with a rein; the plural "arms" is used for honour.
notes: abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ. printed in the reference ಋಗ್ವೇ. ೧-೧೫೨-೨

en: - यमिष्णा (*yamiṣṇā*)—as the best controllers of the world
- रश्मेव (*raśmeva*)—as one keeps horses under control with bridles
- सं यमतुः (*saṃ yamatuḥ*)—you keep under control, such as you

O Mitra and Varuṇa, the most excellent among all beings that are real, you two, though not of equal form, as the best controllers of the world, keep all the people under control with your arms, as one keeps horses under control with bridles. I cause you to increase with praises.
(I proceed) by my praises to exalt you, Mitra and Varuna, the
eldest of all existing things : you two, though not the same, are the firmest
restrainers with your arms, and hold men back (from evil) as they check

O Mitra and Varuṇa, this praise of mine spreads over you and covers you. O beloved ones, it goes to you with the food, the oblation, and goes to your sacrificial grass. O Mitra and Varuṇa, grant us an unassailed, unconquered house. O good givers, the house given by you is to be a protector against cold, wind and heat.
- सुदानू (*sudānū*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa, excellent givers
- वरूथ्यं (*varūthyaṃ*)—a protector against cold, wind and the like

O Mitra and Varuṇa, this praise of mine joins you both and pervades. O beloved Mitra and Varuṇa, that same praise, together with the oblation, approaches you. The seat of darbha grass is spread out for you. O Mitra and Varuṇa, excellent givers, give us a house that is unassailed, given by you, and a protector against cold, wind and the like.

This my praise is addressed to you both, and proceeds, to you beloved (deities) together with the oblation : the sacred grass is spread before you : grant us, Mitra and Varuna, unassailable dwelling, that through your favour, munificent divinities, may be a (secure) shelter.

O Mitra and Varuṇa, invoked with good praise, with the food, the oblation, or the song of praise, beloved of the whole world, come near. You two, endowed with greatness, hold in check the people who desire food or fame for themselves, as a man engaged in a rite does by his work. The word for "rite" is read among the names of work.
- अपसेव (*apaseva*)—as he obtains his position by his own work
- महित्वा चित् (*mahitvā cit*)—by your greatness itself
- सं यतथः (*saṃ yatathaḥ*)—join with their accomplishments, such as you
- उप आ यातं (*upa ā yātaṃ*)—be gracious and come to us

O Mitra and Varuṇa, as a man devoted to rites obtains his position by his own work, so you, by your greatness, join men who desire food with their accomplishments. You are dear to all and are invoked with a hymn of good praise; be gracious and come to us.
Come, Mitra and Varuna, beloved by all, and invoked with reverence to the propitious rite, you who by your bounty support men labouring for sustenance as a workman (maintains himself) by work.

The two who are like horses, strong, whose praises are pure, and who are truthful: Aditi, the goddess, bore them as an embryo. Moreover, these two, Mitra and Varuṇa, were greater than the great even as they were being born; they are terrible to the mortal, the harming enemy, and are his slayers. Aditi bore them in her own womb. ⟨NOTE:196⟩
notes: ಮರ್ತಾಯ, ಘೋರಾ: Sāyaṇa ಮರ್ತಾಯ ರಿಪವೇ ಹಿಂಸಕಾಯ ಘೋರೌ ಘಾತಕೌ "terrible, slayers, to the harming mortal foe"; the Kannada ಪ್ರತಿಪದಾರ್ಥ takes ಮರ್ತಾಯ as "for the welfare of man" and ಘೋರಾ as "destroyers of the foe"

en: - ऋता (*ṛtā*)—who are of the nature of truth
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—in the form of an embryo
- जायमाना (*jāyamānā*)—at the very time of being born
- प्रमहांता (*pramahāṃtā*)—such Mitra and Varuṇa as had attained very great majesty
- नि दीधः (*ni dīdhaḥ*)—Aditi obtained as her sons

Those Mitra and Varuṇa who, like horses, are strong, worthy of pure praises and of the nature of truth, whom Aditi bore in her womb, who even when born had attained greater majesty than those who have greatness
such Mitra and Varuṇa Aditi obtained as her sons, for the benefit of man, to be destroyers of the harming enemy.
Who (are) strong as horses, accepters of pious praise, observers of truth, whom Aditi conceived : whom, mighty of the mighty at your birth and formidable to mortal foes, she bore.

All the gods, united in mutual affection, delighting in your greatness, that is, praising you, laid strength in you. Moreover, since you two encompass the wide heaven and earth, your rays, unharmed and undeluded, are there. ⟨NOTE:197⟩
notes: ಸ್ಪಶೋ ರಶ್ಮಯಶ್ಚ ರಾ ವಾ ಸಂತಿ: the words after ರಶ್ಮಯಶ್ಚ look damaged; only "rays" is clear

en: - रोदसी चित् (*rodasī cit*)—both heaven and earth
- परि भूथः (*pari bhūthaḥ*)—pervade and overpower (such of you)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, you, whom all the gods, assembling together, praising you, for your greatness, established your strength in, you who pervade and overpower both the wide heaven and earth, such as you have rays that are unharmed and free of obstruction.

Inasmuch as all the gods equally pleased and rejoicing in your greatness conferred strength upon you, and since you are pre-eminent over the wide heaven and earth, your courses are unobstructed, unimpeded.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you indeed hold strength day by day. You make firm the ridge of the sky, the lofty region of the atmosphere, that is, the cloud or the sun.

As a post, that which is set up, holds a calf, so do you hold: this is the meaning. The cloud, made firm by you, filling the atmosphere, and the sun, the All-god, nourished by the food, the oblation, of man (the words for "man" and for "food" are read among the names of man and the names of food), spread out earth and heaven, made firm by you alone.
- दृंहेथे (*dṛṃhethe*)—you make endowed with firm strength
- नक्षत्रः (*nakṣatraḥ*)—the cloud that pervades the atmosphere
- धासिना (*dhāsinā*)—satisfied by the food in the form of the oblation
- आ आतान् (*ā ātān*)—cause to be abundant

O Mitra and Varuṇa, you, the well known, hold great strength every day. You make the lofty region of the atmosphere endowed with firm strength, like a firm pillar. The cloud that pervades the atmosphere and is firm, and the sun, satisfied by the food in the form of the oblation given by man, cause the earth and the heaven to be abundant.
You manifest vigour daily, you strengthen the summit of the sky as
if with a pillar; the solid firmament and the universal deity (the sun)
replenish earth and heaven with the food of man.

O Mitra and Varuṇa, you hold the wise sacrificer (the word for "wise" is read among the names of the intelligent) in order to fill the belly with Soma. When the priests, who are supported together with him, fill the sacrificial seat, the house of the sacrifice, then, O sustainers of all, when the water sent by you comes, the young women, that is, the rivers or the quarters, are not harmed, not overcome by dust, and, not dried up, bear abundance. ⟨NOTE:198⟩
notes: ವಿಪ್ರಂ in the Kannada ಪ್ರತಿಪದಾರ್ಥ, while Saṃhitā and Sāyaṇa have ವಿಗ್ರಂ

en: - विश्वजिन्वा (*viśvajinvā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa, who are pleasing to the whole world
- न मृष्यंते (*na mṛṣyaṃte*)—are not obstructed by anyone
- अवाताः (*avātāḥ*)—not drying up in the least
- वि भरंते (*vi bharaṃte*)—spread abundance of water

O Mitra and Varuṇa, when the priests fill the house of sacrifice, then you, the well known, take refuge in the wise sacrificer in order to fill your belly with Soma juice; that is, you become his refuge. O Mitra and Varuṇa, pleasing to the whole world, when you send water, then the rivers are not obstructed by anyone, and spread around an abundance of water that does not dry up.
You two support the sage (worshipper), filling his belly when he and
his dependants fill the sacrificial chamber ; when, sustainers of all, the
rain (is sent down by you), and the young (rivers) are not obstructed, but,

O Mitra and Varuṇa, the wise man always asks you, with his tongue, that is, with speech, for this water. The word "ā" is seen as a preverb, so the fitting verb "asks" is supplied; because water was the subject of the previous ṛk, the water turning in the mind is referred to by the word "this". When your approacher, truthful and free of deceit, comes to the sacrifice, O you whose food is ghee, may that greatness of yours, which consists in giving what is desired, be yours. Moreover, you two destroy the sin of the sacrificer who gives the oblation.
- आ भूत् (*ā bhūt*)—he approaches you, then
- धृतान्नौ (*dhṛtānnau*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa, whose food is ghee
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—of the sacrificer who offers the oblation

O Mitra and Varuṇa, when your worshipper approaches you sincerely in the sacrifice, then the wise sacrificer always asks you with his speech for water. O Mitra and Varuṇa, whose food is ghee, may the greatness of giving generously be in you. May you two destroy the sin of the sacrificer who offers the oblation.

The wise man always (solicits) you with his prayers for this (supply of water), when approaching you sincerely in sacrifice : may your magnani- mity be such that you, the feeders upon ghi, may exterminate sin in the donor (of the oblation).
O Mitra and Varuṇa, your dear deeds, ordained by you, are those which the non-sacrificing people, vying with you, harm; and the gods who are not joined with the praise that carries the oblation

The mortals, men, are not joined with हसा (*hasā*) ⟨NOTE:199⟩. And those who have चाप्यः (*cāpyaḥ*) ⟨NOTE:200⟩, that is, work (अपः कर्म (*apaḥ karma*)): possessing it, they are अयज्ञसाचः (*ayajñasācaḥ*), not joined with sacrifice; the meaning is that they perform fruitless works. And those who are न पुत्राः (*na putrāḥ*): they who fill (पृणंतीति (*pṛṇaṃtīti*)) are sons (पुत्राः (*putrāḥ*)); those who are not sons are those who do not fill (the gods with offerings). "Destroy all of them" (वि चयिष्ट (*vi cayiṣṭa*)) is to be carried on from the preceding.
notes: ಹಸಾ: the word ending ಓಹಸಾ is cut off in the supplied text; read as ಓಹಸಾ of the Ṛk
ಚಾಪ್ಯಃ printed; the Saṃhitā and Pratipadārtha read ಅಪ್ಪ್ಯಃ / ಅಪ್ಪಃ

en: - ओहसा (*ohasā*)—by the praises that extol you
- अयज्ञ साचः (*ayajña sācaḥ*)—are devoid of sacrifice (and)
- न पुत्राः (*na putrāḥ*)—those who do not worship and satisfy you, destroy all of them

O Mitra and Varuṇa, the rites that are directed to you and agreeable to you, which men devoid of rites harm, vying with you; the gods who are not joined with the praises that extol you; the mortals who are not joined with those same praises; those who, though possessed of rites, are devoid of sacrifice; and those who do not worship and satisfy you: destroy them all.
(Exterminate also), Mitra and Varuna, those who, emulously
contending, disturb the rites that are agreeable and beneficial to you both :
those divinities, those mortals, who are not diligent in adoration,
those who performing works perform not sacrifices. those who do not

When the कीस्तासः (*kīstāsaḥ*), the intelligent udgātṛs (the word is read among the names of the intelligent: उशिजः कीस्तास (*uśijaḥ kīstāsa*)), utter the praise (वाचं (*vācaṃ*)) separately, then some ब्रह्मचा (*brahmacā*) ⟨NOTE:201⟩, meditating on Agni and the others and praising them, recite the Nivid mantras. This being so, we utter to you two true praises. By your greatness you two do not go together with the other gods.
notes: ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚಾ: garbled; the Kannada Pratipadārtha has ಬಹ್ವೃಚರು, Ṛgvedic reciters

en: - मनानाः (*manānāḥ*)—meditating on Agni and the others
- सत्यानि उक्ता (*satyāni uktā*)—true mantras of praise
- महित्वा (*mahitvā*)—through the loftiness of your greatness
- नकिः यतथः (*nakiḥ yatathaḥ*)—you neither join nor go along
notes: ತೇ ಚಿತ್ printed; the Saṃhitā reads ಕೇ ಚಿತ್

en: O Mitra and Varuṇa, when the intelligent udgātṛs recite the praise addressed to you, then some Ṛgvedic priests, meditating on Agni and the others, recite and praise with the mantra called Nivid. On that occasion we recite true mantras of praise addressed to you two. Through the loftiness of your greatness you neither join nor go along with the other gods.
When the intelligent priests offer praise, then some of them, glorify-
ing (Agni and other deities), recite the Nivid hymns; such being the case,
we address to you sincere adoration, for in consequence of your greatness
you do not associate with (other) divinities

O Mitra and Varuṇa, protectors, at your approach (अभिष्टौ (*abhiṣṭau*)), for the house or for happiness: among the singers who have come to you, whatever of yours is to be given by you, that house and the rest, becomes अस्कृधोयु (*askṛdhoyu*), uninterrupted. So Yāska: अस्कृधोयुरकृध्वायुः । कृध्विति ह्रस्वनाम निकृत्तं भवति । (*askṛdhoyurakṛdhvāyuḥ | kṛdhviti hrasvanāma nikṛttaṃ bhavati |*) (Ni. 6-3) **GLOSS**. इत्था (*itthā*) means "truly". When is your approach? He says: when the गावः (*gāvaḥ*), the praises, ring out after (अनु स्पुरान् (*anu spurān*)), and when the sacrificers yoke (युनजन् (*yunajan*)) in the rite, in the sacrifice (रणे (*raṇe*)), the Soma that is ऋजिष्यं (*ṛjiṣyaṃ*), going straight, धृष्णुं (*dhṛṣṇuṃ*), the assailer of enemies, and वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*), the showerer of desires.
- अभिष्टौ (*abhiṣṭau*)—as the result of the approach
- युवोः (*yuvoḥ*)—the houses and the rest given by you
- अस्कृधोयु (*askṛdhoyu*)—remain unbroken and eternal, or great

O Mitra and Varuṇa, when the praises addressed to you are recited, when the sacrificers offer in the sacrifice the Soma that goes straight, assails enemies and showers desires, then, as the result of the approach of you, the protectors of the house, the houses and the rest given by you remain unbroken and eternal, or great.
Upom your approach, Mitra and Varuna, protectors of the dwelling,
your (bounty) is unlimited; when (your) praises are uttered, and the
sacrificers add in the ceremony the soma that inspires straight-forwardness
and resolution, and is the showerer (of benefits)

O Indra and Varuṇa, honourable ones (महे (*mahe*)), for you two the sacrifice is श्रुष्टि (*śruṣṭi*), swift. So Yāska: श्रुष्टिति क्षिप्रनामाशु अष्टीति (*śruṣṭiti kṣipranāmāśu aṣṭīti*) (Ni. 6-12) **GLOSS**. The Soma, the sacrifice, accompanied by the priests (सजोषा (*sajoṣā*)), is today set out, started, all around. That Soma, like Manu, for the sacrificer who has spread the sacred grass (वृक्तबर्हिषः (*vṛktabarhiṣaḥ*)), for food (इषे (*iṣe*)), for great happiness (सुम्नाय (*sumnāya*)), for worshipping you, आववर्तत् (*āvavartat*), brings you here.
- वृक्तबर्हिषः (*vṛktabarhiṣaḥ*)—for the sacrificer who has spread the well prepared seat of darbha grass
- उद्यतः (*udyataḥ*)—is offered (is engaged in your worship)
notes: ನಾಂ printed in the Pratipadārtha; the Saṃhitā reads ವಾಂ

en: O venerable Indra and Varuṇa, for the sacrificer who, like Manu, has spread the well prepared seat of darbha grass and worships you, the Soma that is made ready to worship you, for food and for great happiness, is now offered everywhere, swiftly, addressed to you, by the priests; and it is engaged in your worship.

Mighty Indra and Varna promptly has the soma returned, engaged conscientiously (with the priests) to offer sacrifice to you to obtain food, for him by whom, like Manu. the sacred grass has been clipped; he who (invited you hither) to-day for exceeding happiness.

O Indra and Varuṇa, you two, those well known, are the best (श्रेष्ठा (*śreṣṭhā*)) देवताता (*devatātā*) ⟨NOTE:205⟩ in the sacrifice, since इष्टिर्देवतातेति (*iṣṭirdevatāteti*) is read among the names of sacrifice. You are तुजा (*tujā*), impellers of wealth: be so. Moreover, among heroes you two are शविष्ठा (*śaviṣṭhā*), exceedingly strong. Moreover, among the मघोनां (*maghonāṃ*), those who give, you are मंहिष्ठा (*maṃhiṣṭhā*), the greatest givers; तुविशुष्मा (*tuviśuṣmā*), of great strength; through ऋतेन (*ṛtena*), truth, वृत्रतुरा (*vṛtraturā*), destroyers of foes; and सर्वसेना (*sarvasenā*), possessed of whole armies: be so.
notes: ದೇವತಾತಾ ದೇವತಾತ್: second word garbled; the Kannada reads ದೇವಪೂಜಕವಾದ ಯಜ್ಞದಲ್ಲಿ

en: - ता हि (*tā hi*)—you two, the well known
- देवताता (*devatātā*)—in the sacrifice that worships the gods
- सर्वसेना (*sarvasenā*)—and also in the form of all armies ⟨NOTE:206⟩
notes: ಸರ್ವಸೇನಾ: Kannada ಸಕಲ ಸೇನಾರೂಪರಾಗಿಯೂ "in the form of all armies"; Sāyaṇa ಕೃತ್ಸಸೇನೌ "having whole armies"

en: O Indra and Varuṇa, in the sacrifice that worships the gods, you two, the well known, are the best givers of wealth. You two alone are of exceeding strength among heroes, and the most generous givers among those who possess wealth. You yourselves, of abundant strength, through truth are destroyers of foes and are also in the form of all armies.
You two are the principal (divinities) at the worship of the gods;
the distributors of wealth; the most vigorous of heroes; the most liberal
among the opulent; possessed of vast strength; destroyers of foes by truth;

O Bharadvāja, praise Indra and Varuṇa with praiseworthy (नमस्येभिः (*namasyebhiḥ*)) strengths (शूषैः (*śūṣaiḥ*); the word for "śūṣa" is read among the names of strength) and with pleasures (सुम्मेभिः (*summebhiḥ*)) ⟨NOTE:207⟩. Praise (गृणीहि (*gṛṇīhi*), that is, extol) those two, Indra and Varuṇa. Of the two, the one, Indra, slays Vṛtra, the demon of that name, with the thunderbolt. The other, Varuṇa, the wise (विप्रः (*vipraḥ*), that is, the knowing), joins (सिषक्ति (*siṣakti*), that is, comes together) with strength to protect the praisers in their troubles (वृजनेषु (*vṛjaneṣu*)).
notes: ಸುಖೈಶ್ಚ ಸರ್ವೈಶ್ಚ ಕಾನಾ ಸ್ತುತೌ: ಸರ್ವೈಶ್ಚ unclear; only "pleasures" and "⟦ಕಾನಾ⟧ in praise" are clear

en: - ता इंद्रवरुणा (*tā iṃdravaruṇā*)—those same Indra and Varuṇa
- वृजनेषु (*vṛjaneṣu*)—in times of trouble, to protect the praisers

O Bharadvāja, praise those same Indra and Varuṇa, renowned for venerable strengths and pleasures. Of the two, Indra slays Vṛtra with the thunderbolt. The other, Varuṇa, being wise, joins with strength to protect the praisers in times of trouble.
Praise Mitra and Varuna, renowned for all glorious energies and
enjoyments: one of whom slays Vritra with the thunderbolt, the other,
intelligent by his might, comes to the aid (of the pious when) in difficulties.

Among men (नरां (*narāṃ*), that is, mankind) there are ग्नाः (*gnāḥ*), women, from Yāska's statement: मेना ग्ना इति स्त्रीणां (*menā gnā iti strīṇāṃ*) (Ni. 3-21) **GLOSS**; and नरः (*naraḥ*), men; and all the gods (देवासः (*devāsaḥ*); here the word means both gods and goddesses, and the masculine form is used for both). They are स्वगूर्ताः (*svagūrtāḥ*), self-impelled. When (यत् (*yat*)) they make you grow (ववृधंत (*vavṛdhaṃta*)) with praises, then, O Indra and Varuṇa, you two, endowed with greatness, surpass (प्र भूतं (*pra bhūtaṃ*), that is, prevail over) these praisers. And O heaven and earth, both wide and extensive, the words "you two surpass them" are to be carried on to you also.
- ववृधंत (*vavṛdhaṃta*)—they cause your increase with praises, then
- प्र भूतं (*pra bhūtaṃ*)—become of more abundant greatness
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—O deity of the heavenly world
- पृथिवि च (*pṛthivi ca*)—and O earth (you two)
- उर्वी (*urvī*)—being of extensive form, are above all

O Indra and Varuṇa, when, among mankind, women, men and all the gods, self-impelled, cause your increase with praises, then you, endowed with greatness, become of more abundant greatness than all these praisers. O deity of the heavenly world, O earth, you two also, being of extensive form, are above all.
When amongst mankind, both males and females, and when all the
gods spontaneously striving glorify you, Indra and Varuna, you become
pre-eminent in greatness over them, as do you, wide heaven and earth

O Indra and Varuṇa, both addressed in the dual. Whichever sacrificer, of his own accord (त्मन् (*tman*)), offers (दाशति (*dāśati*), that is, gives) oblations to you two, he alone (स इत् (*sa it*)) becomes सुदानुः (*sudānuḥ*), of fine giving. He becomes स्ववान् (*svavān*), wealthy, and ऋतावान् (*ṛtāvān*), possessed of sacrifice. Moreover, he, दास्वान् (*dāsvān*), the giver, with food (इषा (*iṣā*)) won by victory from the hater (द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)) would cross over, that is, attain. And also he would obtain (वंसत् (*vaṃsat*), that is, share) wealth (रयिं (*rayiṃ*)), and sons and people who are wealthy (रयिवतः (*rayivataḥ*)). ⟨NOTE:208⟩
notes: ದ್ವಿಷೋ ದ್ವೇಷ್ಟುರಿಷಾನ್ನೇನ ಜಯಲಚ್ಛೇನ: ಜಯಲಚ್ಛೇನ garbled; the Kannada Pratipadārtha takes ತರೇತ್ as "crosses troubles" and ದ್ವಿಷಃ as "of the enemy", Sāyaṇa takes ತರೇತ್ as "attains"

en: O Indra and Varuṇa, whichever sacrificer, addressing you, offers oblations of his own accord, he alone becomes an excellent giver, wealthy and possessed of sacrifice.
He, being generous, obtains food won from his enemies and is delivered from hardship. He obtains wealth and sons possessed of wealth.
He who spontaneously presents you, Indra and Varuna (oblatious), is liberal, wealthy and upright: he shall prosper with the food of his adversary, and possess riches, and opulent descendants.

O Indra and Varuṇa, you two, who are praised (देवा (*devā*), the two gods), to the sacrificer who has given the oblation (दाश्वध्वराय (*dāśvadhvarāya*)), you bestow (धत्थः (*dhatthaḥ*), that is, give) such wealth (रयिं (*rayiṃ*)) as is वसुमंतं (*vasumaṃtaṃ*), accompanied by riches, and पुरुक्षुं (*purukṣuṃ*), abundant in food or full of fame. And that which breaks (प्र भनक्ति (*pra bhanakti*), that is, shatters) the ill-fame (अशस्तीः (*aśastīḥ*)) of the harming enemies (वनुषां (*vanuṣāṃ*)), the meaning being the dishonours wrought by foes, may such wealth be in us (अस्मे (*asme*), that is, in us).
- देवा (*devā*)—you who are divine in nature
- दाश्वध्वराय (*dāśvadhvarāya*)—to the sacrificer who has offered the oblation
- यः अपि (*yaḥ api*)—which riches and the like

O Indra and Varuṇa, divine in nature, the food accompanied by riches and abundant, and the wealth, which you give to the sacrificer who has offered the oblation, those, and such wealth and the like as destroys the ill-fame of harming enemies, may it be full in us.
May that opulence comprising treasure and abundant food, which
you bestow, deities, upon the donor (of the oblation), that, Indra and
Varuna, which baffles the calumnies of the malevolent, be ours.

And also, O Indra and Varuṇa, to us, the praisers (सूरिभ्यः (*sūribhyaḥ*)), may wealth be सुत्रात्रः (*sutrātraḥ*), well guarded, and देवगोपाः (*devagopāḥ*), that is, of which the gods are the guardians. Moreover, ours, whose strength (शुष्मो (*śuṣmo*)) in battles, being the overcomer of enemies and a destroyer, would at once completely overshadow (प्र तिरते (*pra tirate*)) the glories (द्युम्ना (*dyumnā*), that is, the fames) of those enemies. ⟨NOTE:209⟩
notes: ಪೃಶನಾಸು, ಶಕ್ರೂಣಾಮ್: read as ಪೃತನಾಸು, ಶತ್ರೂಣಾಮ್; Pratipadārtha has ಶುಷ್ಕಃ for ಶುಷ್ಮಃ

en: - ततुरिः (*taturiḥ*)—and being the destroyer of enemies

O Indra and Varuṇa, may wealth, well protected and guarded by the gods, be obtained by us, the praisers, whose strength in battles defeats enemies and destroys them and at once completely covers all their fame.

May that opulence, Indra and Varuna, which is a sure defence, and of which the gods are the guardians, be ours, celebrating your praise, whose destroying prowess in battles victorious (over foes) speedily obscures (their) fame.

O Indra and Varuṇa, you two who are praised (गृणाना (*gṛṇānā*)), to us, for good fame (सौश्रवसाय (*sauśravasāya*), that is, the state of having good fame), quickly (नु (*nu*)) bestow (पृंकं (*pṛṃkaṃ*), that is, give) wealth (रयिं (*rayiṃ*)). Moreover, O gods, the strength (शर्धः (*śardhaḥ*)) of you two, the great (महिनस्य (*mahinasya*)), thus praising it, we would cross the evils (दुरिता (*duritā*)) as one crosses waters by a boat.
- गृणाना (*gṛṇānā*)—you who are praised by us
- सौश्रवसाय (*sauśravasāya*)—for the gaining of excellent happiness
- अपो न (*apo na*)—as one crosses water

O Indra and Varuṇa, you who are praised by us, quickly give us wealth for the gaining of excellent happiness. O divine ones, praising in this manner the strength of you who are great, may we cross our sins as one crosses water by a boat.

Divine and glorified Indra and Varuna, quickly bestow upon us wealth for our felicity ; and thus eulogising the strength of you two, mighty (deities), may we pass over all difficulties as (we cross) the waters with a boat.

O praiser, to Varuṇa, the सम्राज (*samrāja*), the ruler of kings by his command; बृहते (*bṛhate*), the great, the grown; देवाय (*devāya*), the shining; recite now a hymn (मन्म (*manma*), a praise) that is प्रियं (*priyaṃ*), pleasing, and सप्रथः (*saprathaḥ*), broad on every side. So Yāska: सप्रथाः सर्वतः पृथुः (*saprathāḥ sarvataḥ pṛthuḥ*) (Ni. 6-7) **GLOSS**. This Varuṇa who, endowed with greatness (महिना (*mahinā*)), महिव्रतः (*mahivrataḥ*), of great works, and endowed with insight (क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)) and with radiance (शोचिषा (*śociṣā*)), and as one free from old age, illumines (विभाति (*vibhāti*)) the two wide worlds, heaven and earth.
- यः आयं (*yaḥ āyaṃ*)—this same Varuṇa who
- अजरो न (*ajaro na*)—and free from decay

O praiser, this same Varuṇa who, united with his greatness, possessed of great works, endowed with insight and free from decay, causes both the wide heaven and earth to shine with his radiance: to that universal ruler, the grown, the shining Varuṇa, at once recite and worship with a hymn that is pleasing and extensive.
Repeat acceptable and all-comprehensive praise to the imperial mighty divine Varuna, he who, endowed with greatness. with wisdom, and with splendour, illumes the spacious (heaven and earth).

O Indra and Varuṇa, सुतपौ (*sutapau*), drinkers of the pressed Soma, drink this pressed Soma, the intoxicating (मद्यं (*madyaṃ*), that which gladdens). Moreover, O धृतव्रता (*dhṛtavratā*), upholders of rites, your chariot comes along the road (स्वसरं (*svasaraṃ*), the way) towards the sacrifice, for the drinking (देववीतये (*devavītaye*)) of the gods, and also for the drinking of the Soma by you two (पीतये (*pītaye*)).
- इंद्रा वरुणा (*iṃdrā varuṇā*)—O Indra and Varuṇa
- सुतपा (*sutapā*)—you who drink the pressed Soma
- धृतव्रता (*dhṛtavratā*)—O Indra and Varuṇa, upholders of rites
- देववीतये (*devavītaye*)—for the drinking of the gods
- स्वसरं प्रति (*svasaraṃ prati*)—following the road of the sacrifice

O Indra and Varuṇa, you who drink the pressed Soma, drink this Soma juice that is satisfying and has just been pressed. O Indra and Varuṇa, upholders of rites, your chariot comes following the road of the sacrifice, for the drinking of the gods and for your drinking.

Indra and Varuna, observant of holy duties, drinkers of the Soma juice, drink this exhilarating effused libation: your chariot approaches along the road to the sacrifice, (that you may partake) of the food of the gods, aud drink (the Soma).

O Indra and Varuṇa, वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*), showerers of desires, partake (आ वृषेथां (*ā vṛṣethāṃ*), that is, eat) of the Soma, the sweetest (मधुमत्तमस्य (*madhumattamasya*), exceedingly sweet and full of juice), the showerer (वृष्णः (*vṛṣṇaḥ*)). So the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa: यथाभागमावृषायध्वमिति यथाभागमश्नीतेत्येवैतदाह । (*yathābhāgamāvṛṣāyadhvamiti yathābhāgamaśnītetyevaitadāha |*) (2-4-2-20) **GLOSS**. For you two this food (अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*)), in the form of Soma, has been poured round (परिषिक्तं (*pariṣiktaṃ*)) into the vessels by us. Then, having sat down on this sacred grass at the sacrifice, may you be exhilarated, that is, at the Soma drinking; this is the remainder to be supplied.
- परिषिक्तं (*pariṣiktaṃ*)—has been filled into the vessel
- अस्मिन् बर्हिषि (*asmin barhiṣi*)—on this seat of darbha grass

O Indra and Varuṇa, you who shower desires, partake of the Soma juice that is exceedingly sweet and juicy. For you this Soma juice has been filled into the vessel by us. Sitting down on this seat of darbha grass, be satisfied.
Drink, Indra and Varuna, showerers (of benefits), of the most sweet
soma the shedder (of blessings): this, your beverage, is poured forth by
us: sitting on the sacred grass, be exhilarated (by the draught).

O Indra and Viṣṇu, I well impel you two (सं हिनोमि (*saṃ hinomi*), that is, I urge duly) with the rite (कर्मणा (*karmaṇā*), the praise) and with the oblation (इषा (*iṣā*)). At the end (पारे (*pāre*)), at the completion, of this work (अपसः (*apasaḥ*), the rite) that has been recited, enjoy (जुषेथां (*juṣethāṃ*), that is, be served by) the sacrifice. Moreover, leading us across (पारयंता (*pārayaṃtā*), taking us to the further shore) by safe paths (अरिष्टैः (*ariṣṭaiḥ*), free from disturbance), bestow (धत्तं (*dhattaṃ*), give) wealth (द्रविणं (*draviṇaṃ*)) on us.
- कर्मणा (*karmaṇā*)—with the rite in the form of praise
- अस्य (*asya*)—of the recitation of this ukta mantra
- पारयंता (*pārayaṃtā*)—lead and show us the shore

O Indra and Viṣṇu, I worship you with the rite in the form of praise and with the oblation. At the end of my rite and of this recitation of the ukta mantra, enjoy the sacrifice. Lead us by paths free from harm. And without trouble show us the shore. Give us wealth.
I earnestly propitiate you, Indra and Vishnu, by worship and (sacrificial) food : upon the completion of the rite, accept the sacrifice, and grant us wealth, conducting us by safe paths.
The two well-known Indra and Viṣṇu who are the जनितारा (*janitārā*), generators, of all (विश्वासां (*viśvāsāṃ*)) the मतीनां (*matīnāṃ*), the praises.

May the two also be कलशा (*kalaśā*), vessels, and सोमधाना (*somadhānā*), receptacles of the Soma. Now a direct address: O Indra and Viṣṇu, may the utterances (गिरः (*giraḥ*), the words) in the form of śastras, which are being recited (शस्यमाना (*śasyamānā*)) to you, reach you (प्रावंतु (*prāvaṃtu*), that is, attain). And may the stomas (स्तोमासः (*stomāsaḥ*)), the hymns of praise that are being sung (गीयमानासो (*gīyamānāso*)) by the praisers (अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*)), reach you.
- कलशा (*kalaśā*)—and are in the form of vessels
- सोमधाना (*somadhānā*)—in the form of receptacles in which Soma is placed, such
- प्र अवंतु (*pra avaṃtu*)—may they come and reach you
- प्र (अवंतु) (*pra (avaṃtu)*)—may they come and reach you

O Indra and Viṣṇu, you who are the place of origin of all praises and are in the form of vessels, in the form of receptacles in which Soma is placed: may our words of praise that praise such as you come and reach you. May the stomas that are chanted by the praisers also come and reach you.
May the prayers that are repeated to you reach you Indra and Vishnu : may the praises that are chanted reach you : you are the generators of all praises, pitchers recipient of the Soma libation.

Sāyaṇa addresses Indra and Viṣṇu as the lords of the exhilarations, that is, of the Somas; the word "exhilaration" in the compound meaning "lords of exhilaration" is only a restatement. The wealths are the riches that the two bestow. The two of them, bestowing wealth, are to come to the Soma. The hymns of the praisers, the stomas, being recited together with the śastras (the recitations accompanying the uktha), are to anoint you with radiance, that is, to support and strengthen you. The doubling of the prefix expresses regard.
- आ यातं (*ā yātaṃ*)—be pleased to come
- सं अंजंतु (*saṃ aṃjaṃtu*)—may they fill and make you grow

O Indra and Viṣṇu, you who are the lords of all the Somas and lords of wealths also: be pleased to come towards the Soma. May the hymns of the praisers, joined with the śastra-mantras, praise you, fill you with radiance and make you grow.
Indra and Vishnu, lords of the exhilaration, of the exhilarating
juices, come to (drink) the Soma, bringing (with you) wealth : may the
encomiums of the praises repeated along with the prayers anoint you

O Indra and Viṣṇu, your horses, who overcome the hostile harmers (the abhimātis) and who rejoice together, are to bring you hither. Be pleased with, that is, accept, all the invocations, the hymns of the praisers. For that purpose hear my hymns and my utterances in the form of śastras.
- आ वहंतु (*ā vahaṃtu*)—may they bring you
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—the utterances in the form of śastras

O Indra and Viṣṇu deities, may your horses, which overcome the harmful enemies and rejoice together, bring you. Accept all the hymns of the praisers. Listen to the hymns recited by me and to the utterances in the form of śastras.
May your equally-spirited steeds. Indra and Vishnu the triumphant over enemies, bear you hither : be pleased with all the invocations of your worshippers : hear my prayers and praises

O Indra and Viṣṇu, that deed of yours is praiseworthy. What deed? When there is exhilaration from the Soma, you strode widely and far; although the striding belongs to Viṣṇu alone, it is said of both because the two are of one purpose. And you made the atmosphere wider, and you spread out the rajas, all the worlds (Yāska says that the worlds are called rajas), for our life.

O Indra and Viṣṇu deities, that deed of yours, that when exhilaration arose from drinking the Soma-juice you strode over the universe most extensively, is exceedingly praiseworthy. You have made the atmosphere extensive. You have manifested all the worlds as fit for our life.
Indra and Vishnu, that (exploit) is to be glorified, by which, in the
exhilaration of the Soma, you have strode over the wide (space): you have
traversed the wide fimameut : you have declared the worlds (fit) for our

O Indra and Viṣṇu, fed with ghee, you who grow by the oblation, that is, the Soma, who are the eaters of the first, the pure part of the Soma, to whom the sacrificers have given oblations with reverence: bestow wealth upon us. Moreover, you are like the ocean, the sea; for you are a pitcher, the receptacle of the Soma.
- धृतासुती (*dhṛtāsutī*)—you who have food in the form of ghee
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—by the oblation in the form of Soma
- आग्राद्वाना (*āgrādvānā*)—who eat the first part of the Soma
- सोमधानः (*somadhānaḥ*)—in which the Soma is placed
- कलशः (*kalaśaḥ*)—in the form of a pitcher vessel, you are

O Indra and Viṣṇu deities, you who have food in the form of ghee, who grow by the oblation in the form of Soma, who eat the first part of the Soma, and who have oblations offered with reverence: give us wealth. You two are deep like the ocean. You are also in the form of pitcher vessels in which the Soma is placed.
Indra and Vishnu, feeders upon clarified butter, drinking of the
fermented Soma, thriving upon oblations, accepting them offered with
reverence, bestow upon us wealth : for you are an ocean, a pitcher, the

O Indra and Viṣṇu, beautiful to behold, drink this intoxicating Soma. And fill your belly, your stomach, with the Soma. O Indra and Viṣṇu, may the exhilarating foods, which are Soma in nature, come to you. Do also what concerns my hymns and my invocation.⟨NOTE:212⟩
notes: ಉಪ ಕೃಣುತಂ in the bhāṣya, but ಶೃಣುತಂ in the Saṃhitā and Pada; read here as "hear"

en: - दस्रा (*dasrā*)—you who have an attractive form
- पृणेथां (*pṛṇethāṃ*)—fill yourselves with this juice (O Indra and Viṣṇu)
- अंधांसि (*aṃdhāṃsi*)—the foods in the form of Soma
- आ अग्मन् (*ā agman*)—may they come near

O Indra and Viṣṇu, of attractive form, drink this intoxicating Soma-juice. Fill your bellies with this juice. O Indra and Viṣṇu, may the intoxicating foods in the form of Soma approach you. Hear my hymns and my invocation.
Indra and Vishnu, agreeable of aspect, drink of this sweet Soma ;
fill with it your bellies : may the inebriating beverage reach you : hear my

O Indra and Viṣṇu, you both were victorious: you conquered the enemies. You are not defeated again, ever. Of the two of you, neither one was defeated. O Viṣṇu, and Indra, whatever thing you two contended for with the asuras, standing threefold as world, Veda and speech, and a thousand without measure, that you strode through, that is the meaning. So also the Brāhmaṇa: उभा जिग्यथुरित्यच्छावाकस्योभौ हि तौ जिग्यतुर्न परा जयेथे न परा जिग्य इति न हि तयोः (*ubhā jigyathurityacchāvākasyobhau hi tau jigyaturna parā jayethe na parā jigya iti na hi tayoḥ*)

The passage of the Brāhmaṇa continues: Indra and Viṣṇu fought the asuras, and having conquered them they said, "Let us make an arrangement." The asuras agreed. Indra said, "As far as this Viṣṇu strides in his three strides, that much shall be ours, and the rest yours." Viṣṇu then strode over these worlds, then over the Vedas, then over speech. They ask, "What is that thousand?" One should answer: these worlds, these Vedas and speech. (Ai. Brā. 6-15) **GLOSS** Or else, the thousand is a thousand cows, and the sense is that they strode through it threefold.
- न परा जयेथे (*na parā jayethe*)—you have never been defeated
- न परा जिग्यॆ (*na parā jigyè*)—does not suffer defeat
- अपस्पृधेथां (*apaspṛdhethāṃ*)—you contend with the asuras, in all of them
- वि तत् ऐरयेथां (*vi tat airayethāṃ*)—having won the victory, you make a full stride

O Indra and Viṣṇu, you both always conquer the enemies. You have never been defeated. Neither of you two suffers defeat. O Viṣṇu, in whatever battles you and Indra contend with the asuras, in all of them, having won the victory that is of three kinds and without measure, you make a full stride.
You have both (ever) been victorious : never have been conquered ; neither of you two has been vanquished : with whomsoever you have contended you have thrice conquered thousands.

O Heaven and Earth, you two are घृतवती (*ghṛtavatī*), radiant or full of water, for घृतं (*ghṛtaṃ*) is read among the names of water. The words "you two are" are to be supplied. You are अभिश्रिया (*abhiśriyā*), to be resorted to by all beings. You are wide and widely known for your many works, and you yield honey, that is, water; you are of fair form. You are held apart by the upholding of Varuṇa, the controller of all; you are unageing, eternal, rich in seed or of many functions. Here, since the occasion is the direct praise of Heaven and Earth, "of Varuṇa" is to be so understood. ⟨NOTE:215⟩
notes: ವರ್ಣುಣಸ್ಯೇತಿ ದೃಷ್ಟವ್ಯಂ: the sense of this closing remark is not clear; ವರ್ಣುಣಸ್ಯ for ವರುಣಸ್ಯ

en: - धृतवती (*dhṛtavatī*)—the two that are full of radiance
- धर्मणा (*dharmaṇā*)—by the work that upholds the world
- भूरिरेतसा (*bhūriretasā*)—and are of very great vigour

The radiant Heaven and Earth, both being givers of refuge to all the worlds, having a wide form, having wide fame, milking water, having an excellent form, and, by the work of Varuṇa that upholds the world, having separate existence, are free from decay.
Radiant Heaven and Earth, the asylum of created beings, you are spacious, manifold, water-yiding, lovely, separately fixed by the functions of Varuna, undecaying, many-germed.

The two are असश्चंती (*asaścaṃtī*), not clinging, or not falling apart, and भूरिधारे (*bhūridhāre*), of many streams: the streams of rain from heaven and the streams of juice produced by the oblations on earth; thus both have many streams. They are पयस्वती (*payasvatī*), watery. So Yāska says: असज्यमाने इति ना व्युदस्यंत्याविति वा बहुधारे उदकवत्यौ (*asajyamāne iti nā vyudasyaṃtyāviti vā bahudhāre udakavatyau*) (Ni. 5-2) **GLOSS**. Heaven and Earth, pure in their works, milk for the sacrificer who does good works the घृतं (*ghṛtaṃ*), the water that brings about the prosperity of crops and the like. Then follows direct praise: O Heaven and Earth, rulers of this world, of all that has come to be, pour into us the vigour, seed capable of generating offspring, which is beneficial to men.
- असश्चंती (*asaścaṃtī*)—those who are free from falling
- भूरिधारे (*bhūridhāre*)—who bear many kinds of vigour
- शुचिव्रते (*śucivrate*)—who have pure works and rites, Heaven and Earth
- सुकृते (*sukṛte*)—for the sacrificer who does good works
- अस्य भुवनस्य (*asya bhuvanasya*)—of all that has come to be

Heaven and Earth, who are free from falling, who bear many kinds of vigour, who are rich in water and whose works and rites are pure, milk water for the sacrificer who does good works. O Heaven and Earth, you who are the lords of all that has come to be, pour and establish in us that vigour (water or strength) that is beneficial to men.
beneficent, pure in act : you two Heaven and Earth, rulers over created
beings, grant us vigour. that may be favourable to (the increase of)

O धिषणे (*dhiṣaṇe*), firm, or the abode of all beings, O Heaven and Earth: the mortal who gives you oblations for your easy, straight course, that mortal accomplishes his desires. Moreover, he is born forth, that is, he prospers, with progeny, sons, grandsons and the rest. Above the rite, the vigours sprinkled by you two, of various colours and of like work, come into being as creatures.
- धिषणे (*dhiṣaṇe*)—you who have a firm standing
- ऋजवे क्रमणाय (*ṛjave kramaṇāya*)—for your easy coming
- प्रजाभिः (*prajābhiḥ*)—with sons, grandsons and the rest
- धर्मणः परि (*dharmaṇaḥ pari*)—as the fruit of the upholding work
- सव्रता (*savratā*)—and yet of like work, the beings (creatures) come into being

O Heaven and Earth, you who have a firm standing: the man who, for your easy coming, offers an oblation to you, that same man obtains all his desired ends. He prospers with sons, grandsons and the rest. From the vigours sprinkled as the fruit of your upholding work, creatures that have many kinds of forms and yet are of like work come into being.

Firm-set Heaven and Earth, the mortal who has offered (oblations) for your straight-forwad course, accomplishes (his objects), he prospers with progeny, and invigorated by your operation, many beings of various forms, but similar functions, engendered.

Heaven and Earth are enveloped in धृतेन (*dhṛtena*), water. They resort to water, are mingled with water, and make water grow. They are wide and widely known. They are placed first by the sacrificers in the sacrifice (होतृवूर्ये (*hotṛvūrye*)). The wise praisers ask for happiness (सुम्नं (*sumnaṃ*)) from Heaven and Earth alone, for the sacrifice (इष्टये (*iṣṭaye*); the word is read among the names of the sacrifice), for when there is happiness the sacrifices go on.
- पृथ्वि (*pṛthvi*)—and having wide fame, they are
- पुरो हिते (*puro hite*)—they are worthy of the first honour
- ते इत् (*te it*)—from Heaven and Earth alone
- इष्टये (*iṣṭaye*)—for the sake of the sacrifice

Heaven and Earth are enveloped in water. They are a refuge for water, are satisfied with water, increase water, and have an extended form and fame. In the sacrifice they are worthy of the first honour. The wise praisers ask for happiness from Heaven and Earth alone, for the sake of the sacrifice.
You are surrounded, Heaven and Earth, by water : you are the
asylum of water : imbued with water : the augmenters of water : vast and
manifold ; you are first propitiated in the sacrifice : the pious pray to you
for happiness, that the sacrifice (may be celebrated).

The two are मधुश्चुता (*madhuścutā*), causing water to flow; मधुदुघे (*madhudughe*), milkers of water; मधुव्रते (*madhuvrate*), whose works are for the sake of water; देवता (*devatā*), divine. They give us the sacrifice and wealth, great fame, food and good heroism. May Heaven and Earth sprinkle us with मधु (*madhu*), water (मिमिक्षतां (*mimikṣatāṃ*), may they sprinkle).
- मधुव्रते (*madhuvrate*)—who have works for the sake of water

May Heaven and Earth, who cause water to flow, who milk water, who have works for the sake of water, who are divine in nature, and who give us the sacrifice, wealth, great fame, food and excellent vigour, drench us with water (with rain).

May Heaven and Earth, the effusers of water, the milkers of water, dischargers of the functions of water, divinities, the promoters of sacrifice, the bestowers of wealth, of renown, of food, of male posterity, combine together.

Heaven, the father because he sprinkles the rain, and Earth, the mother because she bears, both give us ऊर्जं (*ūrjaṃ*), food (पिन्वतां (*pinvatāṃ*), may they bestow). Moreover, the two are विश्वविदा (*viśvavidā*), knowing all or making all known; सुदंससा (*sudaṃsasā*), of good works; संरराणे (*saṃrarāṇe*), delighting together in the relation of helper and helped; विश्वशंभुवा (*viśvaśaṃbhuvā*), bringing about the being of all. May Heaven and Earth send to us सनिं (*saniṃ*), what is to be enjoyed, sons and the rest, and वाजं (*vājaṃ*), strength, and रयिं (*rayiṃ*), wealth (समिन्वतां (*saminvatāṃ*), may they send forth).
- पिता (*pitā*)—Heaven, in the form of a father
- द्यौश्च (*dyauśca*)—the deity of the heavenly world
- माता (*mātā*)—and Earth, in the form of a mother
- विश्वशंभुवा (*viśvaśaṃbhuvā*)—who bring good to the whole world
- सनिं (*saniṃ*)—sons and the rest, fit to be enjoyed
- समिन्वतां (*saminvatāṃ*)—may they fill up and give

May Heaven, the deity of the heavenly world in the form of a father, and Earth, in the form of a mother, supply us with food that gives strength. May Heaven and Earth, who know all, who have good works, who delight together and who bring good to the whole world, fill up and give us sons and the rest that are fit to be enjoyed, strength and wealth.
May father Heaven, may mother Earth, who are all knowing, and
doers of good deeds, grant us sustenance ; may Heaven and Earth mutually
co-operating and promoting the happiness of all, bestow upon us posterity,

The shining, good-working, well-known Savitṛ stretches up his golden arms for सवनाय (*savanāya*), for impelling, that is, for giving. Moreover, he who is to be honoured, ever young, of good understanding, standing in the upholding of the रजसः (*rajasaḥ*), of the world or of water, sends out his two hands, full of घृतेन (*ghṛtena*), water.
- मखिः (*makhiḥ*)—the one who is to be honoured

The radiant, good-working, well-known god Savitṛ lifts up and stretches out his golden arms for excellent giving. Savitṛ, who is to be honoured, ever young, of excellent understanding and engaged in the manifold works of the worlds, extends fully his arms, full of water.

The divine and benevolent Savitri puts forth his golden arms for (making) donations : the adorable, youthful, sagacious (deity), stretches out out his hands, filled with water, in the various service of the world.

Of that god Savitṛ, the impeller, in his *savīman*, that is, in his impulsion (*prasava*) or permission. So Yāska says that *savīman* means *prasava* (Ni. 6-7). In what is most excellent, most highly praised, and in the giving of wealth, may we be capable; that is, may we be able. You who are independent in the maintenance (*niveśana*) and in the generation (*prasava*) of all that is two-footed, and you who are independent in the maintenance and generation of what is abundant and four-footed.
- दावने च (*dāvane ca*)—and in the giving, being worthy recipients
- द्विपदः (*dvipadaḥ*)—of men and others who have two feet
- प्रसवे च (*prasave ca*)—and in the generation
- चतुष्पदः (*catuṣpadaḥ*)—of cattle and others that have four feet; in their creation and in their maintenance you are the independent cause

May we be in the permission of the divine Savitṛ and be worthy recipients of the giving of excellent wealth. O god Savitṛ, you who are the independent cause of the generation and the maintenance of all that is two-footed, men and others, and four-footed, cattle and others.

May we be amongst the progeny of the divine Savitri, and (have power) to offer him most excellent donations : for you are he who (are absolute) in the procreation and perpetuation of many (living beings), bipeds or quadrupeds.

O Savitṛ, with your undamaged (that is, unharmed) protecting powers, either splendours or means of protection, which bring happiness, protect our *gaya*, our house or wealth. *Gaya* is read among the names of house in the Nighaṇṭu (*gayaḥ kṛdaraḥ*) and among the names of wealth (*mālvaṃ gayaḥ*). Today protect ⟨NOTE:219⟩; guard us. You are *hiraṇyajihva*, of speech that is beneficial and delightful. So Yāska, beginning with the question why gold is called *hiraṇya*, says that it is so because it is beneficial and delightful (Ni. 2-10). For our happiness, for the newer, be so; guard us and protect us. Let no enemy who wishes us harm (*aghaśaṃsa*) have power over us; the closing words ⟨NOTE:220⟩ are not clear.
notes: ಪರಿ ಯಾಹಿ in the bhāṣya, while the Saṃhitā and Pada have ಪರಿ ಪಾಹಿ
ಮಾಕಿರೀಶತ । ಮೇಶತ ॥ damaged in the bhāṣya

en: - शिवेभिः (*śivebhiḥ*)—and auspicious, by these your splendours
- माकिः ईशत (*mākiḥ īśata*)—let no one obtain the power to do harm

O god Savitṛ, with your unharmed, protecting and auspicious splendours, protect now our house. You of golden speech, take a new form for our happiness and protect us. Let no enemy who desires harm to us obtain the power to do us harm.

You, Savitri, prosper to-day our dwelling with uninjurable protections, confirming happiness ; you who are golden-tongued, (be vigilant) for cur present prosperity : protect us ; let not any calumniator have powcr (to harm) us.

*Deva* means the shining one; *damūnā* means one of a subduing mind or of a giving mind. So Yāska says that *damūnā* is *damamanā*, or *dānamanā*, or *dāntamanā* (Ni. 4-4). *Hiraṇyapāṇi* is he of golden hands; *ayohanu* is he of golden jaws, for *rukma* and *ayas* are read among the names of gold. *Yajata*

means he who is to be worshipped; *mandrajihva* means he of delightful speech. That well-known Savitṛ, each night, at the end of the night, has risen; let him rise. He who for me, the sacrificer who gives the oblation, impels (*ā suvati*) abundant (*bhūri*, that is, plentiful) and desirable (*vāma*, that is, to be won and shared) food. So Yāska says that *vāma* means what is to be won (Ni. 6-31).
- प्रतिदोषं (*pratidoṣaṃ*)—at the end of every night

May the radiant, giving-minded, golden-handed, golden-cheeked, adorable, delightful-voiced, well-known god Savitṛ rise at the end of every night. May he provide abundant and attractive food to me who offer oblations.

May the divine, munificent, golden-handed, golded-jawed, adorable sweet-spoken Savitri, rise regularly at the close of night : when he bestows abundant and desirable (food) upon the donor of the oblation.

May Savitṛ, like one who speaks for us (*upavaktṛ*), raise his two golden (*hiraṇmaya*) arms, with beautiful limbs. He who climbs from the earth, up to the end of the earth, the heights of the sky, that is, the elevated regions of the atmosphere; going, he gladdens everything great that exists, though hidden.
- उपवक्तेव (*upavakteva*)—like one who tells us of his auspicious presence
- उदयान् (*udayān*)—let him lift up and stretch out (this same Savitṛ)

May god Savitṛ, like one who tells us of his auspicious presence, lift up and hold out his golden arms of excellent form. This same Savitṛ climbs the lofty regions of the earth and the atmosphere. Moving about, he gladdens all great beings.
May Savitri put forth like an orator his golden well-formed arms : (he who), from the ends of the earth, ascends to the summit of the sky, and, moving along, delights every thing that is.

O Savitṛ, beget (*sāvīḥ*, that is, bring forth) for us today desirable (*vāma*) wealth, and tomorrow also bring forth desirable wealth. Why say much? Day by day, every day, bring forth desirable wealth. O god, because you are the giver of abundant (*bhūri*, that is, plentiful) desirable wealth that is the abode of a dwelling, therefore may we, by this praise, be sharers in the desirable, that is, possessed of wealth.
- वामं (*vāmaṃ*)—produce wealth of the same kind
- आया धिया (*āyā dhiyā*)—by this same praise

O god Savitṛ, produce for us attractive wealth today, tomorrow, and likewise every day. Produce every day that same wealth. O divine Savitṛ, by the greatness through which you are the giver of a dwelling-house and abundant wealth, make us, as the fruit of this our praise, possessed of wealth.
Beget for us Savitri, wealth to-day, wealth day by day : you are the giver of ample wealth, of a (spacious) mansion : may we, by this praise, become partakers of wealth.

O Indra and Soma, that greatness of you two is great. What is it? You two have made beings that are great and *prathama*, that is, *pratama* or foremost. Yāska says that *prathama* is a name for "chief"; it is *pratama* (Ni. 2-22). Further, you two found the sun and made men obtain it; you two also found *svar*, that is, water, since *hema* and *svar* are read among the names of water. And you two destroyed all the darknesses and the asuras who are revilers.
- प्रथमानि (*prathamāni*)—and of the highest importance, all the classes of beings
- विविदथुः (*vividathuḥ*)—you have established in the atmosphere so that he may be visible to all

O Indra and Soma, the well-known greatness of you two is exceedingly great. You two have created all the classes of beings that are of great power and of the highest importance. You have established the sun in the atmosphere so that he is visible to all. You have created water also. You have destroyed together all the pitch darknesses and the reviling asuras.

Great, Indra and Soma. is that your greatness, for you have made great and principal (beings) : you have made known (to men) Surya and the waters : you have dissipated the glooms and (destroyed) the revilers.

O Indra and Soma, you two cause Uṣas to dawn; that is, you make her shine forth. Further, you two raise the sun together with his light, his brilliance. And you two prop up the sky with the prop, the means of propping, the atmosphere set in the middle. You two spread out the earth, the mother, the mother of all.
- वासयथः (*vāsayathaḥ*)—you have made to appear and shine forth
- ज्योतिषा सह (*jyotiṣā saha*)—together with his radiance
- उन्नयथः (*unnayathaḥ*)—you have made to rise and shine
- स्कंभनेन (*skaṃbhanena*)—by the supporting pillar in the form of the atmosphere
- उप स्कंभथुः (*upa skaṃbhathuḥ*)—you have made it stand resting
- मातरं (*mātaraṃ*)—like a mother to the world
- वि अप्रथतं (*vi aprathataṃ*)—you have made to grow wide

O Indra and Soma, you have made Uṣas appear with her splendour, and the sun rise and shine with his radiance. You have made the heavenly world stand resting upon the supporting pillar in the form of the atmosphere. You have made the earth, the mother of the world, grow wide.

Indra and Soma, you have led on the dawns ; you have upraised the sun with his splendour : you have propped up the sky with the supporting pillar (of the firmament): you have spread out the earth, the mother (of all).

O Indra and Soma, you two slew Ahi, the smiter of the world, and Vṛtra the asura, who stood encircling the waters stationed in the cloud. Then the heaven approved of you two. Further, you two sent forth the waters of the rivers. *Puruṇi* means many, since it is read among the names of "many". And you two filled the seas, the places of water, with waters. Or else, the seas are the waters themselves, since they delight together; the sense is that you filled them with sap. So Yāska asks why the sea is called *samudra* and answers that the waters flow forth together from it, the waters run together to it, beings rejoice together in it, it is *samudaka*, or it wets (Ni. 2-10).
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters stationed in the cloud
- आ पप्रथुः (*ā paprathuḥ*)—you filled with waters

O Indra and Soma, you two have slain Ahi and the asura Vṛtra, who stood encircling the waters stationed in the cloud. Therefore the heavenly world honours you. You made the rivers, full of water, flow forth. You filled the seas with waters.

Indra and Soma, you slew Ahi and Vrita, the obstructer of the waters ; for which the heaven venerates you both : you have urged on the the waters of the rivers until they have replenished numerous oceans.

O Indra and Soma, in the unripe udders of the cows, in the middle, you two have placed ripe milk. Further, in these many-coloured *jagatī*s, that is, cows (*iḷā* and *jagatī* are read among the names of the cow), inside, you have held white milk that is bound by no one, so that it does not flow of itself upon the earth. The particle *id* is a filler.
- रुशत् (*ruśat*)—of dry colour ⟨NOTE:222⟩, that is, milk
- जगृभथुः (*jagṛbhathuḥ*)—you have caused to be held
notes: ಶುಷ್ಕವರ್ಣವುಳ್ಳದ್ದೂ in the Pratipadārtha; the bhāṣya has ಶುಕ್ಲವರ್ಣಂ "white"

en: O Indra and Soma, in the middle part of the unripe udders of the cows you have deposited ripe milk. In the middle of these many-coloured cows you have caused to be held the ⟨NOTE:223⟩ milk that is bound by no one and is of white colour.
notes: ವಯಸ್ಸನ್ನು printed, "age"; ಪಯಸ್ಸನ್ನು "milk" is the sense from the Pratipadārtha and the bhāṣya

en: Indra and Soma, you have deposited the mature (milk) in the immature udders of the cows : you have retained the white (secretion), although not shut up within those many-coloured cattle.

O Indra and Soma, you two swiftly (*aṅga*, that is, quickly) give wealth that is saving, accompanied by offspring and renowned; you place it for us. Further, O fierce ones, with weapons raised, you two have spread out together (or else, wrapped around) strength (*śuṣma*), beneficial to men and overcoming hostile armies, for the *carṣaṇi*s, that is, for men, since *kṛṣṭi* and *carṣaṇi* are read among the names of men.
- उग्रा (*ugrā*)—O Indra and Soma of exceedingly great strength
- पृतनासहं (*pṛtanāsahaṃ*)—and to be used to defeat enemies in battle
- सं विव्यथुः (*saṃ vivyathuḥ*)—you have given in fullness

O Indra and Soma, you two give to us quickly wealth that is protecting, accompanied by sons and others, and renowned. O Indra and Soma of exceedingly great strength, you have furnished to us who are men a strength that is beneficial to men and that is to be used to defeat enemies in battle.

Indra and Soma, promptly bestow upon us preservative, renowned (riches), accompanied by offspring; for you fierce (divinities), have disseminated amongst men, strength, useful to man, victorious over hostile hosts.

Bṛhaspati who is *adribhit*, the breaker of the masses of rock formed by the hands, or the splitter of clouds, since *adri* and *grāva* are read among the names of the cloud. *Prathamajāḥ*: born first, from the vigour of Prajāpati. *Ṛtāvā*: truthful, or possessing water. *Āṅgirasaḥ*: born afterwards. So a Vedic text says: येऽंगारा असंस्तेऽंगिरसोऽभवन्यदंगाराः पुनरवशांता उददीप्यंत तद्बृहस्पतिरभवत् । (*ye 'ṃgārā asaṃste 'ṃgiraso 'bhavanyadaṃgārāḥ punaravaśāṃtā udadīpyaṃta tadbṛhaspatirabhavat |*) (Ai. Brā. 3-34) **GLOSS**. *Haviṣmān*: possessing a share of the sacrifice. *Dvibarhajmā*: he whose going is vast in the two worlds. *Prāgharmasat*: dwelling in a place of intense brilliance. He who is our father, our protector, that Bṛhaspati, being the showerer, roars at heaven and earth; that is, he thunders.
- आद्रिभित् (*ādribhit*)—he who splits the clouds for the sake of rain
- प्रथमजाः (*prathamajāḥ*)—he who was born before all beings
- अंगिरसः (*aṃgirasaḥ*)—he who is born of the family of Aṅgiras
- हविष्मान् (*haviṣmān*)—he who is endowed with oblations
- द्विबर्हज्मा (*dvibarhajmā*)—he who has a path of movement in both heaven and earth
- प्राघर्मसत् (*prāgharmasat*)—he who dwells in a place of exceeding radiance
The Bṛhaspati who is the protector of truth, who splits the clouds for the sake of rain, who was born before all beings, who is born of the family of Aṅgiras, who is endowed with oblations,

who has a path of movement in both heaven and earth, and who dwells in a place of exceeding radiance, and who is a protector to us, that same Bṛhaspati, being the granter of our desires, roars between heaven and earth.

Brihaspati, who is the breaker of the mountain, the first-born (of Prajapati), the observer of truth, the descendant of Angiras, the partaker of the oblation, the traverser of two worlds, abiding in the region of light, is to us a father: he, the showerer, thunders loud in heaven and earth.

Further, Bṛhaspati who, for the worshipper who approaches, present at the sacrifice, in praise, makes a world, a place. (*Cit* is a filler.) He, destroying the *vṛtra*s, the covering darknesses, conquering enemies in battles, overcoming foes, tears apart thoroughly the cities of the asuras.
- वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—the darkness that covers the world

For the sacrificer who is engaged in the sacrifice and who obtains the presence of the gods through praise, the Bṛhaspati who makes an excellent place, that same Bṛhaspati, destroying the pitch darknesses that cover the world, conquering enemies in battles and defeating foes, completely destroys the cities of the enemies.
Brihaspati, who has appointed a region for the man who attends diligently at divine worship, destroying, impediments, conquering foes, overcoming enemies, demolishes various cities (of the Asuras).

This shining, well-known Bṛhaspati conquered the treasures of the Paṇis, the asuras, or of Vala, and the great herds' enclosures with cattle. So two Vedic texts say: बृहस्पतिर्गॊवपुषो वलस्य निर्मज्ञानं न पर्वणो जभार । (*bṛhaspatirgòvapuṣo valasya nirmajñānaṃ na parvaṇo jabhāra |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-68-9) **GLOSS** ⟨NOTE:224⟩; and दूरमित पणयो वरीय उद्दावो यंतु मिनतीर्युतेन । बृहस्पतिया अविंदन्निगूळ्हाः सोमो ग्रावाण ऋषयश्च विप्राः । (*dūramita paṇayo varīya uddāvo yaṃtu minatīryutena | bṛhaspatiyā aviṃdannigūḷhāḥ somo grāvāṇa ṛṣayaśca viprāḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-108-11) **GLOSS** ⟨NOTE:225⟩.

Further, Bṛhaspati, unopposed, met by no one, wishing to share *svar*, heaven, slays the enemy, the asura, with *arka*s, mantras that are the means of worship. ⟨NOTE:226⟩ So Yāska says that an *arka* is a mantra, because with it they worship (Ni. 5-4).
notes: abbreviation ಋ. printed
abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ. printed
ಸ್ವಃ: the bhāṣya glosses ಸ್ವರ್ಗಸ್ಯ "of heaven"; the Pratipadārtha has ಸ್ವಃ—ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷದ ಆಪಃ—ಉದಕಗಳನ್ನೆಲ್ಲಾ "all the waters of the atmosphere"

en: - समजयत् (*samajayat*)—he has taken under his own control from the enemies
- सिषासन् (*siṣāsan*)—wishing to bring completely under his own control
- अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*)—with the help of the mantras alone

The radiant and well-known Bṛhaspati took under his own control from the enemies the wealth of the enemies, and the great enclosures and cattle-pens full of cattle. Unopposed, wishing to bring completely under his own control all the waters of the atmosphere, Bṛhaspati destroys all the enemies with the help of the mantras alone.

This divine Brihaspati has conquered the treasures (of the enemy), and the spacious pastures with the cattle: purposing to appropriate the waters (of the firmament), he destroys with sacred prayers the adversary of heaven.

O Soma and Rudra, hold in us the strength that belongs to the asuras. Further, in each and every house of ours may the sacrifices pervade you two fully, adequately. Also you two, bearing the seven jewels, be happy-making for us, or of the nature of happiness. Be happy-making for our two-footed, our sons and others, and for our four-footed, cattle and others.
- असुरं (*asuraṃ*)—the strength that is in the asuras
- प्र अत्रुवंतु (*pra atruvaṃtu*)—fully approach and pervade

O gods Soma and Rudra, establish in us the strength that is in the asuras. In every house may the sacrifices fully approach and pervade you so as to satisfy you. You who possess the seven jewels, be givers of happiness to us. Be givers of happiness to our sons and others and to cattle and others.

Soma and Rudra, confirm (in us the strength) of Asuras ; may sacrifices in every dwelling adequately reach you : possessors of the seven precious things, bestow happiness upon our bipeds and quadrupeds.
